full_judgment:
Kazi Md Ejarul Haque Akondo J: In this Rule Nisi, issued under article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the respondents were called upon to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 28-7-2003 (decree signed on 4-8-2003) passed by the Bankruptcy Court, Bogra  (respondent No. 2) in Bankruptcy Case No. 03 of 2000 (Annexure-C) and the proceeding of Bankruptcy Execution Case No. 02 of 2004 (Annexure-J) now pending before the Bankruptcy Court No. 3, Bogra (respondent No.5) should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may deem fit and proper.

2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, the operation of the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-7-2003 (Annexure-C) and the proceeding of Bankruptcy Execution Case No. 02 of 2004 (Annexure-J) were stayed for a period of 6 (six) months from date which was subsequently extended time to time.

3. Facts, in short, are that the respondent No.4, as plaintiff, instituted bankruptcy case in the Court of Bankruptcy, Bogra দেউলিয়া বিষয়ক আদালত বগুড়া the respondent No. 2 being Bankruptcy Case No. 3 of 2000 alleging, inter-alia, that the Agrani Bank Ltd. is a nationalized banking institution having its head office in Dhaka. It has branches throughout the country like the branch of Saptapadi Market, Bogra. The defendants-petitioners opened an account being No. 1771 on 15-2-1994 with the respondent-bank, which sanctioned an amount of Taka 20,00,000 as cash credit hypo-loan and Taka 100,00,000 as cash credit pledge-loan on condition to repay the same in between 11-5-1996 to 31-10-1996 at the rate of 14% interest; the petitioners agreed to the terms and conditions of the loan sanction letter. The respondent-bank according to Bank Rules for keeping proper accounting opened Cash Credit Hypo-Account No. 67 and Cash Credit Pledge-Account No. 68 and the petitioners were enjoying the loan facilities through those 02 accounts. The petitioners mortgaged the scheduled land to the respondent-bank vide registered mortgage deed dated 3-11-1992 to repay the cash credit hypo-loan. The petitioners deposited demand promissory note, letter of arrangement and letter of disbursement as security against cash credit hypo-loan and cash credit pledge-loan. The petitioners did not deposit any sum of money after 12-7-1999 and did not take any delivery of chemical fertilizer. The respondent-bank requested them to repay the loan but they did not respond to the same. There was outstanding dues of taka 25,37,652 from the petitioners up to 30-6-2000 against Cash Credit Hypo-Account No. 67 and taka 90,69,294.71 up to 30-6-2000 against Cash Credit Pledge-Account No. 68. The respondent-bank on several occasions contacted them and asked to repay the outstanding dues but they did not take any initiative to that effect as such, the bank issued a legal notice upon them on 3-3-1999 requesting to repay the outstanding dues within 15 (fifteen) days from the date of receipt of the notice but failed.

4. It has been stated that according to দেউলিয়া বিষয়ক আইন, ১৯৯৭, (hereinafter referred to as Act, 1997) the respondent-bank is a creditor of Taka 1,20,00,000 (allotted loan) and the time of repayment of the same has expired on 31-10-1996 but the petitioners did not take any initiative to repay the loan. The bank lastly sent a legal notice to the petitioners on 13-1-2000 requesting them to repay its outstanding dues or to pay security of the dues within 90 (ninety) days from the date of receipt of the notice failing which the bank will proceed against them in accordance with the Act, 1997 seeking declaration of bankrupt. But the petitioners had failed to comply the same on time and thus, they individually and jointly committed an act of bankruptcy (দেউলিয়া কর্ম) as such, they are liable to be declared as bankrupt and hence the case.

5. On conclusion of trial, the Bankruptcy Court, Bogra, the respondent No. 2 by judgment and decree dated 28-7-2003 decreed the suit on contest. Pursuant thereto, the decree-holder- bank, the respondent No.4 filed decree execution case being No. 02 of 2004 before the said Bankruptcy Court, which is now pending for disposal before the respondent No. 5, the Bankruptcy Court No. 3, Bogra (Annexure-J).

6. It has been stated that there is no provision of filing bankruptcy decree execution case in the Act-1997.

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said impugned judgment and decree dated 28-7-2003 and the proceeding of Bank-ruptcy Decree Execution Case No. 2 of 2004, the petitioners had filed this application and obtained the instant Rule.

8. The respondent No. 3, Agrani Bank limited, head office, Dhaka entered appearance and contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition stating, inter-alia, that the petitioners contested the suit in the trial Court and the suit was decreed on contest on 28-7-2003 against which they did not prefer appeal before the Hon'ble High Court Division as per provision of section 96 of the Act, 1997 as such, the instant writ petition is not maintainable in its present form. It has also been stated that after the said judgment and decree the respondent-bank tried to contact the petitioners for recovery of the decretal amount but they did not respond to the same as such, the respondent-bank lastly filed the execution case being Decree Execution Case No. 2 of 2004. It has further been stated that the petitioners are not aggrieved persons, their fundamental rights have not been infringed and their legal rights have not been violated as such, the writ petition is not maintainable under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh.

9. At the outset, Mr Md Helal Uddin Mollah, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the learned Judge of the Bankruptcy Court passed the impugned judgment and decree without following the relevant provisions of the Act, 1997. He further goes to argue that the impugned decree execution case and its proceeding is barred by law, since there is no such provision to execute the judgment and decree of the Bankruptcy Court through instituting execution case. In the circumstances, he prays for disposing of the Rule in the light of the judgment passed in Writ Petition Nos. 7798 and 7799 of 2014.

10. Conversely, Mr Hironmay Halder, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.3 submits that as per the mandatory provision of section 96 of the Act, 1997 the petitioner is to file appeal against the impugned judgment and decree before the Hon'ble High Court Division by paying 10% of the decretal amount as such, the instant Rule is liable to be discharged for the ends of justice.

11. In support of his submission he referred to the case of Mir Niaz Mohammad vs Additional District Judge reported in 13 BLC 108.

12. Admittedly, the impugned judgment and decree was passed by the Bankruptcy Court, Bogra and as per section 96 of the Act, 1997 any person aggrieved by a decision or an order made in the exercise of bankruptcy jurisdiction may prefer appeal before the High Court Division by paying 10% of the total value of the claim of creditors as determined by the Court.

13. In the decision in the case of Mir Niaz Mohammad vs Additional District Judge reported in 13 BLC 108, paragraph-9 it was held:

"In view of the above well settled proposition of law as to the question of maintainability of the writ petition, we have no hesitation to hold that the petitioner has miserably failed to cross the first hurdle as to the question of maintainability of the instant writ petition mainly on two courts. Firstly, since the Bankruptcy Act is a special law and special provision having been provided in section 96 of the Bankruptcy Act, 1997 for preferring appeal against the judgment and decree passed by the Bankruptcy Court and therefore, the question of entertaining an application under Article 102 of the Constitution does not arise at all. Secondly, whether notice/summons was properly served or not or whether the petitioner was a guarantor/mere a shareholder of the borrower company or borrowed money from the bank or not is disputed question of facts and for which remedy lies in the Civil Court and, not under summary writ jurisdiction. So, in order to save the valuable public time since the petitioner could not cross the first hurdle, we do not think it wise to advert to the lengthy arguments made by Mr Md Idrisur Rahman for the petitioner."

14. Moreover, in an unreported recent decision passed in Writ Petition Nos. 7798 and 7799 of 2014 this Division Bench (wherein one of us was a party) held that writ petition is not maintainable challenging the judgment and decree passed by the Bankruptcy Court.

15. Mr Helal Uddin Mollah, the learned Advocate for the petitioners also concedes the said proposition of law.

16. In view of the above findings and decisions, we are of the opinion that the 1st portion of the instant Rule so far as it relates to the challenging of the impugned judgment and decree of the Bankruptcy Court is not maintainable in its present form.

17. Now, we are to see whether the 2nd portion of the instant Rule with respect to the institution of bankruptcy decree execution case pursuant to the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-7-2003 and its continuation is maintainable in its present form or not?

18. In the case in hand, the decree-holder-bank pursuant to the impugned judgment and decree filed the impugned Bankruptcy Decree Execution Case No. 02 of 2004 before the Bankruptcy Court, Bogra, which was subsequently transferred to the Bankruptcy Court No. 3, Bogra, the respondent No.5 for disposal.

19. However, there is no such provision of filing execution case in the Act, 1997 to execute the judgment and decree of the Bankruptcy Court; rather there is a provision of appointing "Receiver" under section 64 of the said Act for recovery of the decretal amount from the judgment debtor.

20. In Writ Petition Nos. 7798 and 7799 of 2014 (as mentioned hereinbefore) this Bench declared the proceeding of bankruptcy decree execution case as without jurisdiction and is of no legal effect.

21. In the above backdrop, the proceeding of Bankruptcy Execution Case No. 02 of 2004 (Annexure-J) pending before the respondent No.5 cannot be said to be lawful.

22. However, we are of the view that the decree-holder-respondent-bank may file application, if so advised, before the Bankruptcy Court concerned in respect of appointment of Receiver to execute the judgment and decree dated 28-7-2003 (Annexure-C) and to recover the decretal amount from the judgment debtors and in that case, the Court concerned be at liberty to deal with the matter expeditiously preferably within 6 (six) months from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment in accordance with law.

23. In the result, the Rule is disposed of with the above observations.

24. Stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby recalled and vacated.

Communicate the judgment to the respondents at once.

End.

lawyer:
Aneek R Haque, Advocate with Syed Sayedul Haque Suman, Advocate (in person)—For the Petitioner. 
Md Saiefuddin Khaled, DAG with Md Asaduzzaman, AAG with Afifa Begum Swapna, AAG and Samar Akhtar Masud, AAG—For the Respondent Nos. 1 and 4. 
Probir Neogi, Senior Advocate with M Sayed Ahmed, Senior Advocate and Sayeed Abdullah Al Manual Khan, Advocate—For the Respondent No. 5. 
Md Zakir Hossain (Masud), Advocate—For the Respondent No. 02. 
Md Khurshid Alam Khan, Senior Advocate—For the Anti-Corruption Commission.

full_judgment:
Md. Nazrul Islam Talukder, J: On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, this Rule Nisi, at the instance of the petitioner was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the failure/inaction of the Respondent Nos.1- 4 to take necessary legal action against the Respondent No. 5 for illegally possessing the abandoned property recorded in `Kha List' at Serial No. 46 at CEN(D)-27, Holding No. 29, Road No.104 at Guishan, Dhaka (As contained in Annexure-A) to the writ petition, should not be declared illegal, without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and why the illegal transfer of the property in question in favour of Respondent No. 5, should not be declared illegal and without lawful authority and why necessary directions shall not be given upon the concerned respondents to do the needful in this regard and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, the Respondent Nos.1, 2 and 5 were directed to submit necessary papers and documents in support of their title and possession of the land in question by way of affidavit-in-opposition within 10 (ten) days from date positively and without fail. 

3. The facts leading up to issuance of the Rule, as stated in the writ petition, runs as follows:— 
1) That the property in question recorded in `Kha List' at Serial No. 46 at CEN(D)-27, Holding No. 29, Road No. 104 at Gulshan, Dhaka" is an abandoned property. The said fact is evident from Bangladesh Gazette dated 23-9-1986 (annexure-A to the writ petition) containing in the `Kha List' showing the case land as abandoned property at Gulshan area. It is alleged that the Respondent No. 5 has been possessing the said abandoned property illegally. 
II) That the Respondent No. 5 is a member of parliament and very powerful and influential person and he, by managing the officials of RAJUK, has possessed the property stated at Serial No. 46 at CEN(D)-27. Holding No. 29, Road No. 104 at Gulshan, Dhaka. The Respondent No. 5 is also using the same property as his current residential house and in this reeard the information about the address of the MPs downloaded from the website of Bangladesh Parliament shows that the Respondent No. 5 is using the same address as his present address which is evident from Annexure-B to the writ petition. 
III) That on 13-4-2015 and 20-1-2016, the Respondent No. 1 vide letter under Memo Nos. 25.00.0000.025.038.027.13-105 and 25.00.0000.020.038/027/1318 asked for written explanation from the Respondent No. 2, the Chairman, RAJUK about the abandoned house stated at Serial No. 46 at CEN (D)-27, Holding No. 29, Road No. 104 at Guishan, Dhaka and for knowing how the same has been possessing by the Respondent No. 5, which is evident from Annexure-C to the writ petition. 
IV) That on 4-7-2019, the Respondent No. 1 again vide letter under Memo No. 25.00. 0000.020.38/96-126 requested the Respondent No. 2, the Chairman, RAJUK to give his explanation how the Respondent No. 5, obtained permission for mutation and for execution of deed for the property stated at Serial No. 46 at CEN (D)-27, Holding No. 29, Road No. 104 at Gulshan, Dhaka and the same is evident from Annexure-D to the writ petition. 
V) That in view of the above facts and circumstances, on 11-8-2022, the petitioner filed an application requesting the Respondent No. 3, the Chairman. Anti-Corruption Commission to hold inquiry into the matter as to how the Respondent No. 5 occupied the abandoned property which is contained at Serial No. 46 at CEN (D)-27, Holding No. 29, Road No. 104 at Gulshan, Dhaka and to take necessary legal action against the Respondent No. 5 which is evident from Annexure-E to the writ petition. The copy of the aforesaid application dated 11-8-2022 has duly been received by the Respondent No. 5 by putting his signature on it but till today Respondent No. 3 has taken no initiative to take any action as prayed by the petitioner and, as such, a direction is also necessary to direct the Respondent No. 5 to hold inquiry into the issue of illegal possession of the abandoned property recorded in `Kha List' at Serial No. 46 at CEN(D)-27, Holding No. 29, Road No. 104 at Gulshan, Dhaka. 

4. Upon the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the petitioner being a public spirited person being aggrieved by the failure/inaction of the Respondent Nos. 1-4 and the actions taken by the Respondent No. 5 and others, filed this writ petition before this court and obtained this Rule. 

5. After issuance of the Rule, the Respondent No. 5 by filing affidavit-in-opposition has denied all the statements and grounds taken in the writ petition and categorically stated as under:— 
a) That on 1-9-1960, DIT the then (Dhaka Improvement Trust) allotted a plot of the land measuring 1 Bigha 07 Katha via letter memo No. DIT/GULSHAN/829 in favour of Dacca Re-Rollins Mills having the address of Plot No. 27 of Block No. CEN(D), District: Dacca, Mouza: Bhola Shamair, Police Station: Tejgaon under the Lay-out Plan of "Gulshan" Model Town and on 10-1-1963, Dacca Re-Roiling Mills registered the plot bearing Registered Lease Deed No. 450 at Sadar Sub-Registry Office, Dhaka which is evident from (Annexure- 1 ) to the affidavit-in-opposition of Respondent No. 5. 
b) That thereafter, on 21-10-1969, Partners (Abdul Hamid Hassan, Abdul Rehman Ebrahim Manji, Abdul Mohamed Ebrahim Manji, Abdul Aziz Abdul Hamid, Abdul Mohamed Abdul Hamid and Abdul Sultan Abdul Hanid) of M/S Dacca Re-rolling Mills had executed an irrevocable General Power of Attorney in favour of Mr. Md. Wachiur Rahman empowering him to take all necessary steps (including executing Sale of Deed in favour of Mrs. Maleka Rahman) in regards to Plot No. 27 of Block No. : CEN(D), District: Dacca, Mouza: Bhola Shamair, Police Station: Tejgaon under the Lay-out Plan of "Gulshan" Model Town, which is evident from Annexure-14 to the Supplementary affidavit-in-opposition of Respondent No. 5. 
c) That on 11-9-1972, the Office of the Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (South). Abandoned Property Cell, Dacca notified (vide Memo No. 2216PAS/2/72) Mrs. Maleka Rahman (with, reference to the Petition No. 8147 of 1972 filed by Md. Wachiur Rahman) that on the examination of the relevant documents and other connected papers it has been proved that Mrs. Maleka Rahman is the actual owner of the said land and therefore, the house was dropped from the list of the abandoned property which is evident from Annexure-2 to the affidavit-in-opposition. 
d) That on 28-10-1975, the said Mr. Wachiur Rahman executed a Registered Deed of Sale No. 22641 in favour of Mrs. Maleka Rahman and after that the said Mrs. Maleka Rahman became the absolute owner of one bigha 7 kathas of land situated at Plot No. 27 of Block No: CEN(D), District: Dacca, Mouza: Bhola Shamair, Police Station: Tejgaon under the Lay-out Plan of "Gulshan" Model Town, which is evident from (Annexure-15) to the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition. 
e) That later on, RAJUK (DIT) gave permission for mutation of the plot in favour of Mrs. Maleka Rahman vide letter under Memo No. DIT/E0/156L on 14-1-1976. (Annexure-3 to the affidavit-in-opposition). 
f) That since the purchase, Mrs. Maleka Rahman was in the possession of the property. On 6-9-1986, Mrs. Maleka Rahman submitted an application to the DIT for permission to transfer the plot to her sons. However, before initiating the transfer process, Mrs. Maleka Rahman filed a case bearing Case No. 323/87 in the First Court of Settlement of Bangladesh Abandoned Buildings, Segunbagicha, Dhaka. Later on 24-1-1994, the settlement court stated that:—
"on perukil of the `ka' and `kha' list of the Abandoned Buildings it appears that in the 'ka' list of Abandoned Buildings the house at Serial No. 57 is CEN(D)-27 (Holding No. 15, Road No. 103) has been included as Abandoned Buildings which does not attract the house of the petitioner and in the `kha' list of the Abandoned Buildings the house at serial No. 46 of page No. 1 is CEN(D)-27 (Holding No. 29, Road No. 103) which also does not attract the house of the petitioner. 
We do not find the house No. CEN(D)-27, Holding No. 29, Road No. 103 of Gulshan Model Town, which belongs to the petitioner, in any one of the above two categories of list of Abandoned Buildings. So, the case is misconceived one and it is dismissed on the same ground". (Annexure-4 to affidavit-in-opposition). 
g) That thereafter, on 12-3-1995, Mrs. Maleka Rahman gifted the plot to her two (2) sons namely Mir Mohammad Hasan and Mir Mohammad Nurul Afsar. (Annexure-5 to the affidavit-in-opposition) 
h) That on 18-2-1996, Mr. Abdus Sobahan, Assistant Secretary of Ministry of Housing and Public Works via letter under Memo No. SHAKHA-9/1P-GUL-100/76/28 informed Mrs. Maleka Rahman that House No. CEN (D)-27, Holding No. 29, Road No. 103. Gulshan Model Town, Dhaka is not in the list of the published gazette for Abandoned Buildings by the Bangladesh Government and for that reason there is no scope to release the plot from the `ka' and `kha' list of Abandoned Buildings. (Annexure-6 to the affidavit-in-opposition) 
i) That thereafter, Rajuk mutated the plot in the name of Mrs. Maleka Rahman's sons namely Mir Mohammad Hasan and Mir Mohammd Nurul Afser vide Memo No. RAJUK/ESTATE/1851 dated 7-7-1996 after the mutation. 
j) That Mrs. Maleka Rahman's 2 (two) sons namely Mir Mohammad Hasan and Mir Mohammad Nurul Afser applied for the partition of the said plot to the RAJUK. Following the application, on 7-9-1996 the RAJUK gave permission to divide Plot No. 27 of Block No. CEN(D) into 27A and 27B measuring 12 katha and 15 katha respectively by which the new holding address becomes Plot No. 27A of Block No. CEN(D), Road No: 103 and Plot No. 27B of Block No. CEN(D), Road No: 103. Mir Mohammad Hasan and Mir Mohammad Nurul Afser also mutated the said land in their name and paid rent in the concerned land office which is evident from Annexure-7, 7A and 7B to the affidavit-in-opposition. 
k) That on 15-3-1997, Mir Mohmmad Hasan and Mir Mohammad Nurul Afser submitted an application to RAJUK for permission to sell Plot No. 27B of Block No. CEN(D), Road No: 103 to Respondent No. 5 and accordingly, on 31-3-1997, the concerned officials of RAJUK gave permission to sell the property to Respondent No. 5 vide letter under Memo No. RAJUK/ESTATE/ 1034STHA which is evident from Annexure-8 and 8A to the affidavit-in-opposition. 
l) That after obtaining permission from RAJUK, Respondent No. 5 purchased the said Plot No. 27B of Block No. CEN(D), Road No: 103 from Mir Mohammad Hasan and Mir Mohammad Nurul Afser vide Deed of sale bearing No. 9977 dated 29-6-1997 under the Gulshan Sub-Register-Office, Dhaka which is evident from Annexure-9 to the affidavit-in-opposition. 
m) That after purchasing Plot No. 27B of Block No. CEN(D), Road No: 103, Respondent No. 5 applied for mutation and via letter Memo No. RAJUK/ ESTATE/167STHA dated 14-1-1998, the concerned official of RAJUK mutated the said land in the name of Respondent No. 5, which is evident from Annexure-10 to the affidavit-in-opposition. 
n) That on 22-11-1998, Dhaka City Corporation issued the office memo for Plot No. 27B of Block No. CEN(D), Road No: 103 stating that from now on, Respondent No. 5 will pay holding tax for the said premises and after that, Respondent No. 5 also mutated his name in the concerned land office and thereby, paid rent of the said land, which is evident from Annexure-11, 11A and 11B to the affidavit-in-opposition. 
o) That thereafter Mr. Abdus Alam Murshedy, the Respondent No. 5 took water, electricity, gas and telephone connection at Plot No. 27B of Block No. CEN(D), Road No: 103 and all utility connections were provided in the name of the Respondent No. 5, which is evident from Annexure-12, 12A, 12B and 12C to the affidavit-in-opposition. 
p) That on 31-3-1997, RAJUK permitted to sell the other portion of Plot No. 27 of Block No. CEN(D), Road No: 103 which is Plot No. 27A of Block No. CEN(D), Road No: 103, to Mrs. Iffat Haque, wife of Mr. M.A. Moin having an address of 2/9, Block-D, Lalmatia, Dhaka vide RAJUK/ESTATE/1033- STHA. Accordingly, on 29-6-1997, that plot was registered in the name of Mrs. Iffat Haque bearing the Registered Deed No. 10073 and Plot No. 27A of Block No. CEN(D), Road No: 103 and the same was mutated in her name on 14-1-1998 vide letter Memo No. RAJUK/ ESTATE/168STHA. 
q) That regarding House No. 27/B, Road Ne 103, Gulshan 2, Dhaka-1212, an Enquiry Committee was formed consisting of 5 (five) members of RAJUK and on 27-3-2016, the said Enquiry Committee categorically stated that the said plot has already been released from the list of "Abandoned Property" on 11-9-1972 vide office Memo No. 2216 PAS/2/72 dated 11-9-1972 issued by Abandon Property Cell of Sadar Sub Divisional Office. The Committee further stated that the said house is situated in both Road No.103 and 104 since, it's a corner plot, which is evident from Annexure-13 to the affidavit-in-opposition. 

6. Being aggrieved by the inaction of the Respondent Nos.1-4 to take necessary legal action against the Respondent No. 5 for illegally possessing the abandoned property, the petitioner filed this writ petition and obtained this Rule. 

7. At the very outset, Mr. Aneek R. Haque, the learned Advocate with Mr. Syed Sayedul Haque Suman, the learned Advocate (in person), appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that since the Respondent No.1, the Ministry of lfousing and Public Works on 13-4-2015, 20-1-2016 and 4-7-2022 constantly requested the Respondent No.2 to give explanation how the Respondent No.5 occupied and possessed the abandoned property recorded in `Kha List' without releasing the same lawfully and how the Respondent No.5 obtained permission from respondent No.2 for mutation and for execution of title deed for the abandoned property but the Respondent No.2 is reluctant to pay heed to the matter and. as such. a direction by this court is necessary directing the Respondent No.3 to hold enquiry into the issue of illegal possession of the abandoned property by the Respondent No.5 recorded in 'Kha List' at Serial No. 46 at CEN(D) -27, Holding No.29, Road No.104 at Gulshan, Dhaka. 

8. He next submits that the Respondent No.5 by illegal means or by abusing his position or by corruption occupied the abandoned property recorded in `Kha List' at Serial No.46 at CEN (D)-27, Holding No.29, Road No.104 at Gulshan, Dhaka and the Respondent No.3 is duty-bound to look into the matter but the Respondent No.3 failed to act as per the statutory requirement and, as such, the failure/inaction of the Respondent No.3 to look into the matter is liable to declared to have been done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

9. He then submits that the available evidence indicates that the Respondent No.5 in abusing his position most illegally occupied and possessed the abandoned property and obtained permission for mutation and for execution of title deed violating the provision of law and, as such, a direction by this court is necessary directing the Respondent No.3 to hold an enquiry into the issue of illegal possession of the abandoned property recorded in Kha List at Serial No.46 at CEN(D)-27, Holding No.29, Road No.104 at Gulshan, Dhaka. 

10. He candidly submits that as per Bangladesh Gazette dated 23-9-1986, (annexure-A to the writ petition), the property has been published in the Bangladesh Gazette as an abandoned property and that the said property has not been released in lawful manner following the provisions of law, so this property is still an abandoned property. 

11. He additionally submits that on 22-9-2014, the Respondent No. 5 knowing fully about the abandoned property submitted an application before the Secretary. Ministry of Housing and Public Work for releasing the property from "Kha" list though he is not a proper authority for releasing the property from the list of abandoned property and the same is still pending because he has no authority to release the property from the list of the abandoned property and this application was filed in the year of 2014 and since then it is pending for decision and disposal. 

12. He vigorously submits that the concerned ministry communicated so many letters to the Chairman, Rajuk questioning how the property was mutated and transferred to somebody else but no answer has been found till today and they remained silent till now. 

13. He strongly submits that it is apparent from the FIR submitted by the Anti-Corruption Commission that the property in question is an abandoned property and the Respondent No. 5 along with others in collaboration with each other transferred the property without releasing the abandoned property from the list of the abandoned property and unless the property is released from the list of abandoned property, all the subsequent transfers are illegal and have no legal basis at all. 

14. He strenuously submits that though it is submitted by the learned Advocates for the Respondent No. 5 that the property in question was released from the list of abandoned property which is evident from Annexure-2, Annexure-4 and Annexure-7 of the affidavit-in-opposition dated 10-11-2022 but the property as stated therein is not similar with the property mentioned in the writ petition and the list of the abandoned property. 

15. He has pointed out that from the judgment of the First Court of Settlement. Bangladesh Abandoned Building, Segunbagicha, Dhaka. (annexure-4 to the affidavit-in-opposition dated 10-11-2022), it appears that the property was mentioned therein as house No CEN(D)-27, Holding No. 15, Road No. 103, but the property mentioned in the writ petition and the list of the abandoned property, is house No. CEN (D)-27. Holding No.29, Road No.104 at Serial No.46 at Gulshan, Dhaka so there is no similarity of the property which has been mentioned in the judgment of the settlement court and in the writ petition together with Bangladesh Gazette dated 23-9-1986. 

16. He categorically submits that the Anti-Corruption Commission has already initiated a case by filing an FIR and the same is underway for investigation so, at this stage, the Respondent No. 1 may be directed to continue with the investigation and to proceed against the persons who are involved in the commission of forgery and abetment in releasing the property from the list of the abandoned property and by making subsequent transfer to defraud the Government making mechanical release of the property from the list of abandoned property and under such circumstances, this Rule may be made absolute directing the Anti-Corruption Commission and other stakeholders and the concerned respondents to proceed with the matter in accordance with law. 

17. He lastly submits that since the property in question is the Government property characterizing it as an abandoned property so the property must go in favour of the Government and the persons who are involved in making forgery and abetment may be brought to justice in accordance with law. 

18. Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the Anti-Corruption Commission, submits that they held an enquiry into the matter following the order of this court and submitted enquiry report and found that the property in question is an abandoned property and there is a forgery in transfer of the property to Respondent No. 5 and others and, as such, this matter may be investigated properly and direction may be given so that investigation may be continued for ends of justice. 

19. 48. Before coming to decision in this matter, we want to make a brief discussion on abandoned property. 

49. The concept of "abandoned property" in Bangladesh dates back to the political upheavals around the Partition of India (1947) and the Liberation War of 1971. It primarily refers to properties left behind by owners who migrated-often due to communal violence, political instability, or war. When British India was partitioned into India and Pakistan in 1947, a large number of Hindus migrated from East Pakistan (now Bangladesh) to India, while many Muslims migrated from India to East Pakistan. The Pakistan government declared many properties left behind by Hindus as "evacuee property." These properties were managed under the East Bengal (Evacuee Property) Act, 1949, on behalf of the owners. After Bangladesh gained independence in 1971, a new wave of property abandonment occurred, especially properties left behind by non-Bengalis (Biharis) and those who were considered to have collaborated with the Pakistani army. To handle these, the Bangladesh government enacted several laws: The abandoned property (Control, Management and Disposal) Order, 1972), declared any property whose owner was absent from Bangladesh during or after the war as "abandoned property." The Abandoned Property (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance. 1977, provided further clarification on administration and disposal of such properties. The Ministry of Housing and Public Works and Custodian of Enemy and Abandoned Property were given authority to manage these properties.

61. It is stated by the Anti-Corruption Commission in its affidavit-in-compliance dated 8-2-2024 that the Respondent No. 5, Abdus Salam Murshedi, CEN(D)27/B, Gulshan, Dhaka filed an application before the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Words, Bangladesh Secretariat, Dhaka for excluding the house from the "Kha" list of the House No. CEN(D)-27 (27B) Holding No.29, Road No.104, Gulshan, Dhaka. This statement along with the application has not been opposed or denied by the Respondent No. 5 by any means. For convenience of discussion. we want to quote the said application as under:— 
বরাবর, 
সচিব মহোদয় গৃহায়ন ও গনপূর্ত মন্ত্রণালয় 
বাংলাদেশ সচিবালয়, ঢাকা।
বিষয়ঃ সি.ই.এ. (ডি)-২৭ (২৭বি) হোল্ডিং নং ২৯, রোড নং ১০৪, গুলশান, ঢাকা বাড়ীটি পরিত্যক্ত খ তালিকা হইতে অবমুক্তির।
মহোদয়,
বিনীত নিবেদন এই যে, গুলশান আবাসিক এলাকার সি.ই.এন (ডি)-২৭ নং প্লটটি মূল মালিকের আবেদনের প্রেক্ষিতে রাজধানী উন্নয়ন কর্তৃপক্ষ কর্তৃক বিভাজন করতঃ সিইএন (ডি)-২৭এ ও সিইএন (ডি) ২৭বি নামক ২টি প্লট সৃজন করা হয়। অতঃপর রাজউক স্মারক নং রাজউক/এষ্টেট/১০৩৪ স্থাঃ তাং ৩১-৩-১৯৯৭ ইং মাধ্যমে হস্তান্তরের অনুমতি প্রাপ্ত হইয়া মূল মালিক কর্তৃক বিগত ২৯-৬-১৯৯৭ইং তারিখে রেজিস্ট্রিকৃত সাব কবলা দলিল নং ৯৯৭৭ নএর মাধ্যমে নিম্ন স্বাক্ষরকারী বরাবর ২৭বি প্লটটির স্বত্ব ও দখল হস্তান্তর করা হয়। এইরুপ ক্রয় সূত্রে বর্ণিত প্লটটির স্বত্ব দখলকার নিয়ত হইয়া রাজউক এবং সংশ্লিষ্ট সহকারী কমিশনার (ভূমি) অফিসে নামজারী করতঃ সরকারী খাজনাদি প্রদানের মাধ্যমে বর্ণিত প্লটটির রাজউক কর্তৃক নকশা অনুমোদন করিয়া বসতবাড়ী নির্মান করতঃ শান্তিপূর্ণ ভোগ দখলে নিয়ত আছি। সম্প্রতি কালে সংশ্লিষ্ট ভূমি অফিসের খাজনা প্রদা�� কালে জানা যায় যে, বর্ণিত ২৭ নং প্লটটি ১৯৮৬ সনের গেজেট মোতাবেক সরকারের পরিত্যক্ত সম্পত্তি “খ” তালিকায় অন্তর্ভূক্ত রহিয়াছে। প্রকৃত পক্ষে বর্ণিত সম্পত্তিটি পরিত্যক্ত নহে এবং এতদ্?সংক্রান্ত আমার যাবতীয় কাগজ পত্রাদি আপনার বরাবরে জমা প্রদান করিলাম। অতএব প্রার্থনা, প্রদানকৃত কাগজ পত্রাদি যথাযথ ভাবে যাচাই বাছাই অন্তে বর্ণিত প্লটটি “খ” তালিকা ভূক্ত হইতে অবমুক্তির প্রয়োজনীয় আদেশ প্রদানে মহোদয়ের মর্জি হয়।
বিনীত নিবেদক,
আব্দুস সালাম মুর্শেদী 
সি.ই.এন. (ডি) ২৭/বি 
গুলশান, ঢাকা।

62. In the aforesaid letter, the Respondent No. 5 has clearly admitted that the property in question is an abandoned property and the same has not been released from the list of abandoned property. 

63. Furthermore, from the enquiry report, it has been spelt out that ingredients of cheating by personation. forgery of valuable security and document, forgery for the purpose of cheating using the forged document as genuine as well as the abetment of forgery and criminal misconduct by the public servants by using their position have been made out and, as such, the Durnity Daman Commission relying upon the enquiry report based on oral and documentary evidence lodged the case under sections 420/467/468/471/109 of the Penal Code, 1860 read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (II of 1947). 

64. The learned Advocate for the Respondent No.5 has pointed out that the respondent No.5 is a bonafide purchaser who purchased the property in question from the two sons of Mrs Maleka Parvin and he has got the land mutated in his name and he is also paying rent and different bills to the government against the property; furthermore, he has produced the registered deeds in support of his title and possession over the case property and as per section 60 of the Registration Act, 1908 and section 103 of the Evidence Act, 1872, the title deeds of the Respondent No.5 are presumed to be correct and valid until those are cancelled and declared illegal under sections 39 and 43 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877: moreover, the writ petition contains a disputed questions of fact which cannot be decided in this writ petition and the petitioner is not an aggrieved person having no locus standi to file the instant writ petition and, as such, the writ petition is not maintainable and sustainable in the eye of law. 

65. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials of record submitted by the respective parties. our considered view is that admittedly, the property in question is an abandoned property which is evident from Annexure-A to the writ petition and the property in question has not been released from the list of abandoned property by the competent authority and it is not a disputed question of fact, hence this writ petition is very much maintainable and sustainable in the eye of law; furthermore, we have found that Md. Wachiur Rahman and his wife Mrs Maleka Parvin in connivance with other vested quarters transferred the property to different persons including the respondent No.5 camouflaging he identity of the property in question. In that view of the matter though the property was transferred in the name of respondent No. 5 and others, our considered view is that the nature and character of the case property as abandoned property has not been changed even though the property has been transferred in the name of respondent No.5 and others since the property in question has not been released by a competent authority following the provisions of law. 

66. The learned Advocates for the Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 have pointed out that the Rule has been issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why failure/inaction of the Respondent Nos. 1-4 to take necessary legal action against the Respondent No. 5 for illegally possessing the abandoned property recorded in `Kha List' at Serial No. 46 at CEN(D)-27, Holding No. 29, Road No. 104 at Gulshan, Dhaka (As contained in Annexure-A), should not be declared illegal. without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and why the illegal transfer of the property in question in favour of Respondent No.5, should not be declared illegal and without lawful authority and why necessary directions shall not be given upon the concerned respondent to do the needful in this regard but the fact remains that the concerned respondents have taken necessary steps in this regard and as a result of which the Anti-Corruption Commission has already initiated a criminal case by filing an FIR against the II (eleven) persons so under such circumstances, since they have already taken steps there is no inaction in the present matter at hands and under such circumstances the Rule may be disposed of with necessary direction and order. 

67. Anyway, it will not be out of place to mention that there is a land scarcity in the Capital of the Country. However some influential individuals are trying to acquire them through unfair means. The same undermines equity, reduces public access and erodes trust in institution. 

68. Under the aforesaid facts and circumstances, we are inclined to dispose of the Rule by making the following directions and orders:—
1. That the property in question has not lost its nature and character as an abandoned property and it will remain as an abandoned property unless or until the property in question is released from competent court of law. 
2. That since the property is an abandoned property, the subsequent transfers by the interested persons by making different papers and documents without releasing the same from the list of abandoned property by the competent authority are, ipso facto, inoperative and not binding upon the government. 
3. That since the property is the property of the Government, the Respondent No. 5 is directed to handover the property to the government represented by the Respondent No. 1, Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works. 
4. That from the facts narrated above, our conclusive view is that many persons are trying to grab this property by many means since it is a valuable property situated at the lucrative place of the Capital of the Country; moreover, due to scarcity of land in the Capital of the Country, the concerned respondents are directed to reserve/use this property for public purposes rather than leasing them to private individuals. 
5. That since FIR has been lodged, the Anti-Corruption Commission is directed to proceed with the investigation in accordance with law following the provision of Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 and they are also directed to proceed with the persons who are involved in the commission of forgery and abetment in any way in transferring the property in the name of Respondent No. 5 and others if any. 
6. That the Respondent No. 5 is directed to handover the possession of the house in question to the Government represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works within 3 (three) months from the date of receipt of this judgment and order. 
7. That the Respondent No. 1 is also directed to take over the possession of the house within 3 (three) months and submit affidavit-in-compliance before this court stating clearly whether they have taken over the possession of the house through the Registrar, High Court Division, Supreme Court of Bangladesh within 15 (fifteen) days from the date of taking over possession of the property in question. 

69. With the aforesaid observation, direction and order, the Rule is disposed of. 

Communicate the judgment and order to the concerned respondents, at once. 

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 3314 of 2014
lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate with Alikur Rahman, Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners
Moudud Ahmed, Senior Advocate instructed by Md. Taufique Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent No. 1. 
None Represented ------ For Respondent Nos. 2-6
parties:
Comprehensive Holdings Limited and another ------ Petitioners
Vs.
MH Khan Monju and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 28th day of May, 2014 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 194 of 2012 with Civil Rule 444(0 of 2012)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J: This petition for leave to appeal has been filed against the judgment and decree dated the 28th day of May, 2014 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 194 of 2012 allowing the appeal.

2. Facts necessary to dispose this petition are that respondent No. 1 as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No.202 of 2010 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka for the following relief:

(a) Declaration that the allotment of 2 (two) apartments in the name of the plaintiff as fully described in Schedule to the plaint pursuant to the booking money received by the Principal defendants dated 16-6-2007 and the payment schedule dated 19-6-2007 followed by the booking money is valid, lawful, still subsists and thereby creates legal obligation of the Principal defendants to handover the apartment in favour of the plaintiff;

(b) Declaration that the impugned letter issued by the Principal defendant No. 1 under the signature of the Principal defendant No.3 dated 11-7-2000 for taking back of the booking money is illegal, void, malafide, fraudulent authority and not binding upon the plaintiff;

(c) To pass a decree for mandatory injunction directing the Principal defendants to handover 2(two) complete and ready apartments to the plaintiff as fully described in the Schedule to the plaint pursuant to the payment received by them on 16-6-2007 by taking the balance consideration money from the plaintiff within a certain period at the cost of the Principal defendants;

(d) To pass an order of injunction restraining the Principal defendants from selling or handing over the apartments described in Schedule to anybody else except the plaintiff and or pass such other order or orders as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper for ends of justice.

(e) Cost of the suit and exemplary cost be awarded in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants for harassment and malafide activities of the Principal defendants."

3. In the plaint, it was stated, inter alia, that the plaintiffs relative, late Mohiuddin Ahmed (former IGP), was the lessee of the suit premises who died leaving behind the sons and the daughters as his heirs who were the present land owners with whom the principal-defendants (in law there is nothing as the principal-defendant, but will be referred to so, as mentioned in the plaint) entered into an agreement for construction of a multi-storied building and subsequently allotted two apartments in favour of the plaintiff and received a sum of Taka 30,00,000 (thirty lac) from him against the total price of the apartments. The price for the two apartments being Nos.A-4 and A-5 comprising an area of 1700 square feet of each apartment with 2(two) car parking spaces, was fixed at Taka 4,800 00 (four thousand eight hundred) per square feet and the consolidated price of the 2(two) apartments were settled at Taka 1,69,20,000 (one crore sixty nine lac and twenty thousand taka only). The booking was given by the principal-defendants taking the said sum of Taka 30,00,000 (thirty lac) as booking money from the plaintiff through 6 (six) cheques bearing Nos.CD-10/AA 7768263, 7768264 dated 16-6-2007 of Janata Bank, College Gate Branch, Dhaka and Cheque No.3842622, 3843623 dated 16-6-2007 of Janata Bank College Gate Branch, Dhaka. The aforesaid 6(Six) cheques of Taka 5,00,000 each were duly encashed by the principal-defendants and they issued booking slip with payment schedule dated 19-6-2007. The plaintiff paid the aforesaid booking money and made up his mind to make payment of the balance consideration price according to the payment schedule. The plaintiff came to know that the principal-defendants could not obtain the approval of the plan from the RAJUK due to the dispute between the co-sharers of the suit premises. As a result, they could not start construction work for a long time. The plaintiff met the principal-defendants and one Tanvir Ahmed, Executive of the developer company who informed him that the approval of the plan was being delayed due to some dispute between the co-shares which may delay the project for indefinite time and at this stage they would not take any money from the plaintiff. He further assured that after removal of the dispute, the developer will try to have approval of the plan from the RAJUK and after that they would receive the balance amount. Thereafter, the plaintiff met the DMD of the company who assured him that he (the plaintiff) was not required to pay the balance money at that stage and the balance price would be taken after approval of plan and he advised the plaintiff "to stay over and cool down for the time being." In the "erstwhile" of December, 2008, the plaintiff again requested the marketing officer of the developer company, Tanvir Ahmed to let him know the development of the approval of the plan and construction of the real estate building and Tanvir informed the plaintiff that the approval of plan was on process and it was forthcoming. He then asked the plaintiff to come to their office for discussion and accordingly the plaintiff went to the office and met the DMD of the developer company and on lengthy discussion, the DMD demanded Taka 6500 per square feet otherwise he threatened that they would sell the apartments to another person. After a long bargaining, the "DMD stroke on a price of Taka, 6200 per square feet which was not acceptable to the plaintiff. The plaintiff felt serious shock in his mind for such malafide and fraudulent attitude of the developer company.

4. The plaintiff was awaiting for approval of the plan. The principal-defendants took money from the plaintiff on 16-6-2007 and submitted the plan to the RAJUK on 15-5-2009 and the RAJUK approved the plan on 30-7-2009 for construction of a 8 (eight) storied residential building in the suit premises which was communicated to the landowners as well as the developer vide Memo No. নঅ/৩সি-১-০১২৯/০৯/২২৬-৩সি-১/এ ১২৯/০৯ dated 4-10-2009. After approval of the plan, the principal defendants started construction work in the last part of December, 2009 and the basic construction work was going on. The plaintiff approached the principal-defendants from time to time, but they refused to receive the money. The plaintiff finding no other alternative filed an application to the President of REHAB for getting justice and REHAB being the guardian of all developers issued a letter on 7-4-2009 requesting the principal-defendants to consider the grievance of the plaintiff and directed them to do the needful in accordance with the law. But the principal defendants having failed to realize excess money @ 1400 (6200/4800 = 1400) for per square feet as demanded earlier issued the impugned letter on 11-7-2010 requesting the plaintiff to take back his money. The principal-defendants made false statements in the impugned letter and also practiced fraud in making a false statement that the plaintiff did not make the payment following the payment schedule and avoided their request vide the so- called letters dated 4-7-2007 and 4-8-2007 which had no practical existence and the developer might have created some documents with malafide intention to use the same against the plaintiff and, as such, the impugned letter issued by principal-defendant No.3 was illegal, void, malafide, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff and that the plaintiff was entitled to necessary declaration against the impugned letter and his right was required to be protected by the Court. The plan having been approved on 30-7-2009 was communicated vide Memo dated 4-10-2009, the question of issuance of the notices for making payment on 4-7-2007 or 4-8-2007 did not arise at all. At that time the plan was not submitted and the developer company delayed the project for their own problem and not for any problem created by the plaintiff and, as such, the impugned letter was liable to be declared to be illegal, void abinitio, malafide and without any lawful authority. The plaintiff was always ready to pay the balance consideration money but the developer demanded much more excess price from the payment schedule which tantamount to fraud on the part of the developer with intent to cheat the innocent plaintiff for procuring more money by the trap. The cause of action for the suit first arose on 16-6-2007, when the principal defendants received the booking money of Taka 30,00,000 lac from the plaintiff and then on 19-6-2007 when the principal defendants issued the booking receipt of 2 apartments along with the payment schedule and then on different dates when the plaintiff approached the principal-

defendants to take money from him and lastly on 7-4-2009 (this date has been wrongly mentioned, the correct date is 11-7-2010), when principal-defendant No.3 issued the impugned letter for taking back the booking money and the cause of action was still subsisting within Police Station, Dhanmondi under the jurisdiction of the Court.

5. In the suit, the petitioners herein who were defendant Nos. 1 and 3 and defendant No.2 appeared and filed written statement and then filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 read with section 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the plaintiff had no contractual or legal right in respect of the two apartments and the two car parking spaces along with the undivided and undemarcated share of land in question inasmuch as no contract was made between the plaintiff and principle defendant No.1, namely, the Company; that in view of the provisions of section 54A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 as inserted by Act XVI of 2004 and section 21A of the Specific Relief Act as inserted by Act XXVII of 2004 and section 17A of the Registration Act, 1908, a party must have a registered contract for the purchase of any immovable property and in the absence of a registered contract, no contract claimed by a party can be enforced through the process of the law, but the plaintiff did not have any contract at all. The plaintiff filed the suit for declaration that allotment of two apartments was made in his name and such declaration was in effect a declaration as to a contract; it was well settled that a party to a suit could not seek any declaration as to a contract and more importantly the plaintiff had no contract with principal-defendant No.1; that the plaintiff had no legal right to enforce in court, as it was evident from the avennent made in the plaint or in other words, he had no valid and legal enforceable contract in support of the case made out in the plaint and hence the plaint of the suit disclosed no cause of action; that since the plaintiff had no registered deed of agreement in support of his claim over the two apartments and two car parking spaces along with undivided and undemarcated share of the land in question, his claim was not legally maintainable; that the prayers made in the plaint were found upon contractual right as he made his claim in respect of the two apartments and the two car parking spaces along with the undivided and undemarcated share of the land in question and since he had no registered contract in support of his claim for the two apartments and the two car parking spaces along with the undivided and undemarcated share of the land in question; the prayers made in the plaint could not be granted by the Court; consequently, the plaint was liable to be rejected.

6. The application was opposed by the plaintiff by filing a written objection contending, inter alia, that the exigencies under which a plaint could be rejected under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code were absent in the instant case and, as such, the question of rejection of the plaint did not arise at all; that the plaint was not liable to be rejected either under section 54A of the Transfer of Property Act or under section 17A of the Registration Act or under section 21 A of the Specific Relief Act; that the fact alleged in the plaint and the question raised by the defendants could only be decided on thrashing out the evidence to be produced by the parties at the peremptory hearing of the suit.

7. The application for rejection of the plaint was heard along with the application for temporary injunction filed by the plaintiff and the learned Joint District Judge by his order dated 10-4-2012 rejected the application for temporary injunction, but allowed the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code and rejected the plaint on the findings that the two apartments and the two spaces for car parking were in the category of immovable property and that no written agreement was executed and registered between the plaintiff and the defendants, rather on 16-6-2007, the plaintiff paid Taka 30,00,000 to the defendants by 6 (six) cheques as a booking money and entered into an oral contract with them to purchase the suit premises, but the provisions of sections 54A of the Transfer of Property Act, section 21 of the Specific Relief Act and section 17A of the Registration Act did not approve entering into any unregistered agreement to sell an immovable property and such kind of contract was not enforceable in law. The learned Joint District Judge further held an agreement for sale of an immovable property must be written and registered and that by the oral agreement, no title and right was created in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the two apartments and the two car parking spaces. Therefore, the plaintiff was not entitled to any declaratory or mandatory decree from the Court. The learned Joint District Judge concluded that considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, it appeared to him that there was no cause of action to file the suit and the same was barred under the provisions of Order VII, rules 11(a) and 11(d) of the Code.

8. Since the order rejecting the plaint is a decree with the meaning of section 2(2) of the Code, the plaintiff filed the above mentioned first appeal before the High Court Division and a Division Bench by the impugned judgment and decree allowed the same, set aside the decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge with the direction upon the trial Court to proceed with the suit in accordance with the law. The learned Judges also made the observation that "If defendants want to bury the suit at an early date they can do so by invoking provision of Order 14 Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure by framing special issue as to maintainability of the suit"; hence this petition for leave to appeal.

9. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Counsel, for the petitioners, in fact, canvassed the grounds on which the learned Joint District Judge rejected the plaint. In support of his contention, he has relied upon the relevant provisions of the three laws, namely, section 54A of the Transfer of Property Act, section 21A of the Specific Relief Act and section 17A of the Registration Act and submitted that the High Court Division passed the impugned judgment and decree on total misreading and misconception of those provisions of the laws as well as the provisions of sections 42 and 55 of the Specific Relief Act and the facts stated in the plaint along with prayers made therein and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree calls for interference by this Court by giving leave.

10. Mr. Moudud Ahmed, learned Counsel, who entered caveat on behalf of respondent No.1 has supported the impugned judgment and decree. He has further submitted that reading the plaint as a whole along with the relief sought therein, it is prima-facie clear that the plaintiff had cause of action to maintain the suit and the nature of the transaction did not require any written agreement and that to be registered too and that the provisions of sections 54A of the Transfer of Property Act, section 21A of the Specific Relief Act and section 17A of the Registration Act had no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the case as stated in the plaint. He has lastly submitted that the questions raised by the defendants need a full-fledged hearing of the suit and to be decided on the evidence to be produced by the parties at the peremptory hearing of the suit, the High Court Division did not commit any error of law in passing the impugned judgment and decree and the same does not call for any interference by this Court and there being no merit in the leave petition, the same be dismissed.

11. From the impugned judgment, it appears that the High Court Division allowed the appeal on the finding, inter alia, that "It has been decided by all the Court of this subcontinent that the plaint was to be rejected within the four corners of the plaint. On a reading of the plaint it appears that plaintiff nowhere stated that there was an agreement or the agreement was registered or not. It is a plain case that plaintiff was given assurance for two apartments but later on, dispute arose. Defendant cancelled it. The Plaintiff, through this suit, questioned the action of developer to the effect that allotment of two apartments in the name of plaintiff being cancelled by the impugned letter with the signature of principal-defendant after taking booking money. The booking money is with the defendants and suit instituted for not performing of contract. We find that the plaint cannot be rejected under any of the provision of Order VI sub-rule (a) and (b) of the said order. Law, as has been applied, was applied wrongly without applying judicial mind. We find substance in this appeal."

12. From a reading of the plaint, it appears that the plaintiff did not at al assert that there was any agreement written or oral between him and the defendants for purchasing the two apartments of the building to be constructed by the principal-defendants (hereinafter referred to as the developer) along with the two car parking spaces on the suit premises. What he stated in the plaint was that the two apartments were booked in his name receiving booking money of Taka 30,00,000 by giving booking slip by the developer along with the payment schedule. The booking was cancelled by the developer asking the plaintiff to take back the booking money which, in fact, gave cause of action to the plaintiff to file the suit.

13. From the order of the trial Court, it appears that it treated the two apartments and the 2 (two) car parking spaces which were booked for the plaintiff by the developer against the receipt of booking money of Taka 30,00,000 as immovable property. The trial Court further held that the plaintiff entered into an oral agreement with the developer for purchasing the two apartments by paying booking money to the tune of taka 30,00,000 by 6 (six) cheques on 16-6-2007 and such oral contract was barred by law and was not enforceable in law and that by such oral contract, the plaintiff did not acquire any right, title and interest in the two apartments and car parking spaces, so the plaintiff was not entitled to get any declaratory decree and decree for mandatory injunction as well from the Court. In holding so, the trial Court totally misread the plaint inasmuch as nowhere in the plaint, the plaintiff ever said that there was an oral contract between him and the developer to purchase the two apartments and the two car parking spaces,

14. So, the first question that has to be looked into in this case is whether the two apartments and the two car parking spaces which were booked by the developers for the plaintiff on receipt of the booking money and giving booking slip and payment schedule can be treated as an immovable property as defined in section 3 of the Transfer of Property Act which reads as under:

"immovable property" does not include standing Timber, growing crops or grass."

And to decide the question, we have to see the provisions of রিয়েল এস্টেট উন্নয়ন ও ব্যবস্থাপনা আইন, ২০১০ in short, the Ain, 2010 which was gazetted on 5th October, 2010. Sections 19-32 of the Ain, 2010 were given immediate effect, but the other provisions of the Ain were given retrospective effect with effect from December, 2008. The preamble of the Ain, 2010 reads as under:

“রিয়েল এস্টেট উন্নয়ন ও উহার ব্যবস্থাপনা অন্যান্য আনুষঙ্গিক বিষয়ে বিধান প্রণয়নকল্পে প্রণীত আইন

যেহেতু রিয়েল এস্টেট ও উহার ব্যবস্থাপনাসহ অন্যান্য আনুষঙ্গিক বিষয়ে বিধান প্রণয়ন করা সমীচীন ও প্রয়োজনীয়

সেহেতু এতদ্বারা নিম্নরূপ আইন করা হইল”

15. The very preamble of the Ain, 2010 shows that the enactment of the law was necessary for the development of the real estate and its management along with other relevant

matters and in this Ain, for the first time, a new concept of a property such as "real estate" was brought which is altogether different from the immovable property as defined in section 3 of the Transfer of Property Act and it will be more clear if we see the definition of "real estate" as given in section 2(12) in the Ain, 2010 which reads as under:

“২। সংজ্ঞা।–বিষয় বা প্রসঙ্গের পরিপন্থী কোন কিছু না থাকিলে, এই আইনে-

(১২)“রিয়েল এস্টেট (real estate)” রিয়েল এস্টেট অর্থ উন্নয়ন, ব্যবস্থাপনা ও ক্রয়-বিক্রয়ে নিমিত্ত আবাসিক বা প্রতিষ্ঠানিক বা বাণিজ্যিক প্লট অথবা এপার্টমেন্ট বা ফ্ল্যাট, প্রতিষ্ঠানিক বা মিশ্র ফ্লোর স্পেস জাতীয় স্থাবর ভূ-সম্পত্তি”

<u>16. From the above quoted definition, it is prima facie clear that the "real estate" is conceptually and practically quite different from the immovable property as defined in the Transfer of Property Act. Two other definitions, namely, "ক্রেতা" and "রিয়েল এস্টেট ডেভেলপার বা ডেভেলপার" are also relevant to understand the concept of "real estate", a new phenomenon of immovable property different from the "immovable property" as defined in the Transfer of Property Act and those read as follows:</u>

<u>“২। (৪) “ক্রেতা” অর্থ রিয়েল এস্টেট ক্রয়ের উদ্দেশ্য রিয়েল এস্টেট ডেভেলপার এর সহিত চুক্তিবদ্ধ কোন ব্যক্তি”</u>

<u>(১৫) “রিয়েল এস্টেট ডেভেলপার” অর্থ রিয়েল এস্টেট ব্যবসা পরিচালনার উদ্দেশ্য এই আইনের ধারা ৫ এর অধীন নিবন্ধিত কোন ব্যক্তি।”</u>

17. From the above, it is clear that the sale and purchase of a "real estate" as contemplated in the Ain, 2010, is completely a new phenomenon and it has to be understood keeping in mind the provisions of the Ain, 2010. That before the Ain, 2010, there was no law regulating the sale and purchase of a "real estate" is clear from the preamble of the law itself as quoted hereinbefore. And in the context, we can very much also take judicial notice of the practice that prevailed in the country in respect of sale of the apartments/flats by the developers to the prospective buyers before the enactment of the Ain, 2010. Before this law came into being, it was in practice that after negotiation as to the price of an apartment/flat with the developer, booking money used to be paid to the developer who in turn used to give booking slip against such payment along with the payment schedule to make the balance price of the apartment/flat by installments, and of course, in some cases, a written agreement used to be executed between the purchaser and the developer setting the terms of the subsequent payment and that after full payment of the price of the apartment/flat by the prospective buyer/purchaser to the developer sale deed/transfer deed in respect of the apartment used to be executed and registered by the developer in favour of the purchaser/buyer by virtue of the power of attorney given to them by the land owner. And in the Ain, 2010 which came into effect on and from 7-12-2008 (except sections 19-32), the detailed provisions have been made as to the purchase-sale, registration of the sale deed/transfer deed of a "real estate" and handing over of its possession and other relevant matters. And this will be clear if we see sections 8 and 9 thereof which reads as under:

“৮। রিয়েল এস্টেট ক্রয়-বিক্রয়ের শর্তাবলী।–

(১) প্রসপেক্টাসে বা বরাদ্দপত্রে রিয়েল এস্টেট এর বিক্রয়যোগ্য এলাকার বিভাজনসহ যথাযথ ব্যাখ্যা বা বিশ্লেষণ উল্লেখ করিতে হইবে।

(২) রিয়েল এস্টেট উন্নয়ন বা ক্রয় বিক্রয় সংক্রান্ত বিস্তারিত শর্ত, পক্ষদের মধ্যে সম্পাদিত চুক্তিতে উল্লেখ করিতে হইবে।

(৩) কোন ডেভেলপার ক্রেতার সম্মতিক্রমে বরাদ্দকৃত নির্দিষ্ট প্লট বা ফ্ল্যাট পরিবর্তন করিতে পারিবে।

(৪) কোন ডেভেলপার ক্রেতার নিকট হইতে চুক্তিতে উল্লিখিত শর্তের বাহিরে অতিরিক্ত অর্থ গ্রহণ করিতে পারিবে নাঃ

তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, যদি কোন পক্ষ পরবর্তীতে কোন উন্নতমানের সরঞ্জামাদি সংযোজনের প্রস্তাব করিয়া পরস্পর সম্মত হইয়া এই মর্মে সম্পূরক চুক্তি সম্পাদন করিলে এই বিধান কার্যকর হইবে না।

৯। হস্তান্তর দলিল সম্পাদন ও রেজিস্ট্রেশন।–(১) রিয়েল এ্স্টেটের সমুদয় মূল্য পরিশোধের পর ডেভেলপার অনূর্ধ্ব ৩ (তিন) মাসের মধ্যে ক্রেতাকে রিয়েল এস্টেটের দখল হস্তান্তর, দলিল সম্পাদন ও রেজিস্ট্রেশন কার্যাদি সম্পন্ন করিয়া দিবে।

(২) রিয়েল এস্টেট এর দখল হস্তান্তরকালে উহার আয়তন কম বা বেশী হইলে তাহার মূল্য ক্রয়কৃত দর (rate) অনুযায়ী ৩ (তিন) মাসের মধ্যে সমন্বয় করিতে হইবে।

(৩) কোন ডেভেলপার কোন ভূমির মালিকের নিকট হইতে বা পক্ষে আম-মোক্তারনামা দলিল বলে ভূমি প্রাপ্ত হইয়া উক্ত ভূমিতে রিয়েল এস্টেট নির্মাণ এবং তদীয় অংশে প্রাপ্ত রিয়েল এস্টেট ক্রেতাগণের নিকট বিক্রয়ের প্রস্তাব করিলে ভূমির মালিক বা তাহার পক্ষে আম-মোক্তারনামা দলিলে উপ-ধারা (৪) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, এই মর্মে ডেভেলপারকে ক্ষমতা অর্পণ করিতে হইবে যাহাতে ডেভেলপার তাহার অংশে প্রাপ্ত রিয়েল এস্টেট বাবদ দলিল স্বয়ং সম্পাদন করিয়া বিক্রয় বা অন্য কোনভাবে হস্তান্তর করিতে পারে।

(৪) উপ-ধারা (৩) এ বর্ণিত মতে ভূমির মালিক বা তাহার পক্ষে ডেভেলপারকে আম-মোক্তারনামা দলিলের মাধ্যমে দলিল সম্পাদন করিয়া রিয়েল এস্টেট বিক্রয় বা হস্তান্তর ক্ষমতা অর্পণ করা না হইলে, নির্মিত রিয়েল এস্টেট বিক্রয় বা হস্তান্তরযোগ্য হইবার পর ডেভেলপার কর্তৃক লিখিতভাবে অনুদ্র্ধ ১৫(পনের) দিনের মধ্যে ভূমির মালিক বা তাহার পক্ষে ক্রেতার অনুকূলে দলিল সম্পাদন করিয়া দিতে হইবে।

(৫) প্রচলিত অন্য কোন আইনে ভিন্নতর যাহাই থাকুক না কেন, ডেভেলপার কর্তৃক উপ-ধারা (৪) এর অধীন অনুরুদ্ধ হইয়া নির্ধারিত সময়ের মধ্যে ভূমির মালিক বা তাহার পক্ষে দলিল সম্পাদন করা না হইলে, ডেভেলপার স্বয়ং এই ধারার ক্ষমতাবলে তদীয় অংশ এইরূপে ক্রেতার বরাবরে দলিল সম্পাদন করিয়া দিতে পারিবে যেন ডেভেলপার নিজেই উক্ত ভূমি ও রিয়েল এস্টেটের মালিক।”

18. In section 8, thought it has been stated that the detailed terms and conditions of the development of the "real state" and its purchase and sale i.e. the developer and the purchaser /buyer, but it has not been mandated that such agreement must be registered and registration has been spoken of only in case of the sale deed in respect of the "real estate" after the full payment for the same by the buyer/purchaser. In his regard, another section of the Ain, 2010 may be referred to and this is section 10 which reads as follows:

“১০। ভূমি মালিক ও ডেভেলপারের মধ্যে চুক্তি।–

(১) ভূমির মালিক রিয়েল এস্টেট উন্নয়নের লক্ষ্যে ডেভেলপারের সহিত লিখিত দ্বি-পাক্ষিক চুক্তি (Joint Venture Agreement) সম্পাদন করিবেন।”

(২) উপ-ধারা (১) এ উল্লেখিত চুক্তিতে রিয়েল এস্টেট উন্নয়ন বাবদ ডেভেলপারের প্রাপ্ত অংশের পরিমাণ উল্লেখপূর্বক প্রাপ্ত অংশ ডেভেলপারের প্রাপ্ত অংশের পরিমাণ উল্লেখপূর্বক প্রাপ্ত অংশ ডেভেলপারের মনোনীত ক্রেতা বরাবর দলিল সম্পাদন ও রেজিস্ট্রেশন করিয়া দেওয়ার ক্ষমতা প্রদানের লক্ষ্যে ডেভেলপার বরাবর আম-মোক্তারনামা দলিল সম্পাদনের শর্ত উল্লেখসহ ভূমি উন্নয়ন বা নির্মাণ কাজ শুরু ও শেষ করিবার সময় উল্লেখ থাকিবে।

(৩) উপ-ধারা (১) এ উল্লেখিত চুক্তির শর্ত অনুযায়ী রিয়েল এস্টেট উন্নয়ন বা নির্মাণ কাজ শুরু ও শেষ করিতে হইবে।”

19. Sub-section (1) of the section has spoken about a joint venture agreement by the land owner with the developer for the development of the "real estate" and again it has not been mandated that such agreement has to be registered. But in sub-section (2) thereof registration has been spoken about only in case of giving power of attorney to the Developer by the land owner to execute and register the sale deed in favour of the purchaser/buyer by the developer of its portion of the share of the "real estate". So, presently, the law requires that an agreement has to be executed between the parties, i.e. the purchaser and the developer stipulating in detail the terms for the development, purchase-sale of the real estate but registration of such agreement is not necessary. But we do not see any bar to register such agreement for sale of a "real estate", it is the option of the parties. But the trial Court in rejecting the plaint failed to consider the above provisions of the Ain, 2010 and also the subtle difference between the agreement for sale of an immovable property as conceived in the Transfer of Property Act and the agreement for sale of a "real estate", a new concept of immovable property as conceived of in the Ain, 2010 and before too as well as discussed hereinbefore.

20. As stated earlier, in the plaint, nothing was stated about any formal agreement between the plaintiff and the developer for the purchase of the two apartments and the two car parking spaces. It was stated that booking of the two apartments was given by giving booking slip on receipt of Taka 30,00,000 and by giving a payment schedule. It is also very significant to state that the developer issued the impugned letter dated 11-7-2010 to the plaintiff asking him to take back the booking money paid by him earlier after the Ain, 2010 came into effect, so the developer was legally obliged to follow the provisions of the Ain, 2010. And further this law having been enacted after the amendment was brought in the Transfer of Property Act, the Registration Act and the Specific Relief Act vide sections 54A, 17A. and 21A respectively in 2004 and no provision having been made therein making registration of the agreement for sale/purchase of a "real estate" compulsory, it could not be said that no right, title and interest accrued to the plaintiff over the two apartments and the two car parking spaces for non-existence of any registered deed of agreement for the purchase of the two apartments by the plaintiff as held by the trial Court.

21. Another distinguishing feature between the sale of an immovable property as contemplated in section 54A of the Transfer of Property Act, section 21A of the Specific Relief Act and section 17A of the Registration Act and that of a sale of a "real estate" is that in case of a sale of an immovable property as contemplated in those 3 (three) laws, it is the owner of the immovable property who enters into an agreement to sell the same, but in case of sale of a "real estate", it is the developer who sells the "real estate" from his share of the "real estate" to the prospective buyer by virtue of a power of attorney given to it by the land owner. And in all the said 3 (three) sections of the 3 (three) laws, the phraseologies used are "contract for sale of any immovable property" and not the "real estate" a new concept of the immovable property. As already stated hereinbefore, in case of an agreement or contract for sale of a "real estate" registration having not been made compulsory in the Ain, 2010 and this law being a special law enacted specially for the development of the "real estate", its management and the other related matters (আনুষঙ্গিক বিষয়), the provisions of this Ain shall prevail over the provisions of section 54A, 21A and 17A of the Transfer of Property Act, the Specific Relief Act and the Registration Act respectively.

22. In the plaint, it was stated that the developer gave booking for two apartments being

Nos. A-4 and A-5 comprising an area of 1700 square feet of each apartment with two car parking spaces at the basement of the residential building at a price of Taka 4,800 in favour of the plaintiff. It was further stated that booking was given by the developer by giving a booking slip receiving a sum of Taka 30,00,000 (thirty lac) from him on 16-6-2017 as booking money and by giving payment schedule on 19-6-2007 and they (the developer) failed to make any construction and thereby delayed the matter for years together due to the dispute between the co-sharers of the land owners and after removal of the dispute, the developer got approval of the plan for constructing of a 8 (eight) storied residential building only on 30-7-2009 which was communicated to them on 4-10-2009 and thereafter they started the construction work and then demanded excess amount to the plaintiff which he declined to pay and then the developer issued the malafide letter to the plaintiff on 11-7-2010 asking him to take back the money which he deposited three years back showing the flimsy ground that the plaintiff did not make the payment of the installments and also making false statement that they had already sold away the apartments to somebody else. In the plaint, it was further asserted that as per the payment schedule given on 19-6-2007, thatch the plaintiff approached the developer to pay the installments, they did not accept the money saying that the installments would be accepted after the approval of the plan. On these statements of facts, a question arises whether giving booking of the two apartments along with the two car parking spaces on receipt of a sum of Taka 30,000 would amount to a contract and whether on such contract, the plaintiff acquired any right, title and interest in the two apartments/flats and this question cannot be decided without going into the detailed of the facts of the case and the evidence to be produced by the plaintiff at the peremptory hearing of the suit.

23. In the context, section 14 of the Ain, 2010 is also very significant. The section reads as follows:

“১৪। ক্রেতা কর্তৃক এককালীন মূল্য বা কিস্তি পরিশোধে ব্যর্থতা।–(১) ক্রেতা কর্তৃক স্থিরীকৃত সময়ের মধ্যে রিয়েল এস্টেট এর এককালীন মূল্য বা কিস্তির মূল্য পরিশোধে ব্যর্থতার ফলাফল সম্পর্কে প্রসপেক্টাস বা বরাদ্দপত্রে বিশদ উল্লেখ থাকিতে হইবে।

(২) চুক্তিতে বা বরাদ্দপত্রে ভিন্নতর যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, কোন কারণে রিয়েল এস্টেট ক্রেতা এককালীন মূল্য বা কিস্তির অর্থ পরিশোধে ব্যর্থ হইলে ক্রেতাকে, রেজিস্টার্ড ডাকাযোগে, অন্যূন ৬০(ষাট)দিনের পূর্ব নোটিশ প্রদান ব্যতীত তাহার রিয়েল এস্টেট এর বরাদ্দ বাতিল করা যাইবে না।

(৩) উপ-ধারা (২) এ বর্ণিত বরাদ্দ বাতিলের ক্ষেত্রে ক্রেতার জমাকৃত অর্থ বরাদ্দ বাতিল আদেশের পরবর্তী ৩ (তিন) মাসের মধ্যে প্রাপকের হিসাবে প্রদেয় চেকের মাধ্যমে একত্রে ফেরত প্রদান করিতে হইবে।

(৪) উপ-ধারা (২) এ বর্ণিত বিধান অনুযায়ী কোন ক্রেতা বিলম্বে কিস্তির অর্থ পরিশোধ করিতে চাহিলে, দেয় কিস্তির উপর বিলম্বিত সময়ের জন্য কিস্তির অর্থের উপর ১০% হারে সুদ প্রদান সহকারে কিস্তি পরিশোধ করিতে পারিবে।

(৫) উপ-ধারা (৪) এ বর্ণিত বিধান অনুযায়ী ক্রেতা সর্বসাকুল্যে ৩(তিন) বার কিস্তির অর্থ পরিশোধে বিলম্ব করিলে ডেভেলপার সংশ্লিষ্ট ক্রেতার বরাদ্দ বাতিল করিতে পারিবে।”

<u>24. A reading of this section shows that if the purchaser of a "real estate' fails to pay its price at a time or fails to pay the installments, then without giving 60 (sixty) days notice by registered post to the purchaser, no allotment can be cancelled. Sub-section (4) further shows that a purchaser of a "real estate" has the option to pay the installments beyond time by paying interest at the rate of 10% and sub-section (5) shows that the developer shall have the right to cancel the allotment of a real estate if the purchaser fails to pay the installment for three times in total as contemplated in sub-section (4). In the plaint, the plaintiff asserted that his booking of the "real estate" was cancelled without giving him any prior notice. And whether the notice as required by section 14(2) of the Ain, 2010 was given to him or not is basically a question of fact and that cannot be decided without considering the evidence that has to be produced at the peremptory hearing of the suit.</u>

25. The letter cancelling the booking of the two apartment’s shows that the booking of the allotment of the "real estate" was cancelled on the ground that the plaintiff failed to make the payment of installments as per the payment schedule and avoided the request of the developer to pay the installments vide letters dated 4-7-2007 and 4-8-2007. In the plaint, the plaintiff asserted that no such notices were given to him before cancelling the booking of the two apartments and two car parking spaces. In the plaint, it was further asserted that the developer got approval of the plan for constructing the building only on 30-7-2009 which was communicated to them on 4-10-2009, therefore, the question of issuance of the notices for making payment on 4-7-2007 or 4-8-2007 did not arise at all. Whether the plaintiff failed to make the payment as per the payment schedule and whether the developer at all asked him to make the installments is again a question of fact. It is also very interesting to note that in the letter of cancellation of the allotment, it was stated that the two flats booked by the plaintiff had already been transferred to a 3rd person. For all these reasons, we find that the defendants' application for rejection of the plaint did not deserve any consideration.

26. The next question to be decided in this petition is whether the plaintiff filed the suit for specific performance of the contract simpliciter, as found by the trial Court.
