If on a reading of the plaint and the prayers made therein, it is found that the plaintiff filed the suit for specific performance of contract simpliciter, then of course, the suit could not be proceeded with in view of the provisions of section 54A of the Transfer of Property Act read with section 17 A of the Registration Act and section 21A of the Specific Relief Act; the three sections of the said three laws read as follows:

"54A. Contract for sale to be registered etc: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Act or any other law for the time being in force, a contract for sale of any immovable property can be made only by an instrument in writing and registered under the Registration Act-1908, whether or not the transferee has taken possession of the property or any part thereof.

27. In a contract for sale of immovable property, a time, to be effective from the date of registration, shall be mentioned for execution and registration of the instrument of sale and if no time is mentioned, six months shall be deemed to be the time.

17A. Registration of contract for sale etc:

(1) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Act or any other law for the time being in force, a contract for sale of any immovable property shall be in writing, executed by the parties thereto and registered.

(2) A contract for sale referred-to in sub-section (1) shall be presented for registration within thirty days from the date of execution of the contract and the provisions regarding registration of instruments shall apply.

21A. Unregistered contract for sale not specifically enforceable—Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Act or any other law for the time being in force, no contract for sale of any immovable property can be specifically enforced unless—

(a) the contract is in writing and registered under the Registration Act-1908, whether or not the transferee has taken possession of the property or any part thereof; and

(b) the balance amount of the consideration of the contract is deposited in the court at the time of filing the suit for specific performance of contract."

<u>28. Keeping in view the above provisions of law, if we now look at the prayers made in the plaint as quoted hereinbefore, it would prima facie contract simpliciter, as contemplated in section 12 of the Specific Relief Act. The plaintiff made as many as five prayers. Of these five prayers, prayers (a) and (b) are for declaration that allotment of the two apartments in the name of the plaintiff as described in the schedule to the plaint pursuant to the booking money received by the principal-defendants dated 16-6-2007 was lawful and still subsists and "thereby creates" legal obligation on the principal-defendants to hand over the apartment in favour of the plaintiff and for declaration that the impugned letter issued by principal-defendant No.1 under the signature of principle-defendant No.3 dated 11-7-2010 for taking back the booking money was illegal, null and void, fraudulent, without any lawful authority and not binding upon the plaintiff respectively. By no imagination, the second declaration can be treated or construed as one for specific performance of contract and such declaration clearly attracts the provisions of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. So far as the first declaration is concerned, it appears to us a bit debatable, i.e. straightway, it cannot be said either it comes within the periphery of a suit for specific performance of contract as provided in section 12 of the Specific Relief Act or attracts the mischief of section 42 thereof and this debate can only be resolved on a full scale hearing of the suit and on assessment of the evidence to be produced by the parties at the trial.</u>

29. So far as prayer (c) is concerned, it is also very difficult to straightway come to a decision that the said prayer does not come within the purview of section 55 of the Specific Relief Act. It is better to quote the said section:

"55. Mandatory injunction—When, to prevent the breach of an obligation, it is necessary to compel the performance of certain acts which the Court is capable of enforcing, the Court may, in its discretion, grant an injunction to prevent the breach complained of, and also to compel performance of the requisite acts."

<u>30. A reading of the section shows that a Court of law can give mandatory injunction if it is necessary to compel the performance of certain acts which the Court is capable of enforcing and also to compel performance of the requisite acts to prevent the breach of an obligation by the defendant(s) and to get a relief in a suit as in the instant case, the plaintiff must satisfy the Court by producing evidence that the defendants had an obligation to him which they were breaching. So, it cannot be said that the relief as made in prayer (c) in the plaint was barred under any of the clauses of rule 11 of Order VII of the Code.</u>

31. For the discussions made hereinabove, we do not find any illegality in the ultimate decision of the High Court Division that the plaint could not be rejected under any of the provisions of Order VII, rule 11 of the Code, though it passed the judgment in a slipshod manner without considering the relevant provisions of the laws along with the averment made in the plaint as discussed hereinabove.

We find no merit in the petition and the same is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1132 of 2016
lawyer:
Abdul Wadud Bhuiya, Senior Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman. Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners 
Quamrul Hoque Siddique, Advocate instructed by Haridas Paul, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent Nos.1(a), 4(b), 4(d), 5-6, 7(a)-7(d), 8, 9(a), 9(c)-9(d) & 17. 
None Represented ------ Respondent Nos.1 (b)-1(g), 2-3, 4(a), 4(c), 4(e), 7(e)-7(h), 9(b), 9(e), 10-16 & 18-244.
parties:
Masum Billah (Md.) and another ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Md. Saidur Rahman and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 12th January, 2016 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.6086 of 2002)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J: This civil petition for leave to appeal has been filed by 2 (two) of the defendants, namely, Md. Masum Billah, son of late Yakub Ali and Abul Hashem, son of Munshi Abdul Gani (number of the defendants are not available from the record) against the judgment and order dated the 12th day of January, 2016 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.6086 of 2002 making the Rule absolute.

2. Facts necessary to dispose this petition are that predecessor-interest of respondent Nos. 1(a)-1(g), respondent Nos. 2 and 3, predecessor-in-interest of respondent Nos. 4(a)-4(e), respondent Nos. 5 and 6, predecessor-in-interest of respondent Nos. 7(a)-7(h), respondents No.8, predecessor-in-interest of respondent Nos.9(a)- 9(e) and respondent Nos. 10-18 herein as the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 164 of 1973 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Court No.2, Barisal for partition of the suit land. Subsequently, the suit having been transferred to the Court of Assistant Judge, Banaripara, Barisal was renumbered as Title Suit No. 169 of 1984.

3. The suit was decreed on 30-6-1987 in preliminary form against the contesting defendants as well as the other non-contesting defendants. Against the said decree, defendant No. 176 filed an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the said decree. The application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No.43 of 1989. This miscellaneous case was allowed by the learned Assistant Judge by his order dated 18-1-1995 in the following terms:

অতএব,

হুকুম হইল যে,

অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি তরপছানীদের বিরুদ্ধে একতরফা সূত্রে ১,০০০ টাকা খরচায় মঞ্জুর করা হইল। বিগত ইং ৩০-৬-৮৭ তারিখের প্রচারিত ডিক্রী রদ ও রহিতান্তে মূল মোকদ্দমা উহার পূর্বের নম্বরে ও ফাইলে পূর্বের নম্বরে ও ফাইলে পূনর্বহাল করা হইল।”

4. Thus, it is clear that the decree passed in the suit was set aside as a whole. Therefore, the decree passed in the suit on 30-8-1987 became non-existent. It further appears that after the suit was restored to its original file and number, the same was contested by defendant Nos. 3 and 15 by filing written statement and on conclusion of trial, the learned Senior Assistant Judge by his judgment and decree dated 28-5-1998 dismissed the suit. Against the judgment and decree of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No. 130 of 1998 before the District Judge, Barisal. The learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Barisal having heard the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 23-5-2002 dismissed the appeal and thus affirmed the judgment and decree of the learned Assistant Judge. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the learned Additional District Judge, the plaintiffs filed the above mentioned civil revision before the High Court Division. A Single Bench by the impugned judgment and order made the Rule absolute and set aside the judgment and decree complained of; hence this petition for leave to appeal.

5. Heard Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiya, learned Counsel for the petitioners and Mr. Quamrul Hoque Siddique, learned Counsel who entered caveat on behalf of respondent Nos. 1(a), 4(b), 4(d), 5-6, 7(a)- 7(d), 8, 9(a), 9(c)-9(d) and 178.

6. From the revision application, it is prima facie clear that the judgment and decree impugned therein was the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court passed in Title Appeal No. 130 of 1998 affirming those dated 28-5-1998 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Bainapatra in the suit being Title Suit No. 169 of 1984 after the same had been restored to its original file and number. But the High Court Division without considering the legal flaws in the judgment of the Courts below passed in the suit and in the appeal respectively, devoted its whole energy on the legality of the order passed in Miscellaneous Case No.43 of 1989 setting aside the decree passed on 30-6-1987, as if it were a revision preferred against the order allowing the said miscellaneous case. We consider it better to quote the entire findings of the High Court Division which is as under:

"I have considered the question raised that whether, after final decree having been executed on satisfaction, the decree of a partition suit can be set aside by laying application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. This suit was for partition in which it is to be settled (sic) whether a party has saham or share of land. It appears out of 202 defendants, at the instance of single defendant, entire decree has been set aside. Partition suit is different from other suits. In partition suit share of land was allowed to plaintiff or defendant as per their individual saham. In setting aside any exparte decree, the applicant must disclose (sic) the impugned exparte decree how he is effected ie whether (sic) his share of land crept up from his saham has been allotted to other. Omnibus statement for setting aside exparte decree does not hold good. It can be set aside in respect of saham of which applicant/ defendant is entitled. It appears that defendant No. 176 stated that entire judgment was obtained by practicing fraud. This is not correct as when other defendants appeared one cannot say that entire judgment was obtained by practicing fraud. It is to be borne in mind that defendant Nos. 170-2002 were impleaded by order dated 19-2-1976.

Now, the question put forward by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that if decree having been executed to the satisfaction of all the appeared defendants whether it can be set aside under Order IX rule 13 of the code of civil procedure.

In the case of Venkata Reddy vs Pothi, AIR 1963 (SC) 992 it is held where no appeal has been filed against the preliminary decree, the rights determined therein become final and conclusive and cannot be questioned in the final decree.

In the case of Sadar uddin vs Jaharlal, AIR 1942 Cal-153, it is held when no appeal is preferred against the final decree and only the preliminary decree is appealed against, but a copy of the final decree is placed on record of the appeal, it is the duty of the appellate court in dealing with the appeal to give necessary' and consequential directions regarding final decree.

It appears that suit was decreed and decree was satisfied by giving possession of the respective parties, final decree was drawn and possession of the parties have been delivered by advocate commissioner, in such situation, an application under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is incompetent, an appeal can be taken. After final decree being satisfied by giving possession to individual saham holder it ended finally, in such a situation application under order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is totally incompetent and is entertaining the application courts below totally suffer from corum-nonjudice. I find substance in this rule."

7. In the context, it is necessary to bring on record a very broad admitted fact that the plaintiffs did not move the higher Court against the order allowing the miscellaneous case, rather they very much participated in the peremptory hearing of the suit and produced evidence in support of their case after restoration to its file and number and then they having lost in the suit, filed appeal against the decree of the trial Court. Since the plaintiffs accepted the order passed in the miscellaneous case and participated in the hearing of the suit, they could not challenge the propriety or the correctness of the order passed in the miscellaneous case in any manner whatsoever in a proceeding which arose out of the decree passed in the suit. Unfortunately, the High Court Division failed to comprehend this simple factual and legal aspect of the case. In the context, we consider it necessary to refer to the finding of the learned Senior Assistant Judge in allowing the miscellaneous case which reads as follows;

“ধার্য্য তাং সরকারী ছুটি থাকায় অদ্য নথি মজহর পক্ষের বিগত ইং ১৪-১১-৯৫ তারিখের একতরফা জবানবন্দীর আলোকে আদেশের জন্য পেশ করা হয়।

ছানীর দরখাস্ত ও নথি পর্যালোচনা করিয়া দেখিলাম। অত্র মোকদ্দমায় বিবাদী পক্ষের প্রতি মূল মোকদ্দমার সমন জারীর বিবরন সন্তোষজনক নহে বিধায় অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি মঞ্জুর যোগ্য”

8. From the above, it is clear that the summons of the suit was not served upon defendant No. 176 who filed the miscellaneous case for setting aside the decree passed in the suit and the trial Court rightly allowed the same.

<u>9. From the judgment of the High Court Division, it is apparent that it failed to consider the very fundamental fact that the decree which was passed earlier in the suit did not exist, the moment the same was set aside in the miscellaneous case. The High Court Division also failed to consider that mere passing of a final decree and its execution thereof shall not debar a defendant to file an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code if, in fact, summons were not served upon him and he was affected by the very preliminary decree. The High Court Division was also wrong in relying upon the principle of law laid down in the cases of Ven Kata Reddy (Supra) and Sadaruddin (Supra) in passing the impugned judgment and order, as the facts and circumstances of the instant case were completely different and distinct from those eases.</u>

<u>10. The High Court Division was also oblivious of the provisions of section 144 of the Code which clearly entitles a party to pray for restoration of possession even if the possession is delivered pursuant to a decree passed in a suit. It also failed to consider that the preliminary decree having been set aside, the suit was heard afresh and the parties participated in the hearing and produced evidence and then the suit having been disposed of on merit, there was no bar to pass afresh final decree and, as such, the High Court Division was obliged to dispose of the revision on merit in the context of the judgment and decree impugned before it, but it did not and thereby committed serious error of law in passing the impugned judgment and order and, as such, the same cannot be sustained.</u>

11. In view of the above, we find no other alternative but to send the revision back to the High Court Division for hearing afresh and for disposal in accordance with law on the basis of the evidence on record. Accordingly, this petition is disposed of in the following terms:

The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is set aside. The revision is sent back to the High Court Division for hearing afresh and for disposal on merit in accordance with law considering the evidence.

If so advised, the parties may mention the revision before the competent Bench for early hearing and, if mentioned, the concerned Bench shall hear the same on priority basis.

End.

lawyer:
Md. Solaiman Hossain, Advocate ------ For the Plaintiff. 
Ashok Kumar Biswas, Advocate ------ For the Defendant.
parties:
Sils Reza S Adhikaree, represented by 
his Attorney Elder Michael A Shah ------Plaintiff
Vs.
Gloria Samadder and anothers ------Defendant
full_judgment:
Syed Refaat Ahmed J: This divorce suit is being disposed of against the backdrop of a prayer for decree of judicial separation in terms of section 22 of The Divorce Act, 1869 ("the Act"). The suit resulted in a judgment and Order of 16-9-2014 by which, however, a Decree Nisi for dissolution of marriage was issued under section 16 of the Act. That Decree Nisi drew necessarily on the provisions of section 10 of the Act as is wholly contrary in its scope, nature, applicability and prescription to section 22. While section 10 endorses dissolution of marriage at the behest of either party on specific grounds shown, section 22 endorses the possibility of seeking judicial separation short of an absolute dissolution of marriage on limited grounds of adultery, or cruelty, or desertion. It is also contemplated that a decree for judicial separation shall have the effect of a "divorce a mensa et torn". The decree of "divorce a mensa et toro" (from bed and board) remains in itself a largely rare, if not obsolete, form of a divorce order which does not end the marriage but allows parties to reside separately. Under section 22 of the Act a decree of judicial separation has the effect of a "divorce a mensa et toro" by which the marriage bond remains technically unbroken but the parties pray for a legal or judicially sanctioned separation.

<u>2. A "divorce a mensa et toro", therefore, rises in the context of a marriage as is just and lawful ab-initio and the law remains otherwise averse to dissolving it but for some supervening cause. Thus, for example, the court may decide it to be improper or impossible for the parties to live together should, for example, instances of intolerable ill temper and adultery be cited. Such a decree entitles the parties, although still married, to live apart without being guilty of desertion. An entitlement also arises in such cases for the wife to be supported by her husband while so living apart. An essential consequence significantly of a decree of judicial separation akin to "a divorce a mensa et toro" is that such a decree does not automatically lead to a divorce. The prospects are therefore, always open for a couple to eventually reconcile. Should, however, reconciliation not be possible, it would be open to the couple to proceed with a dissolution of marriage upon divorce proceedings being initiated under the Act explicitly to that end.</u>

3. In the course of this suit proceedings this Court has been given to understand by the parties that the avenue available under section 22 was pursued by the plaintiff Silas Reza S. Adhikaree to obtain a decree of judicial separation under circumstances where no entitlement accrued to him under section 10 of the Act for outright dissolution of marriage. It has been impressed upon this Court by both parties that notwithstanding such formal invocation of a section 22 process the parties are agreed on their marriage having irretrievably broken down meriting otherwise a decree absolute of divorce.

4. It is noted that the Decree Nisi of 16-9-2014, as issued by a predecessor presiding Judge, apparently seeks to accommodate such position adopted by the parties anticipating, thereby, a section 16 decree absolute for dissolution of marriage. The Order of 16-9-2014 issuing the Decree Nisi reflects a prima facie satisfaction that even given the concept of an irretrievable breakdown of marriage not being specifically recognized under the Act, and the absence in the facts of aggravated grounds for dissolution of marriage outright as contemplated in section 10, the parties have nevertheless agreed on their inability and unwillingness to continue as a married couple. This, therefore, entitles this Court to deal with the parties' predicament in a manner as justice may demand. That notion of ensuring justice inherent in section 16 of the Act appears to have been the intent behind the Decree Nisi issued by this Court on 16-9-2014. Indeed, the plaintiffs supplementary-affidavit of 2-3-2016 draws on such inherent power of this Court to do real and substantial justice under section 16 and prays additionally for a decree absolute of divorce to be made under section 16 read with section 22 of the Act.

5. The facts of this case, as extensively recorded in the judgment and order of 16-9-2014, speak of a marriage duly solemnized on 30-12-2001 by the Bishop of Dhaka between the plaintiff non-resident Bangladeshi living and working in Italy and the defendant Ms. Gloria Samadder. Ms Samadder having joined her husband in Italy and set up home there between 26-10-2003 to 11-7-2010 nevertheless returned thereafter to Bangladesh with a female child born in Italy on 8-1-2004.

6. Differences of opinion as well as of cultural orientation are generally cited by both parties as contributing to their relationship souring, and irretrievably so. Indeed, the defendant herself in her counter-affidavit of 9-3-2015 cites enduring verbal abuse and psychological torture by her husband. It is against this backdrop that the parties executed on 2-2-2012 a deed for separation (Annexure-'B') by which both recognized the other's freedom to live separately without exercising control in any way and significantly refraining from bringing any suit for restoration of conjugal rights. Furthermore, the deed specifically provided for alimony or maintenance as well as child support. Accordingly, the plaintiff agreed to pay the defendant Taka 5,00,000 alimony as well as.

"a reasonable amount as per his financial ability for maintenance and education cost of the daughter regularly until she attains the age of majority."

7. It was agreed that such monthly payment will be "at least Taka 10,000.

8. The initial response of the defendant to the Decree Nisi, as reflected in the counter-affidavit of 9-3-2015, has been to dispute the availability to the Plaintiff of the option of an outright dissolution of marriage. Ms. Samadder has indeed contended she entered into and executed the deed of separation of 2-2-2012 under "compulsion" without, however, elaborating to this court's satisfaction the nature and extent of such compulsion. The counter-affidavit itself read with a further application for alimony and maintenance etc. under sections 37 and 42 of the Act, however, dwell on Ms. Samadder being financially short-changed by an unfavourable financial settlement under the deed of 2012. Citing the plaintiff’s reportedly high earnings in Italy and her own efforts here in Bangladesh to make ends meet as a part-time teacher, the Defendant Gloria Samadder now seeks a judicial intervention for increased alimony for herself and sufficient financial support for her daughter until the latter gets married. It is in that context that an additional alimony of Taka 13,00,000 is sought along with an enhanced child support of Taka 25,000 per month.

9. The plaintiff in response has satisfied this Court of good faith compliance with the terms of the Deed of 2012 of payment of Taka 5,00,000 as alimony with acknowledged receipt by the defendant and of regular monthly payments of Taka 10,000 child support as also acknowledge by the defendant. Furthermore, an affidavit of 13-9-2015 depicts the plaintiff as being financially strapped given the recent economic downturn and recession in Europe and attest to the plaintiff being on contract leave for a year and residing in Bangladesh during that time. It is noted that the Plaintiff has since returned to his place of employment in Italy. These grounds are cited to counter the defendant's claim to additional alimony and monthly child support payments at an enhanced rate. It is also emphatically argued that given his due compliance with the deed of 2-12-2012 the defendant's enhanced claim is unjustified and may, therefore, not receive favourable consideration by this Court.

<u>10. The facts as above noted do indeed paint a picture for this Court of the parties mutually agreeing initially on living separately but always of intent never in fact to reconcile and continue with the marriage at any point in time in the future. A perusal of the deed of 2-12-2012 satisfies this Court of such intent of the parties. There is nothing on record that convinces this Court that the defendant Ms. Samadder may have been induced or somehow being compelled to enter into that mutual agreement of 2-12-2012 against her free will and to the prejudice of her interests. These facts and circumstances evidently convinced this Court on 16-9-2014 to issue a Decree Nisi exceptionally as per the provisions of section 16 of the Act notwithstanding the plaintiff initial filing of this suit under section 22 of the Act. Drawing further upon this Court's explicit authority under section 16 of the Act to ensure that justice is served in the facts and circumstances this Court finds no reason why a decree absolute of divorce may now not ensue. The learned advocate for the plaintiff Mr. Md Solaiman Hossain and that for the defendant Mr. Ashok Kumar Biswas remain in agreement that this should be the most reasonable outcome of these proceedings. That said, and as always has been this Court's primary concern throughout, this Court deems it necessary to invoke its authority under section 37 of the Act to declare this marriage to be dissolved but conditional upon certain beneficial terms recognized in favour of the parties daughter Samantha Hridi Adhikaree.</u>

11. Accordingly, it is, hereby, ordered that (a) the plaintiff shall make a monthly payment of Taka 25,000 favouring Samantha Hridi Adhikaree up until such date that she attains the age of majority; and (b) no impediments shall be placed by either parent for Samantha Hridi Adhikaree to gain Italian citizenship should she at any point in time before she reaches the age of 18 request for the same as per "Citizenship Rules on gaining Italian nationality" brought on record under Annexure-'H' of the plaintiffs counter-affidavit dated 13-9-2015. It shall further be incumbent upon the parties to execute a proper instrument to that effect recording the facts of the Decree Nisi of 16-9-2014 and the decree absolute of today's date and recording the terms favouring Samantha Hridi Adhikaree no later than 8 (eight) weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and order and thereafter to file, jointly or separately, an Affidavit-in-Compliance within 1 (one) week of such execution of a proper instrument. The respondent's application for alimony and maintenance etc. is to be treated as disposed of as hereinabove.

12. In view of the above, this Court fined no reason why the Decree Nisi of 16-9-2014 should not be made absolute subject only to the observations and condition in the term above.

13. Accordingly, the said Decree Nisi made absolute in the terms above.

Communicate this order at once.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 120 of 2013
lawyer:
Aminul Haque, Advocate instructed by Madhu Malati Chowdhury Barua, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner. 
Nurul Islam Chowdhury, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent No. 1
None Represented ------ Respondent No. 2.
parties:
Sharifullah (Md.) and another’s ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Md. Tafazzal Hossain and another ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 19th day of April, 2012 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 561 of 1999)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J: The delay of 15 days in filing the petition is condoned.

2. This petition for leave to appeal has been filed against the judgment and order dated 19-4-2012 passed by a learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.561 of 1999 making the Rule absolute with some direction.

3. Short facts necessary to dispose this petition are that respondent No.1 as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No.284 of 1983 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka for partition of the suit land. Subsequently the suit being transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka was renumbered as Title Suit No.270 of 1985 and then again it was renumbered as Title Suit No.41 of 1992 on being transferred to the Court of Artha Rin Adalat and Subordinate Judge, Dhaka.

4. The suit was decreed exparte on 2-8-1993 against the defendant-petitioner herein and respondent No.2. The defendant-petitioner along with the other defendant (respondent No.2, herein) filed an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) for setting aside the ex-parte decree. The application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No.27of 1994.

5. Respondent No.1 as the plaintiff filed written objection to contest the miscellaneous case. The case being ready for peremptory hearing, hearing commenced and after examination of the defendant-petitioner (in the miscellaneous case), the plaintiff-opposite party (in the miscellaneous case) was examined as OPW 1 on 19-11-1998. Then on 17-1-1999 i.e. after almost two months, he (the plaintiff-opposite party) filed an application under sections 151 and 152 of the Code for correction of his depositions by expunging some portions of his statement in cross examination. The trial Court by its order of the same date (17-1-1999) rejected the prayer. Challenging this order the plaintiff filed the above mentioned civil revision before the High Court Division. A learned Judge of the Single Bench by the impugned judgment and order made the Rule absolute directing the trial Court "to correct the deposition and cross examination of the OPW and to dispose of the case within 4(four) months from the date of receipts of this judgment and order in accordance with law "; hence this petition of leave to appeal.

6. Heard Mr. Aminul Haque, learned Counsel for the petitioner and Mr. Nurul Islam Chowdhury, learned Advocate-on-Record who entered caveat on behalf of plaintiff-respondent No. 1.

<u>7. We have considered the provisions of Order XVIII of the Code and sections 137 and 138 of the Evidence Act. These provisions of the respective law have dealt with the hearing of the suit and examination of witnesses. From a reading of these provisions of laws it appears to us that a witness is not entitled to correct his deposition after putting his signature in the deposition sheet and if such a recourse is allowed to be practiced by a witness, then the whole purpose of cross examination shall be frustrated and in the process the cross examination shall become a mockery. But the High Court Division totally failed to consider the above mentioned provisions of the laws and also the impact of such a recourse resorted to by the plaintiff-opposite party and it, in a very casual manner, allowed the prayer of the plaintiff-opposite party. So, the High Court Division committed an apparent error in making the Rule absolute with the direction as quoted hereinbefore, and as such, the impugned judgment and order cannot be sustained and that must be set aside. Since we have heard the learned Counsel for the petitioner and the learned Advocate-on-Record for plaintiff-respondent No.1, we are inclined to interfere with the impugned judgment and order in a summary manner without giving any leave, as if leave is granted it would cause delay in the disposal of the miscellaneous case, the case being of the year 1994. Accordingly, this petition is disposed of in the following terms:</u>

8. The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is set aside and that of the trial Court is restored.

End.

lawyer:
AF Hassan Ariff Senior Advocate with Ashik Al jalil Advocate ----- For the Petitioners. 
Fida M Kamal Senior Advocate and Kamal-ul-Alam Senior Advocate with Md Arifur Rahman, Advocate ----- For the Opposite-Parties.
parties:
Nazrul Islam (Md) and another ----- Petitioners
VS
Samsun Nahan Azim and others ----- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
At the instance of the plaintiffs Leave was granted under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure against the judgment and order dated 1-4-2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka discharging the Rule in Civil Revision No. 226 of 2009 and affirming the judgment and order dated 22-6-2009 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 77 of 2007 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure allowing the Miscellaneous Case by which the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 10-1-2005 passed in Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 was set aside and the above suit was restored to its original file and number.

2. The facts relevant for disposal of Rule are that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 for Specific Performance of Contract impleading the defendant-opposite-parties and obtained an ex-parte decree on 11-3-1987. Subsequently, the defendant No. 2 Government filed Miscellaneous Case No. 46 of 1987 under order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex-parte decree, which was rejected on 15-4-1990. Against the dismissal order, the defendant No. 2 Government filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 158 of 1990 which was allowed by order dated 3-4-1993 and set aside the ex-parte decree dated 11-3-1987. Thereafter Mrs Shamsun Nahar Azim opposite-party No. 1 filed an application on 15-8-1993 under Order I, rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure for addition of party and by order dated 18-6-1995 she was added/ impleaded as defendant No. 3 in the suit. In the meantime the petitioners preferred Civil Revision No. 1739 of 1993 before the Hon'ble High Court Division and same was dismissed. Then the petitioners filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1001 of 1997 in the Appellate Division, Supreme Court of Bangladesh which was also dismissed on 24-6-2001. Thereafter, the record of the Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 was received back to the trial court on 2-7-2003 but the learned Advocate of the Added defendant No. 3.was not found in court to intimate the date of hearing of the suit. So, the court passed order to serve the notice upon the defendants through process server. Although the notice were duly served upon the defendant as per report of the process server but the defendant-opposite-party did not appear to contest the suit, ultimately the suit was again decreed ex-parte on 10-1-2005.

3. The defendant No. 3 opposite-party No. 1 herein appears to have filed an application under Order IX, rule 13 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 22-8-2007 for setting aside the ex-parte decree and the same was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 77 of 2007 stating, inter alia, that the present-petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 on 24-11-1984 in the First Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Dhaka for specific performance of contract. The suit property was enlisted as Abandoned property within the meaning of PO 16 of 1972; the applicant, Shamsun Nahar is the wife of Late Captain Anwarul Azim, who sacrificed his life for the sake of independence of Bangladesh in the Liberation war in 1971. In order to pay tribute and homage to her husband's sacrifice, the government allotted the suit abandoned property to petitioner's family by allotment Letter dated 17-12-1974 and delivered possession. Till then petitioner has been in possession of the suit property by paying electricity, gas, water charge and monthly rent to the government. That the learned trial court passed an order on 9-5-2004 for issuing summons upon the defendant No. 3-opposite-party No. 1 after the case record of the suit was received back by the trial court on 2-7-2003 and the defendant No. 3 had no scope to know the progress of the suit. That the summons of the suit was not served upon her on 25-10-2004 and she did not receipt any notice from the court. The process server in collusion with the plaintiffs submitted his report that the summons were duly served upon the defendant No. 3. In the service return the defendant No. 3 or her representative put any signature. Defendant No. 3 as opposite-party No. 1 recently came to know about the ex-parte decree. Then she went to the court and inquired about the matter through her learned Advocate and being confirmed applied for certified copy of the judgment and obtained certified copy on 4-7-2007. Since the defendant had no knowledge about the ex-parte decree, there has been a delay of 944 days in filing this Miscellaneous Case, which may kindly be condoned. At the time of filling of the application, the defendant No. 3 also filed an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908.

4. The Plaintiffs-opposite-parties contested the said Miscellaneous case by filling written objection, denying the allegations of non-service of summons/notice upon the defendant No. 3 and stating further that the notice of the suit were duly served upon the defendants; that the Miscellaneous case is barred by limitation; that the suit was decreed ex-parte on 10-1-2005. The opposite-party No. 1 was added as defendant No. 3 in Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 on 18-6-1995 and aware of the proceeding of the suit and present Miscellaneous case was filed after eighteen months of the ex-parte decree which is not sustainable in law and filed just to harass the opposite-parties.

5. In support of her case, the petitioner-defendant No. 3 examined herself as PW 1. The

plaintiffs-opposite-parties examined two OPW's including OPW No. 2, process server, Abdur Rahman, who served the summons in the suit.

6. The learned Joint District Judge allowed the Miscellaneous case by judgment and order dated 12-6-2009 and restored the suit to its original file and number on the findings that the summons of Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 was not served upon the defendant No. 3 and the defendant No. 3 as petitioner filed the present Miscellaneous Case within 30 days after obtaining the certified copy of the impugned judgment and decree. There was a fraud upon the defendant-petitioner in respect of service of summons by the court through process server. The process server did not serve the summons in presence of Mokabila witnesses. Consequently, the defendant had no knowledge about the proceedings of Title Suit No. 375 of 1984.

7. Against the judgment and order dated 22-6-2009, the plaintiffs-petitioners filed Civil Revision No. 226 of 2009 before the District Judge, Dhaka under section 115(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, which was on transfer heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka who by judgment and order dated 1-4-2010 discharged the Rule and affirming the order of the trial court allowing the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by the defendant No. 3.

8. The Plaintiffs-petitioners being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 1-4-2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka discharging the Civil Revision No. 226 of 2009 filed this revision and obtained the present Rule.

9. Mr AF Hassan Ariff, the learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr Ashik Al Jalil, advocate for the plaintiffs-petitioners submits that the defendant No. 3 came to the court with unclean hands and the application is hopelessly barred by 944 days and the defendant could not explain the delay properly. He further submits that the application was not filed within 30 days from the date of obtaining certified copy, same was filed after 18 days, which was beyond 30 days fixed under Article 164 of the Limitation Act in as much as a valuable right has been acquired by the plaintiffs firmly which cannot be taken away lightly by violating the requirement of law as fixed in Article 164 of the Limitation Act. Moreover the learned trial court erred in law in misreading and misconstruing the prayer for condonation in the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He finally submit that both the courts below erred in law in allowing the Miscellaneous case and dismissing the revisional application and the defendant No. 3 being an allotee/lessee under the government has no locus-standi to file the Miscellaneous case for setting aside the ex-parte decree.

10. In support of his submissions learned Senior Advocate referred to a decision reported in 25 DLR 254.

11. In this revisional application Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr Najmul Karim, Advocate for the defendant No. 3 opposite-party No. 1. Subsequently Mr Fida M Kamal, learned Senior Advocate also appears in this case and made his submissions.

12. Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Advo-cate submits that both the courts below concurrently found that summons/notice upon the defendant No. 3 was not served properly in accordance with law. He further submits that the trial court held that the impugned ex-parte decree passed in Title Suite No. 375 of 1984 was obtained without service of summons upon the defendant No. 3 for that reason she was prevented from appearing in the suit. Thus the learned Joint District Judge rightly condoned the delay and set aside the ex-parte decree. In this connection learned Advocate refers decisions reported in 35 DLR (AD) 162 and 12 BLC (AD) 75.

13. The learned Advocate submits that the opposite-party No. 1 filed application for being added as defendant No. 3 in the Title Suit on 15-8-1993 but this order was not signed by the presiding Judge and Civil Revision No. 1739 of 1993 was filed by the plaintiffs-petitioners before the Hon'ble High Court Division, without impleading defendant No. 3, as the plaint was not amended impleading defendant No. 3 and the same was dismissed and Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1001 of 1997 was also dismissed. Then the case record of Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 was received back by the trial court on 2-7-2003 and plaintiff by order dated 18-6-1995 was directed to amend the plaint adding Shamsun Nahar as defendant No. 3, but the plaint was not amended accordingly.

14. He also submits that thereafter the learned trial court passed gkrt order on 9-5-2004 to intimate the order dated 18-6-1995 to the learned Advocate for defendant No. 3. Since no intimation was given as he could not be found, learned trial court by order dated 15-9-2004 issued notice through court upon defendant No. 3 and summons was shown to have been served by order dated 15-10-2004 and subsequently suit was decreed ex-parte for second time on 10-1-2005. Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, by referring those orders and service return of the process server submits that the address of the defendant No. 3 mentioned in the plaint and the address of the notice are not same, further PW 1, Shamsun Nahar deposed that no notice was served on her on 15-10-2004 and OPW 2, process server admitted that the Mokabila witnesses were declined to put their signature in the summons, inspite that he wrote the names of two persons as Mokabila witness which clearly proved that the defendant No. 3 was not aware about the ex-parte decree. He further submits that when notice was 'not served upon the defendant No. 3 properly, the ex-parte decree is liable to be set aside. He submits that there was no earthly reason for the opposite-party not to contest the Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 if she had received the summons, particularly in view, of the fact that on her prayer she was added as Defendant No. 3 in the suit on 18-6-1995.

15. He finally submits that both the courts below concurrently found that the summons were not properly served by the process-server and for that reason she was prevented from appearing in the suit and delay was rightly condoned from the date of impugned ex-parte decree dated 10-1-2005. Thus the High Court Division as a Second Revisional Court cannot interfere the findings of the court 'below and prayed for discharge of the Rule. In support of his contention he also referred decisions reported in 1 MLR (AD) 210 and 17 BLD (AD) 295.

16. Mr Fida M Kamal, Senior Advocate subsequently appeared on behalf of the opposite-party No. 1 and submits that the suit was decree ex-parte for the first time on 11-3-1987 and after passing of the ex-parte deciee the plaintiff amended the schedule of the plaint by filing an application on 2-4-1987 under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure by practicing fraud upon the court. He further submits that even if the application seeking setting aside ex-parte decree is barred by the limitation when ex-parte decree is challenge on the ground of fraud/collusion was found on record then decree could not be sustained.

17. In support of his submission Mr Fida M Kamal, learned Advocate cited a case of Government of Bangladesh vs Mashiur Rahman reported in 50 DLR (AD) 205.

18. I have heard the submissions of the learned Advocate of both the parties, thoroughly examined the case record, counter affidavit and the documents exhibited in the miscellaneous case and the deposition of the PW and OPW's.

19. It appears that earlier Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 was decreed ex-parte on 11-3-1987. Against the ex-parte judgment and decree, defendant No. 1, Government filed Miscellaneous Case No. 46 of 1987 under Order IX, rule 13 and the same was dismissed by the judgment and order dated 15-8-1990. Against the dismissal order, defendant No. 1 filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 158 of 1990 before the District Judge, Dhaka and same was allowed by the judgment and order dated 3-4-1993 and the suit was restored to its original file and number. Thereafter on the prayer of the present opposite-party No. 1 Shamsun Nahar Azim on 15-8-1993 under Order 1, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court by Order No.74 dated 18-6-1995 added her as defendant No. 3 in the suit but the plaintiffs did not take any step to amend the suit register, even the order dated 18-6-1995 was not signed by the concerned judge till 9-5-2004 as evident from Order No. 91 dated 21-4-2004 and Order No. 92 dated 9-5-2004.

20. For better appreciation and proper adjudication of the matter the Order No. 60 dated 15-8-1993, Order No. 74 dated 18-6-1995, Order No. 91 dated 21-4-2004 and Order No. 92 dated 9-5-2004 are quoted below:—

"Order Nb. 60 dated 15-8-1993

বিবাদী পক্ষে হাজিরা দাখিল করিয়াছে। বাদী পক্ষে কোন তদবীর করে নাই। দরখাস্তে কারী মির্সেস শামসুন নাহার আজিম দোঃ কাঃ বিঃ ১ আদেশের ১০(২) নিয়ম ততসহ ১৫১ ধারায় বিধান মতে এক দরখাস্ত মূলে ওকালতনামা সহ ৩নং বিবাদী পক্ষ ভীক্তি হওয়ার আবেদন করে। আসামী ২৯-৯-১৯৯৩ ইং দরখাস্ত শুনানী।”

“Order No. 74 dated 18-6-1995

অদ্য জনৈক শাসসুন নাহার আজিমী বিবাদী হিসাবে পক্ষভূক্ত করার আবেদন সম্বলিত ১৫-৮-১৯৯৩ ইং তারিখের দরখাস্ত এবং অত মামলার কার্যক্রম স্থগিত রাখার শুনানীর জন্য দিন ধার্য্ আছে।

বিবাদী সরকার পক্ষ এবং পক্ষভূক্ত হওয়ায় প্রার্থী পক্ষ হাজিরা দিয়াছে জনৈক শামসুন নাহার আজিমকে পক্ষভূক্ত করার আবেদন স্বলিত বিগত ১৫-৮-১৯৯৩ ইং তারিখে আনীত দেঃ কাঃ বিঃ আইনের ১ আদেশের ১০(২) নিয়মে ও ১৫১ ধারয় দরখাস্তটি শুনানী এবং আদেশের জন্য নথি পেশ করা হইল।

21. Heard. Perused the petition. The plaintiff and defendant are not found available at the time of hearing. The prayer appears be justified and hence the same is allowed for ends of justice. Let the petitioners be added as defendant as prayed for (VOP). To 9-8-1995 for petition hearing."

"Order No. 91 dated 21-4-2004

22. Today is the date fixed for FPH plaintiff files hazira. Defendant takes no step.

23. It appears that the present plaintiff preferred Civil Revision No. 1739/1993 before the Hon'ble High Court Division. In the Judgment of that Civil revision the Hon'ble High Court Division observed that in view of the written statement filed by the Govt. Shamsunnahar Azim ought have been added as defendant in the suit by the plaintiff. Against that Judgment and order the plaintiff preferred Civil petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1001/ 1997 where the Hon'ble Appellate Division upholding the Judgment of the Hon'ble High Court Division observed that Shamsunnahar Azim ought to have been added as defendant in the suit by the plaintiff. It appears that as per order of the Hon'ble Court the plaintiff did not make necessary amendment in order to implead Shamsunnahar Azim as defendant. Furthermore, this court ought to have given direction to make such amendment. Thus the present suit be withdrawn from FPH. The plaintiff is directed to make necessary amendment in view of the above mentioned Judgment by adding Shamsunnahar Azim as stated in the written statement filed on behalf of the defendant No. 2. To 9-5-2004 for taking necessary steps"

"Order No. 92 dated 9--5-2004

24. Plaintiffs files a petition praying for exemption from taking step on the ground stated therein.

বিজ্ঞ কৌশলীর বক্তব্য শ্রবন করিলাম। দাখিলী দরখাস্ত ও নথি পর্যালোচনা করা হইল। নথী পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে সামছুন্না্হার আজিম এর দরখাস্তের প্রেক্ষিতে তাহাকে বিবাদী শ্রেণীভূক্ত করার জন্য ইং ১৮-৬-১৯৯৫ তারিখে আদেশ প্রদান করা হয়। কিন্তু তদানুযায়ী আরজি সংশোধন করা হয় নাই। অর্থাত আরজিতে বিবাদী হিসাবে তাহার নাম অর্ন্তভূক্ত রা হয় নাই। নথী পর্যালোচনায় আরও দেখা যায় যে উক্ত তারিখের আদেশটি বিজ্ঞ বিচারক কর্তৃখ ইং ১৮-৬-১৯৯৫ তারিখের হাজিরার উপর লিাপবদ্ধ করা হইয়াছিল। এমনকি ১৮-৬-১৯৯৫ উক্ত তারিখের আদেশটি বিজ্ঞ বিচারক কর্তৃক স্বাক্ষরিত হয় নাই। সে যাহা�� হউক্ শামসুন নাহার আজিমকে অত্র মোকদ্দমায় বিবাদী শ্রেণীভূক্ত করার জন্য আদেশ প্রদান করা হইয়াছে বিধায় তাহাকে ৩নং বিবাদী হিসাবে অর্ন্তভূক্ত করিয় আরজি ও বালাম বহি সংশোধন করা হউক। নথী পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে ১৮-৬-১৯৯৫ ইং তারিখের আদেশের পর লিখিত জবাব দাখিলের জন্য পক্ষভূক্ত বিবাদী কোন সুযোগ পায় নাই। কেননা ইং ২৫-৬-৯৫ তারিখের আদেশে মুল নথী বিজ্ঞ অতিরিক্ত জেলা ও দায়রা জজ আদালতে প্রেরণ করা হইয়াছে এবং পরবর্তীতে উহা মহামান্য হাইকোর্ট বিভাগে এবং আপীল বিভাগে প্রেরীত হইয়াছে। মোকদ্দমার নথী ফেরত আসার পর ৩নং পক্ষভূক্ত বিবাদীকে বিষয়টি অবহিত করানো হয় নাই। তাই ন্যায় বিচারের স্বার্থে ৩নং বিবাদীকে জবাব দাখিল করিয়া অত্র মোকদ্দমায় প্রতিদ্বদিতা সুযোগ প্রদান করা সমীচীন হইবে। আগামী ১২-৭-০৪ ইং তারিখে ৩নং পক্ষভূক্ত বিবাদীর জবাব দাখিলের জন্য ৩নং পক্ষভূক্ত বিবাদীর জবাব দাখিলের জন্য ৩নং পক্ষভূক্ত বিবাদী পক্ষের বিজ্ঞ কৌশুলীকে জাত করানো হউক।”

"Order No. 95 dated 15-9-2004

25. The date fixed being holiday the record is put up today. Plaintiffs files hazira, defendant No. 3 filed no written statement nor taken any steps. defendant No. 3 not yet informed.

26. It appears that the learned Advocate for the defendant No. 3 was not informed as the office could not find out him. So notice through the court should be issued upon defendant No. 3. It further appears that the defendant No. 2, namely the Government filed the written statement. But the learned GP was not informed. So notice through the court be issued upon defendant No. 3 fixing 25-10-2004 for S/R let the learned GP be informed."

"Order No. 96 dated 25-10-2004

27. Plaintiffs and defendant (govt) files hazira. Court notice upon defendant No. 3 returned duly served as per peons report. It appears that court notice issued upon defendant No. 3 was duly served, but the defendant No. 3 did not appear before the court on the specified date. It also appears that the suit was earlier fixed for peremptory hearing. But the defendant No. 2, namely the government of Bangladesh did not take any steps at the time of recording evidence of PWs through commission. Thus to 9-11-2004 for exparte disposal"

28. This background of the suit has to be kept in mind while considering the question of service of notice in this suit and decreed the suit in ex-parte as well as filing of the Miscellaneous Case No. 77 of 2007 after long delay of 944 days. In this connection learned Advocate for the opposite-party No. 1 has also drawn our attention to the order sheets of the Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 which is already quoted above.

29. It is quite clear that on 21-4-2004 plaintiff was directed to amend the plaint adding Shamsun Nahar Azim as defendant No. 3, but the plaint was not amended adding defendant No. 3 under Order 1, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Thereafter the learned Joint District Judge by order dated 9-5-2004 for adding defendant No. 3 by amending the plaint and intimate the order to learned Advocate for the defendant No. 3. It appears that the case record was sent to the High Court Division on 25-6-1995 in connection with Civil Revision 1739 of 1993, the plaintiffs-petitioners being unsuccessful in High Court Division and Appellate Division, the case record along with the copy of the judgment of the High Court Division and Appellate Division was received back by the trial court on 2-7-2003. It is evident from the Revisional application  and CPLA which were exhibited in this case as Exhibit No. 6 and 6(ka) though the petitioner was added as defendant No. 3 in the suit on 18-6-1995 but the plaintiffs-opposite-party intentionally did not add her party in the suit but the learned Advocate of the added defendant No. 3 Was not found in court to intimate the date of hearing of the suit. When the case record was sent back to the trial court on 2-7-2003, and the trial court having found no advocate in the court on that day, the court issued notice upon the defendant No. 3 opposite party No. 1 herein to secure her attendance. Thereafter, the petitioners Nos. 1 and 2 fraudulently shown the notice was duly served upon the opposite party No. 1 on 15-10-2004 in connivance with the process server and considering the unscrupulous peon's report the learned Joint District Judge again decreed the grit by order dated 10-1-2005.

30. Opposite party No. 1 clearly stated m her application under Order IX, rule 13 Code of Civil Procedure that no notice was served upon her in Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 and the process server in collusion with the plaintiffs submitted report that the summons were duly served upon the defendant No. 3.

31. At the hearing of the Miscellaneous Case the petitioner herself was examined as PW 1 an OPW. 2 the process server deposed and proved service report dated 15-10-2004. (Exhibit-Kha).

32. PW 1, Mrs Shamsun Nahar Azim in her deposition stated that:

“....................................মহামান্য হাইকোর্ট ও আপীল ডিভিশনে আমাকে কোন পক্ষ না করায় এবং কোন নোটিশ না দেওয়ায় এবং মূল মোকদ্দমা সম্পর্কে মোটেই অবগত না থাকায় আমি মামলায় কোন তদ্বির করিতে পারি নাই। সর্বোপরি আমার নিযুক্তীর বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবী সাহেব জানাইয়াছে যে আপনার মামলার দায়িত্ব আমার আপনি কোন চিন্তা করিবেন না।....................উক্ত জারী দেখানো হইলেও প্রকৃত পক্ষে উক্ত নোটিশ আমি পাই নাই। জারী নোটিশে লিথিত শাসসুন্নাহার আজিম নামের স্বাক্ষর অত্র মিস মোকদ্দমার তরফদানীগন কর্তৃক নাঃ সম্পত্তি আত্বস্বাতের প্রয়াশে জারীকারণের সহিত যোগসাজশে জ্বাল-জ্বালিয়াতির মাধ্যমে সৃজিত বটে। উক্ত নোটিসে মোকাবেলা স্বাক্ষীদের টিপসহি নাই, পিতার নাম ও সম্পূর্ন ঠিকানা উল্লেখ নাই।.................................আমাকে মূল দেঃ ৩৭৫/৮৪ নং মোকদ্দমায় পক্ষ না করায় পরবর্তীতে একতরফা রায় ও ডিক্রি হাসিল করায় আমার আবেদন ক্রমে পক্ষভূক্তির পরে স্যুট রেজিষ্টার্ড সংশোধন না করায় মূল মোকদ্দমা হইতে উদ্ভূত বিভিন্ন মোকদ্দমা সমূহে পক্ষশভূক্ত না করায় কোন নোটিশ না পাওয়ায় এবং মূল মোকদ্দমার অবস্থান সম্পর্কে মোটেই অবগত না থাকায় উক্ত মোকদ্দমায় কোন তদ্বীরাদি করিতে পারে নাই। In reply to cross examination she stated that ...............“আমার বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবী সাহেব আমাকে বলেছেন যে যেহেতু আপনি অত্র মোকদ্দমার পক্ষ হইয়াছেন। এখন যদি কিছু করতে হয় সরকার করবে। আপনার কিছু করতে হইবে না।”

Such contention of opposite-party No. 1 remain unaffected which transpires from Order No. 95 dated 15-9-2004 stating. "It appears that the learned Advocate for the defendant No. 3 was not informed at the office could not find out him." Thus it is evident that appointed Advocate for the defendant No. 3 is quite negligent in not performing his duties for that she should not suffer for the laches and negligence of her appointed advocate.

33. In the miscellaneous case the process server, Abdur Rahman deposed before the court as OPW No. 2 and proved service Reports Exhibit- ICha stating that: “সামছুন্নাহার আজিম আমার সামনে স্বাক্ষর দিয় নোটিশ গ্রহন করে। মোকাবেলা স্বাক্ষী রিয়াজ মনির, শাহজাহান রোড, মোহাম্মদপুর ঢাকা লেখা নাই। and exhibited the court notice and his signature upon it. In cross examination he admitted that: শহজাহান রোডে A, B, C block আছে। Court notice এর মধ্যে ১/৩ নং শাহাজাহান রোড কিন্তু Block এর নম্বর উল্লেখ নাই। আমি জারি করতে যাই অফিস থেকৈ কয়টার সময়ে উহা আমার স্নরন নাই। আমি আমার অফিস চলাকালীন সময় যাই। শামসুন্নাহার আজিম এর ১/৩ holding এ কয়টি বাড়ী আছে উহা আমার জানা নাই। ১/৩ holding এ কয়টি বাড়ী আছে উহা আমি বলিতে পারিব না। শামসুন্নাহার আজিমকে আমি চিনি না। He also admitted that মোকাবেলা স্বাক্ষীদের পিতার নাম উল্লেখ করি নাই। স্বাক্ষী স্বাক্ষর করিতে না পারিলে টিপসই নিতে হয় তাহা আমার জানা আছে। Courts notice এর মধ্যে মোকাবেলা স্বাক্ষীগন স্বাক্ষর করে নাই। মোকাবেলা স্বাক্ষীদের আমি স্বাক্ষর করিতে বলি উহা উল্লেখ নাই। In particular the signatures and addresses of Mokabila witnesses were not noted in the service report. The Peon has not explained in his report why it was not possible for him to obtain signatures of the Mokabila witnesses.

34. It transpires that 15-10-2004 was Friday, as such OPW No. 2 contention that he went to serve the notice at office hour is of no substance. Thus from the deposition of OPW No. 2 it evident that the court notice it was shown to be served upon the opposite party No. 1 by practicing fraud.

35. It is, therefore obligatory upon the process-server to obtain signature of the Mokabila witnesses in his report and address of the persons, if any, by whom the house in question was identified and in whose presence the copy of notice was served.

36. Under order V, rule 19A of the Code of Civil Procedure the declaration of process server is an evidence of the fact as to the service of summons upon the defendant. The report that the service of was made on the identification of the Mokabila witnesses implies that the process server did not know the defendant and or her house. So in absence of any statement by OPW No. 2 on the point of his identification, the recital as to the identification which is like any other evidence remains uncorroborated, and in the face of denial by the defendant No. 3 there remains a genuine suspicious that the service was made upon the defendant No. 3.

37. In this connection Rule 70 of the CRO volume-1 is very much relevant which provides for service of summons in presence of at least "two independent local residents" service of summon in presence of witnesses without their address is not certainly in accordance with the rule. Again under this Rule 70 the process server is required "whenever possible" to obtain the signatures of the Mokabila witnesses. This implies that in the case of absence of signatures of the Mokabila witnesses the process server is required to explain in his report why it could not be possible to obtain the signatures. The OPW No. 2 in reply to cross examination stated মোকাবেলা স্বাক্ষীদের আমি স্বাক্ষর করিতে বলি উহা উল্লেখ নাই।. The process server admittedly did not mention any explanation to that effect. Such an statement raises a reasonable suspicious that no Mokabila witnesses was present.

38. The service report, (Exhibit-Kha) are devoid of these essential information. The courts below after considering the order sheet, oral and documentary evidence on record and relevant provision of law clearly of the opinion that the summons was not duly served upon the Defendant No. 3 in the Title Suit No. 375 of 1984.

39. In this respect the principle of law is now well settled as enunciated in a case Llpendre Chandra Rishi vs Sufia Begum reported in 42 DLR (AD) 285 = 10 BLD (AD).194 wherein it was held that:

"Service of summons, proof of Summons served by process-server noting the names and address of Mokabila witnesses in the service return-Process-server appearing in Court as a witness-his evidence without examining the Mokabila witness not acceptable—It is obligatory upon the process-server to mention in his report the name and address of the person if any, by whom the house in question was identified and in whose presence the copy of summons was affixed-When service reports were devoid of these essential information, they were unacceptable-Mere personal appearance of the process-server as a witness in Court did not make the report acceptable."

40. Mr AF Hassan Ariff learned Senior Advocate for the petitioner mainly submits that the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was not filed within 30 days from the date of obtaining certified copy and the same was filed after 18 days which was beyond 30 days as provided under Article 164 of the Limitation Act in as much valuable right has been accrued by the plaintiffs. He also submits about the locus standi of the present opposite-party No. 1 since the paramount title holder is not claiming the suit property.

41. In reply to the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners, Mr Fida M. Kamal, learned Advocate for the opposite-parties submits that the ex-parte decree was obtained by practicing fraud upon the court and some elements of collusion and fraud are found on the record. The facts as disclosed in the evidence is that the decree-holder by suppressing summons obtained the ex-parte decree fraudulently and this finding of fact has been arrived at both the courts below. Such decree obtained fraudulently is a nullity in the eye of law. It is by practising deceit and fraud that the decree was obtained and when such fraud and deceit is established, a decree has no existence in the eye of law and it must be set aside. Such enquiry is permissible within the scope of Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure because the term of the rule itself provides for setting aside the ex-parte decree if it is obtained, inter alia, by suppressing the summons. The findings of facts arrived at by the courts below, is that summons were fraudulently suppressed and once fraud is established, limitation will run from the date when the fraud was detected. If fraud is proved there is no question of limitation.

<u>42. In the present case in a hot haste an ex-parte decree was obtained which indicates that a fraud was committed upon the court as well as upon the defendant, then there is no question of limitation and so, the question of limitation as raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioners does not arise in the present case. Even as for arguments sake, it is conceded that the fraud was detected earlier, even the court is not debarred to interfere under Order IX, rule 13 and Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In this connection reliance may be placed to the decision reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167.</u>

43. Moreover, the argument made by the learned Advocate for the petitioners that Miscellaneous Case was filed after 18 days which was beyond 30 days as provided in the Limitation Act and same was not raised before the trial court when the plaintiffs petitioners filed written objection in the miscellaneous case. Furthermore, it is evident from the deposition of OPW 2 and service return (Exhibit-Kha) that no notice was served upon the defendant No. 3. So the submission advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner has no merit.

44. In 35 DLR 164 case it was held under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code, if summons is not duly served on the defendant, that is a good ground for setting aside an ex-parte decree. On a perusal of the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Code, it would be apparent that due service of summons is an essential condition, which must be satisfied before the court can proceed to give a judgment and under Order IX, rule 13, if a party satisfies a court that summons were not duly served upon him, the court is bound to set aside the ex-parte decree. In such a case, question of knowledge is not at all relevant and decree will be set aside even if the defendant had knowledge of institution of a suit.

<u>45. It has also been enunciated in the case of Bangladesh vs Mashiur Rahman reported in 50 DLR (AD) 205 where in it has been held that it is a cardinal principle of administration of justice that no result of any judicial proceeding should be allowed to receive judicial approval from any court of law whenever it is obtained by practicing fraud upon the court; reason being fraud demolishes the very foundation of sanctity of such judicial proceeding. It is also well established principle of law that fraud vitiates all judicial proceedings. Thus contravention of the provision of law cannot be a valid ground for allowing an order obtained by fraud to stand. When the trial Court itself on consideration of the materials on record was satisfied that a fraud had been committed in obtaining the ex-parte decree it was the duty of the trial court to set aside the ex-parte decree. The failure of the trial court in the performance of its legal obligations ought not to have been maintained by the High Court Division in affirming the finding of the trial Court.</u>

46. The learned Advocate for the petitioners has referred the case of Province of East Pakistan vs Md Habibur Rahman reported in 25 DLR 254 but the said decision has got any direct bearing on the question involved in the present case. In the cited case no cause was make out in respect of the service of summons but in the present case the ex-parte decree was obtained by practicing fraud upon the court. So the reported case will not be any help of the petitioners.

47. It also appears that both the court below clearly found that the notice was not served upon the added defendant No. 3 and from the judgment of the courts below, it is found that in arriving their findings the courts below clearly considered the materials facts and circumstances and evidence on record both the oral and documentary and consequently this findings of facts are immuned from attack in the revision. In this respect I can rely on the decision reported in 17 BLD (AD) 295 wherein it has been held:—

"It is a settled principle that the findings of fact. Whether concurrent or not arrived at by the lower appellate Court which is the final Court of fact. Is binding on the High Court Division as a revisional Court except in certain well-defined exceptional circumstances. Such as non-consideration or misreading of the materials evidence affecting the merit of the case."

48. Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case and the provisions of the law and the decisions cited above I am of the opinion that the courts below on proper consideration of the materials and evidence on record and applying the principle of law and the decisions quoted above, arrived at A correct decision, there is no cogent reason to interfere with the decision of the courts below.

49. This revisional application cannot, therefore, succeed.

50. In the result, this rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

51. Since it is an old suit relates to specific performance of contract, both the parties are directed to render effective assistance to the trial court that it can be disposed of the suit within 6 (six) months from the receipt of the record from this court. The learned Joint District Judge is further directed not to grant any adjournment to either the parties except on very urgent reason.

52. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule, is hereby vacated.

Send down the Lower Court records expeditiously.

End.
