full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J: This Civil Appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 13-12-2004 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3315 of 1995 making the Rule absolute.

2. The facts of the case, in brief, are that respondent No. 1 herein as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 43 of 1989 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Kathalia, Jhalakathi, praying for declaration of rayoti right and title in respect of the land described in schedule 'Ka' to the plaint. She stated, inter alia, that the land described in the 'Ka' schedule measuring 4.62 acres belonged to Gunai Mallik, who died leaving 3 sons, Baghai Mallik, Ratan Mallik and Jiten Mallik Jiten Mallik settled 2.25 acres of land by patta dated 28-6-1920 in favour of Mohed Molla and Amerunnessa. Mohed Molla settled his land by patta dated 31-5-1941 to Kalu Shikder who then transferred the said land by patta dated 2-2-1942 to Abdul Kader Mallik and Lal Mallik. Lal Mallik died leaving son, namely Forkan who transferred 90¾ decimals of land by the kabala dated 10-10-1988 to the plaintiff; that Pakkhi Bibi, sister of Hatem son of Ratan, transferred 0.74 acre of land by patta dated 28-5-1943 to Noor Mohammad Mridha and Abdul Kader Mallik; and that Pakkhi Bibi on that date also transferred 0.49 acre of land to Abdul Kader Mallik and Ful Baru Bibi, i.e. father and mother respectively of the plaintiff. Abdul Kader Mallik died leaving son Lal Mallik and a daughter Saleha Begum, the plaintiff as heirs; that the plaintiff thus acquired title in 1.92 acres of land by inheritance and by purchase and owns and possesses the said land upon paying rent to the Government; that at the time of recent survey the land was wrongly recorded in the name of the defendants and that wrong record having clouded the title of the plaintiff, she is constrained to file the suit.

3. The suit was contested by defendant Nos. 2, 3, 13, 14, 21 and 22 as well as by defendant Nos. 4-9 by filing two sets of written statements denying the material averments made in the plaint. The defendants stated, inter alia, that Gunai Mallik owned 4.46 acres of land and died leaving 3 sons and 3 daughters, and the sons of Gunai Mallik, namely Ratan Mallik, Jiten Mallik and Baghai Mallik transferred 2.30 acres of land by patta to Dabiruddin and he transferred 0.43 acre of land to the defendants; that land measuring 1.13 acres appertaining to Khabot No. 379 was recorded in the name of the Executor General, and land measuring 1.20 acres were recorded in the name of the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 4-9; that defendants are not claiming the share of Baghai Mallik; that land measuring 1.13 acres were recorded in the name of Mofezuddin and he transferred the said land to the defendants. The defendants are possessing 1.29½ acres of land out of the land in suit; the plaintiff has no possession in the land; the defendant Nos. 4-9 are in possession of 0.63 acre of land; that plaintiff's predecessor Amirunnessa transferred 0.29 acre of land by patta dated 19th Chaitra, 1342 BS to Hukum Ali, Kasem Ali and Syed Ali and the defendants are in possession of the said 0.29 acre of land and the plaintiff has not included the said 0.29 acre of land in the suit.

4. After hearing the parties and considering the materials on record, the learned Assistant Judge, Kathalia, Jhalakathi, by his judgment and decree dated 27-7-1991 decreed the suit.

5. Against the said judgment and decree, the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 82 of 1991 before the District Judge, Jhalakathi. On transfer, the appeal was heard and disposed of by the Subordinate Judge, First Court, Jhalakathi, who after hearing the parties, allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the appellate Court, the plaintiff preferred Civil Revision No.3315 of 1995 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which upon hearing the parties was made absolute.

7. Against the said judgment and order of the High Court Division, the defendants as petitioners filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 205 of 2005.

8. Leave was granted on the following submissions of the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners:

"(I) The lower appellate Court, as final Court of facts, upon assessing and reassessing the evidence, both oral and documentary, held that the plaintiff will get 0.34½ acre of land but the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute without reversing the said findings.

(II) The appellate Court below correctly held that the suit being for mere declaration of title, is not maintainable without seeking relief for partition because the land in question is unspecified, the High Court Division committed error of law in making the Rule absolute without reversing the said finding; and

(III) The Court of appeal below, as the last Court of facts, has pronounced its verdict upon proper assessment and reassessment of evidence, both oral and documentary, pleadings and other materials on record; the revisional Court erred in law in making the Rule absolute without reversing the findings of the last Court of facts.

9. Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas, learned Advocate-on-Record appearing on behalf of the appellant made submissions in line with the grounds upon which leave was granted. The learned Advocate pointed out that neither the body of the plaint nor the schedule to the plaint specifies the suit land giving its identity marked by boundaries and hence, the appellate Court correctly dismissed the suit, but the High Court Division without adverting to this provision of law as contained in Order VII, rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure, made the Rule absolute thereby, decreeing the suit.

10. Mr. Md. Oziullah, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 1 made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He also submitted that the appellate Court did not properly assess the oral and documentary evidence and, as such, the judgment and decree of the appellate Court was rightly reversed by the High Court Division. He further submitted that the High Court Division upon scrutiny of the evidence of PWs and DWs as well as other materials on record found that the appellate Court did not consider the material part of the evidence of PWs and DWs, particularly with regard to the possession of the plaintiff, and thus the impugned judgment is a proper one in exercise of its revisional jurisdiction.

11. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates appearing for the parties concerned and perused the impugned judgment of the High Court Division and other connected papers on record.

12. We note from the schedule to the plaint that the suit land is described at the end of the 'ka' schedule as follows:

“১-৫ নং দফায় মৌঃ সম্পত্তি ৬.০৭ শতাংশ উহার মধ্যে বাদী এর ১.৯২ শতাংশ উহাই অত্র মোকদ্দমা্র বিরোধীয়”।

13. Although the plot numbers are given in serial Nos. 1 to 5 of schedule 'ka', the description of the suit land is finally stated as 1.92 acres(written as nal) out of 6.07 acres (written as nal) detailed in serial Nos. 1 to 5. We note that serial No. 1 to 5 do not give any details of boundaries of the suit land, nor is there any detail regarding the boundary of the suit land in the body of the plaint. Clearly the description of the suit land appearing in the plaint, in particular in the schedule to the plaint, does not meet the requirements of Order VII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The suit land having not been properly identified in the decree of the trial Court, which has been upheld by the High Court Division, the said decree is not sustainable.

14. We find from the judgment of the appellate Court that there was discussion of the evidence of witnesses before arriving at the decision that the plaintiff was entitled to get 34½ decimals of land but without a prayer for partition she was not entitled to get a decree for declaration of title under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. We note from the impugned judgment that in fact the High Court Division in reversing the decision of the appellate Court, which is the final Court of facts, neither discussed the evidence of the witnesses nor reversed the findings of the appellate Court.

<u>15. In its revisional jurisdiction the High Court Division can only interfere with the judgment of the appellate Court in case of misreading and/or non-consideration of evidence and materials on record, or misconception of law. In the instant case the High Court Division has not adverted to any evidence or materials which has been misread or not considered by the appellate Court and also there is no suggestion that the appellate Court misconceived any provision of law. It is an established principle that in reversing the findings of the final Court of facts, the revisional Court must identify the evidence which has been misread or not considered by the appellate Court. This having not been done, the impugned judgment cannot be said to be in accordance with law and settled legal principles.</u>

<u>16. In view of the above discussion, we are of the opinion that the impugned judgment is not sustainable and is liable to be set aside. The appellate Court has pointed out that the suit, being one for declaration of title simpliciter, is not maintainable without a prayer for partition. Since the plaint does not properly identity the suit land and no boundaries are mentioned in the schedule to the plaint nor any sketch map appended thereto which might assist in identifying the suit land, there is no alternative but for the parties to establish their respective claim in a suit for partition.</u>

17. In the facts and circumstances discussed above, if a suit for partition is filed, the Court before which such suit is filed, will look into the title of the parties afresh, and the finding of the appellate Court regarding title to the suit property shall not be binding upon the Court dealing with the partition suit, if any is filed.

With the above observations, the appeal is allowed without, however, any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is set aside.

End.

lawyer:
Md Omar Faruk, Advocate -----For the Petitioners. 
Md Saifur Rahman, Advocate -----For the Opposite- Party Nos. 1-3.
parties:
Nazumer Nessa and others ----- Defendant-Petitioners
Vs
Hazera Khatun and others ----- Plaintiff- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-3 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 25-3-2001 passed 'by the Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Sadar, Chittagong in Other Appeal' No. 245 of 1998 affirming' those dated 24-8-1998 and 1-9-1998 respectively passed by the' Mirsarai Assistant- Judge, Sadar, Chittagong in Other Suit No. 13 of 1995' should not be set aside and/or' such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may' seem fit and proper. Shorn of unnecessary details, the fact of the case lies in a very short compass. The opposite party Nos. 1-3 as plaintiff instituted Other Suit No. 13 of 1995 in the Court of Mirsarai, Assistant Judge, Chittagong for declaration Of title that the impugned judgment and decree dated 26-4-1992 passed in Other Suit No. 21 of 1990 is illegal, inoperative; void and the same is not binding upon the plaintiffs along with a further, declaration that the deed of gift dated 28-5-1986 is false, fraudulent and collusive. The predecessor of the present-petitioner Nazumer Nessa as defendant No. 1 was contesting the suit by filing written statement on 17-5-1998; The suit as usual was fixed for peremptory hearing and on that date both the plaintiffs and the defendants were absent. When the suit was taken up for hearing. Resultantly, the suit was dismissed for default. Thereafter, the plaintiff filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 1998 under Order IX, rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the suit.

3. The trial court heard' the miscellaneous case and restored the suit in its original position and number on 15-6- 1998. After restoration, the trial court fixed the date on 13-7-1998 for peremptory hearing. The petitioner-defendant was not aware of the fact of restoration of the suit and the date fixed by the court for hearing. As a result of which, the petitioner could not appear before the court on the date of hearing on 13-7 -1998. Consequently, the suit was decreed ex parte on 24-8-1998 in absence 6f the petitioner-defendant.

4. Being aggrieved by the ex parte judgment and decree of the trial court, the petitioner preferred Other Appeal No. 245 of 1998 before the District Judge, Chittagong, Eventually, the appeal was heard by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong on transfer, The lower appellate court upon, hearing the appeal disallowed the same by the impugned judgment and decree dated 25-3-2001. At this stage, the petitioner-defendant No. 1 moved this Court by filing this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule and order of status-quo.

5. During pendency of the Rule, the petitioner died and her legal heirs, have been substituted in her place.

6. Mr. Md Omar Faruk, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the trial court while passing the decree in favour of the plaintiff ex parte did not observe the minimum legal requirement of law by discussing the evidences adduced on behalf of the plaintiff both oral and documentary as to whether such evidences at all entitle the plaintiffs to get a decree as prayed for. He further submits that the cardinal principle of law is that the plaintiff is to prove his own case. But in the present case the trial court in decreeing the suit ex parte utterly failed to observe that the evidences produced before the court by the plaintiffs are sufficient for passing the decree in favour of the plaintiff and, as such, the trial court has committed' an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

7. He further submits that Order XX, rule 4(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that the judgment shall contain a concise statement of the case, point for determination of the decision thereon and the reason for such decision but in the present case the trial court as well as the appellate court has committed an error of law totally ignoring such provision as contained in Order XX, of the Code of Civil Procedure. It is also argued that though' in' a miscellaneous case filed under Order IX, rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure service of notice upon the defendants are ,not required by law but in the event of restoration of the suit and fixing subsequent date for hearing the defendants are required to be informed about hearing of the suit. In the instant case no notice or information was given to the defendants about restoration and subsequent date of hearing and, as such disposal of the suit ex parte without any intimation to the defendants is illegal and contrary to the provision of law. He further submits that both the courts below erroneously found that the learned Advocate for the petitioner was informed about the restoration of the suit and the date, of hearing but it does not mean that this defendant Was personally informed about restoration the suit arid, as such, the judgment arid decree of both the courts below are liable to be set-aside.

8. Mr. Md. Saifur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1-3 submits that the suit was restored on 24-6-1998 and fixed for hearing on 13-7-1998 in presence of the learned Advocates of both the parties. On 13-7-1998 the plaintiff filed an application under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking amendment of the plaint without service of copy of the same upon the defendant as the defendant No.1 was absent on that date. Subsequently, 3-8-1998 was fixed for further hearing. On that date both the parties filed hazira. The plaintiff filed an application praying for disposal of the suit ex parte upon recording evidence of PWs. The trial court fixed on 24-8-1998 for ex parte hearing and decreed the suit ex parte. Therefore, the plea so far taken by the petitioner about ignorance of restoration 'of the suit and of fixing subsequent date for hearing is not at all true and absolutely contrary to the facts and circumstances of the case and the order sheets. It is also argued that to get an ex parte decree set aside the defendants are to fulfill two conditions i.e. no notice was served upon them or the defendant was prevented by sufficient cause for not appearing on the date when the case 'was taken up for hearing by the court. In the instant case, the petitioner utterly failed to satisfy the aforesaid requirements .before the court below and, as such the appellate court rightly disallowed the appeal refusing to set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial court ex parte.

9. Heard the learned Advocates for the parties, gone through the revisional application, impugned judgment and decree of the courts below and the, order sheets of the trial court.

10. From' a perusal of the order sheets of the trial court, it appears that the suit was restored on 24-6-1998 and it was fixed on B-7-1998 for further hearing with an intimation to the learned Advocates for the parties who had seen the order of the court. On 13-7-1998 the plaintiff filed hazira the defendant was-absent and the plaintiff was also filed an application under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the plaint without .service of copy upon the defendant as it appears from the order Sheets. n. On 3-8-1998 the- suit was fixed for further hearing. Both the parties filed hazira but the hearing was adjournment due to engagement of the court otherwise and fixed on 19-8-1998. The plaintiff on the date fixed filed hazira and an application praying for disposal of the suit ex parte, by recording evidence of the plaintiff. The defendant was absent. The trial court fixed 24-8- 1998 for exparte hearing and, on that date the suit was decreed ex parte. Subsequently, the defendant filed an application on 27-8-1998 praying for allowing' them to cross-examine the plaintiff but the said application was rejected. Thereafter, the petitioner preferred an appeal against the ex-parte judgment and decree before the District Judge, Chittagong, 'which was also dismissed on contest on the ground that the appellant could not satisfy the court that she was prevented by sufficient cause when the suit was taken up, for hearing. Moreover, the appellate court clearly found that the defendant was duly informed about restoration of the suit and fixing of subsequent date for further hearing, as it appears from the order dated 3-8-1998 on which date -the defendant-appellant filed hazira before the trial court and, as such, the plea of not aware of restoration of' the suit and fixation of the date of hearing' is absolutely contrary to the' actual' facts and circumstances of the case. The order sheets 'show that the petitioner was fully aware of the proceeding in Other Suit No. 13 of 1995.

12. Now the question before this Court has arisen as to whether the trial court in passing the judgment ex parte has observed and satisfied the minimum legal requirement as provided by law. To appreciate the argument advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioner the impugned ex-parte decree passed by the trial court by its Order No.1S dated 25-8-1998, may be looked into which runs thus:-

অদ্য  মামলাটি একতরফা শুনানির দিনধার্য  আছে । বাদীপক্ষ হাজিরা  দাখিল করিয়াছে । নথি  একতরফা শুনানির  জন্য উপস্থাপন করা হইল | পি, ডবিলউ- ১ হাজী এনামূল হকের পুন: জবানবন্দি  শপথ  নামা পাঠ পূর্বক গ্রহণ করা হইল।

অত্র  মোকদ্দমার আরজী, পি, ডব্লিউ-১ এর  জবানবন্দি, দাখিল  দলিলপত্র ও কাগজপত্র প্রদর্শনী ১-৩(খ) এবং  অত্র  মোকদ্দমার নথি  পর্যালোচনায় বাদীগণ তাদের  অত্র  মোকদ্দমার  একতরফা সূত্রে প্রমাণ সক্ষম হয়েছেন।

প্রদত্ত  কোর্ট ফি সঠিক।

অতএব,

হুকুম হলো যে,

অত্র মোকদ্দমা বিবাদীগণের বিরুদ্ধে একতরফা সূত্রে বিনা খরচায় ডিক্রি হলো। এতদ্বারা ১নং বিবাদীর স্বত্ব ঘোষণা করে প্রচারিত অত্র  আদালতের অপর ২১/৯০নং মোকদ্দমায় ২৬-৪-৯২ ইং তারিখের রায় ও ২-৫-১৯৯২ইং তারিখের ডিক্রি বাতিল ও অকার্য্যকর মর্মে  এবং এতদ্বারা বাদীগণ বাধ্য নন মর্মে ঘোষণা করা হলো এবং ১নং বাদিনীকে সাক্ষী দেখিয়ে ও সুলতান আহমেদকে দাতা দেখিয়ে সৃজিত ১৮-৫-১৯৮৬ ইং তারিখের অরেজিষ্ট্রীকৃত দানপত্র দলিল জাল, ভূয়া ও অকার্যকর মর্মে ঘোষণা করা হলো।

13. From a perusal of the order quoted above passed by, the trial court decreeing the suit ex parte, it appears that the trial court did not observe the minimum legal .requirement as provided in Order rule 4(2) of the, Code of Civil Procedure which provides that the judgment shall contain a concise statement of the case, the point for determination, the, decision thereon and the reasons for such .decision. The trial court in passing the ex parte decree only observed that, the PW 1 has been examined, the evidence recorded by the court and the Exhibits have been perused and found that the plaintiff has been able to prove his case 'and on that 'finding the suit was decreed ex' parte, as 'such, 'the impugned 'judgment and decree of the' trial court has not fulfilled the requirement of law.'

14.The trial court utterly  failed to give reasons for decision.in decreeing the suit ex parte, In the case of Bangladesh vs Israil Ali reported in 1981 BLD (AD) 371, It has been held that;

Ex parte disposal of suit in the manner set out above is not, warranted under the provisions of Code of Civil Procedure. It is expected that the courts below 'should observe the minimum legal requirement in disposing of a suit ex parte;"

15. In the absence of observance of minimum legal requirement of law the judgment passed ex parte by trial court is bad in law. In the case of Shamsuddin Ahmed vs Bangladesh, reported in 45 DLR 675 it has also been held that" a judgment even when it is an ex parte should show application of court's judicial mind as to whether the plaintiff's witness and the papers produced proved the plaintiff's case.

<u>16. Code of Civil Procedure' does not define either an ex parte judgment or 'an ex parte decree.  It refers only to a judgment and a 'decree. In the event a judgment is known to' be annex parte judgment and the decree drawn on the' basis of that judgment is known as an ex parte decree.</u>

<u>Hence, even for' an ex parte judgment 'and the decree; the basic ingredients of judgment must be available to the extent to indicate that the court has applied its mind to the pleading, relief claimed there under; the evidence and conclusion arrived at by the court on the' above:</u>

<u>17. From the above discussions it is manifestly dear that even a judgment rendered ex-parte and a decree is drawn on the basis of that judgment it is appealable. In case: that judgment and decree become final without 'there being any appeal, the decree is executable. In that: sense, there is no difference between a judgment and decree and an ex parte judgment and decree. In view of the above. In the event the defendant is set ex parte, the Court should be more careful in such case and it should consider the: pleadings and evidence and arrive at a finding, as to whether the plaintiff has made out a case for a decree prayed for. In, this context, it may also be mentioned that though a detailed judgment is required-in a contested matter, an' ex parte judgment should show the application of the minimum requirement of consideration of the pleadings, issues, evidence and the relief sought for rendering such judgment.</u>

18. Apart from this, considering the situation like the present one, the Code of Civil Procedure was amended in the year 2006 with the avowed purpose of abridging, and simplifying the procedural law and to avoid delay, expedite disposal, save the public time, private convenience and money. By enacting the Rule 13A of Order IX, and rule 19A of order 41 parliament left it open to the defendant and the appellant to apply under Rule 13A of Order IX, for setting aside an ex parte decree by depositing an amount of cost not exceeding Taka 3000 or for re-admission of appeal under Rule 19 A of Order 41 of the Code, The legislative attempt incorporated in the code to discourage dismissal of the suit for default and passing of an ex parte decree keeping in mind that the litigation between the parties should be ended with contested hearing. Therefore, the court is to consider an application for setting aside an• ex parte decree or an appeal thereof liberally. In the case of KDH Laboratories Ltd. Vs Pubali Bank reported in' 40 DLR 1 it has been observed that,

"Superior Courts do not permit an ex parte hearing as a general rule."

19. This being the position, a suit seeking a declaration of a judgment passed in earlier suit a nullity and a deed of gift as illegal and. void, I think that the matter in dispute ought to have disposed of on contest by giving an opportunity to the defendants to defend themselves, In the circumstances, both the judgments and decree passed by the courts below are liable to be set aside."

20. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, however, there will be no order as to costs, The impugned judgment and decree dated 25-3-2001 passed by the Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Sadar; Chittagong in other Appeal No, 245 of 1998 and judgment and decree dated 24-8-1998' passed' in Other Suit No: 13of 1995 by the Mirsarai Assistant Judge Chittagong are hereby set aside.

21. The trial court is directed to proceed with the hearing of the suit and disposed of the same within 6(six) months from the date of receipt of this judgment positively.

22. The order of status-quo granted at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated.

23. Communicate a copy of this judgment to the Court concerned.

Send down the lower court records at once.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 14th day of February, 2011 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.4 of 2009)
full_judgment:
Md Abdul Wahhab Miah J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated the 14th day of February, 2011 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 4 of 2009 making the Rule Nisi absolute.

2. Facts necessary for disposal of this petition are that respondent No. 3 herein, Manager, Bangladesh Krishi Bank, Tongi Branch, Tongi, Gazipur (hereinafter referred to as the Bank) instituted Artha Rin SuitNo, 36 of 2004 in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Gazipur for recovery of loan amounting to Taka 34,65,698 as well as interest thereon till realization thereof impleading the petitioner herein and respondent No.4, M/s Hossain and sons poultry as defendants. Eventually, the suit was decreed ex-parte on 9-8-2004. The judgment-debtors having failed to pay the decretal dues, the decree-holder- Bank levied Artha Jari Case No. 52.of 2004 on 20-11-2004 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Second Court, Gazipur (hereinafter referred to as the executing Court) for recovery of the decretal dues. In the arthajari case, notice was published in the daily newspaper for auction sale of the mortgaged property of the judgment-debtors. 3(three) bidders participated in the auction held on 4-6-2006 and Md Asaduzzaman Belal became the highest bidder offering Taka 12,01,000. The offer was not accepted by the Executing Court and the auction was cancelled. Thereafter, the second auction was held on 7-8-2005. Again three bidders including Md Asaduzzaman Belal participated in the auction and Md Asaduzzaman Belal became the highest bidder at Taka 12,10,000 and this time, the bid was accepted on 14-8-2005. The auction-purchaser deposited the entire auction money and sale certificate was issued in his favour on 27-9-2005. Thereafter the mortgaged land was duly registered in favour of the auction-purchaser by the Executing Court in the Office of the Sub-Registrar. At this stage, the full brother of judgment-debtor No. 2 (the petitioner herein) as 3rd party claimant filed an application before the Executing Court under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code). The said application was rejected on 7-2-2006 against which the brother of the judgment-debtor filed Civil Revision No. 8 of 2005 which was subsequently rejected on 22-1-2008, though application was filed to withdraw the civil revision. On 26-5-2008, judgment-debtor No. 2 (hereinafter referred to as the judgment-debtor) filed an application before the Executing Court under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (the Ain, 2003) by depositing Taka 6,65,500 with 10% profit (in the application in Bengali, it has been written as ১০%লভ্যাংশfor setting aside the auction sale and the bainama and to pass necessary order to return the mortgaged property to him stating, inter alia, that he had no homestead except the mortgaged property sold in auction. He had been in South Korea for which he could not pay the loan to the Bank and the decree was obtained through fraudulent means. The Executing Court by the order dated 29-7-2008 cancelled the auction sale dated 7-8-2005, the acceptance order dated 14-8-2005 and the sale certificate issued on 27-9-2005. By the same order, the Executing Court also directed that the auction purchaser would get 10% interest from 7-8-2005 to 7-8-2008 amounting to Taka 3,63,000 along with bid money of Taka 12,10,000 and other costs of Taka 70,000, i.e. in total Taka 16,43,000 and directed the judgment-debtor to deposit the money within 30 (thirty) days from date, failing which "the order shall. stand dismissed." Challenging this order, the auction purchaser filed the writ petition on the ground that he was a bonafide purchaser, sale certificate was duly issued in his favour and it was also duly registered in the Office of the Sub-Registrar through the Court and so, there was no scope for cancellation of auction sale and a registered sale certificate on an application filed by the judgment-debtor under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 long after 3 (three ) years of the auction sale.

3. The mortgaged property in question was sold in auction after complying with all the provisions of law, the Executing Court acted illegally in setting aside the sale.

4. 8. 9. 10. Mr Qumrul Haque Siddique, learned Advocate, appearing for the judgment-debtor-petitioner, has submitted that the Executing Court considering the facts, namely: (a) the auction purchaser submitted the bids collusively showing him as the highest bidder in both the auction sale (first auction was held on 14-6-2005, that auction was not accepted, second auction was held on 7-8-2005), (b) the judgment-debtor took a loan of taka 16,14,000 on 13-4-1995 mortgaging the auction sold land (in the impugned order dated 27-7-2008, it has been wrongly mentioned as the suit land) and naturally, it could not be said that value of the auction sold land on 13- 4-1995 was not less than Taka 16,14,000. 11. Mr Siddique has referred to the photostat copies of the two firisty forms filed with the additional paper book on behalf of the petitioner to show that the auction purchaser already received the 3(three) pay orders dated 21-5-2008, 6-8-2008 and 27-8-2008 for the sum of Taka 6,65,500, 6,65,000 and 3,13,000 respectively deposited by the judgment-debtor by making endorsement on the body of those firisty forms, so he could not maintain the writ petition, but these facts could not be brought to the notice of the High Court Division at the time of hearing the writ petition and could not also be brought on record while filing the leave petition. Mr Islam has submitted that the High Court Division took the correct view that in view of the specific provision in the Code, the application filed by the judgment-debtor under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 was not maintainable in law Mr Islam has vehemently opposed the submission of Mr Siddique on the point that the auction purchaser received the auction purchased money along with the other amounts deposited by the judgment-debtor pursuant to the order of the Executing Court impugned in the writ petition by accepting the pay orders making endorsement on the firisty forms. 13. From the impugned judgment and order, it appears that the High Court Division, in fact, made the Rule Nisi absolute on the finding that in view of section 26 of the Ain,2003, the provisions of rules89 and 90 of Order XXI of the Code were applicable, but the judgment-debtor without filing application under any of the said rules filed the application under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 for setting aside the auction sale, the same was not maintainable. The High Court Division further found that at the time of filing the application under section 57 of the Ain, 2003, the judgment-debtor instead of depositing the amount as specified in the proclamation of sale, deposited only the amount on which the mortgaged property was sold in auction and 10% compensation on the bid money. Therefore, the judgment-debtor did not comply with the provisions of Order XXI, rule 89 of the Code which provides that at the time of filing such application the amount specified in the proclamation of sale for the recovery of which “sale was ordered for payment to the decree-holder and a sum equivalent of 5% of the purchase money for payment to the purchaser has to be deposited.”  The High Court Division further observed that the judgment-debtor claimed that he was in Korea and in his absence, the decree was obtained in the suit by practising fraud, but he failed to produce before the Court an iota of evidence to 'show that he informed the Bank about his departure for Korea or about his address in Korea so that the Bank could know about his address in Korea and could communicate with him. The High Court Division further held that mere assertion that "the judgment and decree was obtained by fraud" was not enough, it must be shown that the Bank was aware of the fact that the judgment-debtor left for foreign country (South Korea) and it was informed about his last address, otherwise the provision of service of summons/ notice under sections 7 and J06f the Ain, 2003 and the execution case respectively would be meaning- less and nugatory. The High Court Division further held that if a defendant/judgment-debtor leaves for a foreign country the notice/summons is to be served at his last known address but the Executing Court did not consider "this legal aspect" of the case. The High Court Division further observed that an application could be filed also under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code on the ground of material irregularity or fraud, "if there has been any material irregularity or fraud in the auction sale of processes", but no such application was filed as well. The High Court Division lastly found that inherent power as stipulated in section 57 of the Ain, 2003 is subject to the provision of the Ami 2003, power under that section could be exercised, had there been no provisions in the Code for setting aside the sale and again if the application was filed under Order XXI, rules 89/90, then those could be registered as miscellaneous case and decide on taking evidence and the Executing Court was not empowered to set aside the auction sale after its confirmation and registration of the Bainama.

14. It is true that the application under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 was filed before the Executing Court without making the deposit as provided in Order XXI, rule 89 of the Code and no application was filed for setting aside the auction sale on the ground of material irregularity or fraud in publishing or conducting the sale as provided in rule 90 thereof. The application was filed by depositing the auction money arid compensation at the rate of 10%.

15. From the affidavit-of-compliance filed by the judgment-debtor before the High Court Division, it appears that the judgment-debtor specifically stated therein that as per the verbal order of the Court, he deposited the entire dues of the Bank amounting to Taka 36,35,550 vide two receipts dated 26-1-2011 and 31-1-2011. Though the High Court Division in its judgment observed that no such order was passed, it merely "asked the parties if amicable settlement is possible", but the parties failed, yet fact remains that the judgment-debtor paid the entire dues of the Bank as borne out from the application filed by the plaintiff-Bank in the Artha Jari Case, on 1-8-2011 wherein it admitted the said fact (the application has been filed with the additional paper book filed by the auction purchaser) and also from the certificate issued by the Assistant General Manager of the plaintiff- Bank on 20-7-2011 (the certificate has been filed with the additional paper book filed by the judgment-debtor). With the affidavit of compliance photostat copies of the two receipts showing the payment of the said amount to the Bank were annexed as annexure- ‘4(1)’ and ‘4(2)’. Besides depositing the entire dues of the Bank, the judgment-debtor also deposited Taka 16,43,000 pursuant to the impugned order dated 29-7-2008, this amount included Taka 3 63 000 being the amount of interest from 7-8-2005 (the date of auction sale) to 7-8-2008 on the bid money of Taka 12,10,000 and other costs of Taka 70,000. Although the auction purchaser filed an application before this Court under the caption: "An application for rejecting the additional paper book" these facts of deposit by the judgment-debtor have not been denied. With the application for rejection of the additional paper book filed by the auction purchaser writ-petitioner, the entire order sheets of the Artha Jari Case have been annexed. 16. Before the Executing Court, the judgment-debtor categorically stated that the value of the auction sold land was Taka 40,00,000. Before this Court in the affidavit-in-reply, it has been specifically stated that the mortgaged land was sold in auction at Taka 12,10,000 which was shockingly low. It further appears that the judgment-debtor took loan of Taka 16,14,000 on 13-4-1995 by mortgaging the auction sold land and the Executing Court in the impugned order clearly stated that the sale of the auction sold land (in the order wrongly written as the suit land) on 7-8-2005, i.e. after 10 years at Taka 12,10,2000 "was definitely not a market price." The Executing Court also believed the judgment-debtor's case that there is a homestead in the auction sold land and except that land he has no land to live in.

17. Mr Mahmudul Islam, by referring to the statements made in the supplementary affidavit filed by the auction purchaser writ-petitioner before the High Court Division as well as the passport of the judgment-debtor annexed to the reply filed by him to the supplementary affidavit of the auction purchaser has submitted that the judgment-debtor permanently resides at village Birbagh Bar, Police Station- Belabo, District-Narsingdi, whereas, the auction sold land is at Gazipur. He, by referring to the same supplementary affidavit has further submitted that from the photographs of the auction sold land taken by the writ-petitioner, it is clear that the auction sold land is a plane (sic) land and "there was no standing on (sic) dwelling house or any shed or any kind of hut on (sic) the mortgage property", but the judgment-debtor falsely claimed that he had homestead on the auction sold land. So, the Executing Court was not correct to show sympathy to the judgment- debtor in setting aside the auction sale on the ground that there was homestead in the auction sold land and except this land, he had no land to live in.

18. Whether there is any homestead in the auction sold land is basically a question of fact. From the impugned order of the Executing Court, it appears that it took notice of the said fact as claimed by the judgment-debtor. The High Court Division in its judgment has not said anything whether there is any homestead in the auction sold land or not. The High Court Division has not also said anything as to the place of the judgment-debtor's permanent residence. But the Executing Court, as it appears from the impugned order, believed the assertion of the judgment-debtor made in the application under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 that there IS a homestead on the auction sold land, and except that land, he has no other land to live in. The judgment-debtor made the same assertion in the affidavit-in-opposition and in the affidavit-in-reply filed in the writ petition. Furthermore, it is very difficult to come to any conclusion as to whether there is any homestead on the auction sold land or not relying on the photograph of the auction sold land allegedly taken by the auction purchaser as submitted by Mr Islam. Mentioning of an address in a passport as permanent address does not disprove the assertion of the judgment-debtor made on oath before the High Court Division that there is a homestead in the auction sold land and he has been living there along with his family members. It further appears from the affidavit-in-reply submit- ted by the judgment-debtor that he categorically stated therein that he was in South Korea from before January, 2003 to August, 2006 as evident from his passport, the ex-parte decree was obtained fraudulently on 9-8-2004 and the auction sale was held on 7-8-2005. In support of the said statements the judgment-debtor filed the photostat copy of the relevant pages of the passport before the High Court Division and we have also perused the same; the passport clearly supports the claim of the judgment-debtor that he was in South Korea from before January, 2003 to August, 2006. The fact, that the judgment- debtor was in South Korea during the said period, has not been denied either by the auction purchaser or by the decree holder-Bank, thus it is clear that the ex-parte decree and the auction sale was passed and held respectively during the absence of the judgment-debtor. It is also a fact that as back as on 29-7-2008 (the impugned order challenged in the writ petition) the Executing Court, in order to compensate the auction purchaser, directed the judgment-debtor to pay Taka 3,63,00,000 as 10% interest on the bid money from the date of auction sale, i.e. on 7-8-2005 to 7-8-2008 and also a cost of Taka 70,000 which the judgment-debtor deposited within 30 days from the date of the said order as evident from Order No. XLI dated 28-8-2008 of the Artha Jari Case. Therefore, it appears to us that the auction purchaser was duly compensated, but he, without accepting the said money, filed the writ petition and fought it and ultimately won through the impugned judgment and order. It will not be out of context to state' that although the sale certificate was issued and the Bainama was registered, the auction purchaser was not put into the possession of the auction soldland and it is the judgment-debtor who is in possession thereof.

19. In the impugned order (dated 29-7-2008), the Executing Court gave specific finding that "perusing the submitted tenders it appears that the auction purchaser collusively submitted bids showing him as a highest bidder in both the auction sale."This. is fundamentally a question of fact and, in fact, it worked very much in the, mind of the Executing Court to set aside the auction sale, but the High Court Division did not say a word about the said finding of the Court. In this regard, it is also very pertinent to-keep in mind that the first auction was held on 14-6-2005 and the same auction purchaser as the highest bidder offered Taka 12,01,000 only, but that auction was cancelled and the second auction was held on 7-8-2005, i.e. after less than 2(two) months and this time also only 3(three) bidders including the auction purchaser participated and the bid offered was Taka 12,10,000 only and this time, the bid was accepted, so when the first auction at Taka 12,01,000 was cancelled presumably for the low offer, how the second auction could be accepted at all enhanced amount to Taka 9000 only. We also find reasonableness and rationalism in the observation of the Executing Court that "judgment-debtor took a loan of Taka 16,14,000 on 13-4-1995 mort- gaging the suit land. Naturally in (sic) can be said that value of the suit land. on 13-4- I 995 was not less than Taka 16,14,000. So sale of the mortgaged 'land on 7-8-2005, i.e. after 10 years at Taka 12,10,000 is definitely nota market price." Considering these facts the Executing Court also gave finding that there was material irregularity in conducting the sale which caused substantial injury to the judgment- debtor-applicant.

20. It is a common' knowledge of our 'country that the price of the land always increases and there is no doubt that in. 10(ten) years, it was multiplied. So, it is ridiculous to accept that the land mortgaged in 1995 against the loan of Taka 16) 4,000 could be sold at Taka 12,10,000 only after 10(ten) years. It also appears irrational to us irrational to accept the bid money at Taka 12,10,000, when the decree was passed for Taka 34,65,690. It may further be stated that the judgment-debtor asserted before the Executing Court that the value of the auction sold land was Taka 40,00,000 (Forty lakh). In the affidavit-in-reply to the supplementary affidavit filed by the writ-petitioner the judgment-debtor also specifically asserted that the mortgaged land was sold .in auction at Taka 12,10,000 which was shockingly low. These assertions of the judgment-debtor as to the claim of the value of the auction sold land were not also denied either by the plaintiff-Bank nor the auction purchaser by filing any affidavit before the High Court Division, The Executing Court took notice of the said assertions of the judgment-debtor.

21, The Executing Court also considered the fact that during the relevant time, the judgment- debtor was in South Korea and came to the finding that "From the copy of the passport it appears that during this whole period the petitioner was in South Korea and, as such, ends of justice would be best meet (sic) if the auction sale is set-aside." We do not find this conclusion of the Executing Court without any basis, because the relevant pages of the passport of ,the judgment-debtor substantiates that he had been in South Korea from before January, 2003 to August, 2006, whereas the ex-parte decree was passed on 9-8-2004 and the auction sale was held on 7-8-2005. The Executing Court also gave finding that there was-material irregularity in conducting the sale which caused substantial injury to the applicant (the judgment-debtor) and such injury was the result of fraud. But while making the Rule Nisi absolute, the High Court Division did not at all consider these factual aspects if the case, and, in fact, it set aside the orders of the Executing Court only on technical point that in view of the specific provisions of the Code in Order XXI, rule 89, the application under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 was not maintainable in law.

22. Be that as it may; considering the facts and circumstances of the case. and the findings of the Executing Court, as discussed hereinbefore, particularly, the following;

(a) the finding of the Executing Court that the auction purchaser submitted the bids collusively showing him as the highest bidder in both the auction sales;

(b) the finding of the Executing Court that there was material irregularity in conducting the sale which caused substantial injury to the applicant (the judgment-debtor) and such injury was the result of fraud;

(c) the finding of the Executing Court that the land which was mortgaged on 13-4-1995 against the loan of Taka 16,14,000 was sold in auction after ten years at Taka 12,10,000 only was "definitely not a market price";

(d) the assertion of the judgment-debtor that there is a homestead in the auction sold land and except this land, he has no land to live in as taken note of by the Executing Court;

(e) though the ex-parte decree was passed for realization of Taka 34,65,690, the mortgaged land was sold at Taka 12,10,000 only;

(f) by the order dated 29-7-2008 (impugned in the writ petition), the Executing Court duly compensated the auction purchaser by giving him interest at the rate of 10% from 7-8-2005 (auction was held on this date) to 7-8-2008 amounting to Taka 3,63,000 on the bid money of Taka 12,10,000 and the cost of Taka 70,000 and pursuantto the said order the judgment-debtor deposited in total Taka 16,43,000 as evident from Order No. XLI dated 28-8-2008 (this fact is not disputed);

(g) the judgment-debtor, besides depositing Taka 16,43,000 also paid the entire dues of the Bank amounting to Taka 36,35,550 during the pendency of the writ petition. The decree-holder-Bank duly received the money deposited by the judgment-debtor and filed application in the Artha Jari Case on 1-8-2011 for disposal of the case as being withdrawn, stating specifically that it had no dues due to the judgment-debtor, the Executing Court accordingly, allowed the prayer by its order dated 12-9-2011.

(The prayer in the application in Bengali reads as follows:

"সে মতে ডিক্রীদার ব্যাকের পক্ষে বিনীত প্রার্থনা এই যে, হুজর দয়া করিয়া চালনের অত্র মামলা না কারনে প্রত্যাহার মূলে নিস্পতির আদেশ দিয়া সুবিচার করিতে আজ্ঞা হয়ঃ)

(h) the Executing Court by its Order No. LIII dated 9-1-2012 allowed the prayer of the

judgment-debtor to return the original deed No. 6227 dated 22-11-1994 and original deed No. 6241 dated 23-11-1994 and the original Nathi of"নামজারী ও জমাভাগঃbeing No. 3162/94-95;

(i) though the sale certificate was issued and the Bainama was registered, possession of the auction sale land has not been delivered to the auction purchaser and it is the judgment- debtor who is in possession thereof.

<u>23. We are of the view that this is a fit case to exercise the power conferred upon this Court under article 104 of the Constitution to do complete justice. In this regard, we may refer the case of M/s Gannysons Ltd and another (supra) as relied upon by Mr Siddique. In that case, this Court exercised the power under article 104 of the Constitution for doing complete justice on the following facts:</u>

"Sonali Bank, respondent No.1, obtained a decree in Title Suit No. 249 of 1976 for foreclosure and sale of the mortgaged properties belonging to the appellant company and put it into execution in Title Execution No. 46 of 1980. Appellant-company appeared before the Court and prayed for staying the execution of the decree on the grounds that since the Bank proceeded against the appellant Company's properties being treated as abandoned by the Government, the Directors of the appellant Company were not properly served with notice and that had, therefore, no knowledge of the aforesaid title suit. As a result they did not appear in the suit. Also the Government which was made a party did not take any steps. However, on the prayer of the appellant Company the proceeding in the execution case was stayed till 20-10-1981. In Writ Petition No. 720 of 1981 a Rule was issued at the instance of the appellant company on October 20, 1981. But it abated on 24-3-1982 after the proclamation of Martial Law. In Miscellaneous Case No. 958 of 1981 which was filed by the appellant Company under section 47 of the Code its prayer against the execution of the decree obtained in-Title Suit No. 249 of 1976 was disallowed by the Court. The appellant Company's appeal against this order was dismissed by the High Court Division on 9 November 1982. The appellant Company, being aggrieved, moved this Court, and, succeeded in having the appeal(Civil Appeal No. 43 of 1983) against the order of the trial Court rejecting their objection under section 47of the Code allowed. Appellants filed review petition against the judgment passed in the civil appeal against the concluding paragraph of the judgment which was as follows:

<u>"Decree dated 27-3-1980 passed by the Subordinate Judge,3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 249 of 1976 be stayed for six months and the Miscellaneous Case No. 958 of 1981 pending in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka be struck down."</u>

24. And leave was granted to consider the only ground to the following effect:

"For that consistently with the reasoning's in the main body of the judgment and the decision allowing the appeal (CA No. 43 of 1983) arising out of Miscellaneous Case No. 958 of 1981 started under section 47CPC (at the instance of M/s Gannysons Ltd.) the Title Execution, Case No. 46 of 1980 pending in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, needs to be struck down and the said Miscellaneous Case No. 958 of 1981 of the same court allowed and that the order staying the decree dated 27-3-1980 in Title Suit No. 279 of 1976 of the 3rd Court of the Subordinate 'Judge needs to be deleted."

<u>25. Considering the definition of abandoned property as given in President's Order No. XVI of 1972, it was found that  Gannysons Limited Company, in no circumstances, could be declared as an abandoned property, allowed the review application, declared that the property was not an abandoned property, struck down the execution case subject to payment of the decretal amount to, the Bank directly by the appellants and directed the Government to release the property treating Title Suit No. 508 of 1982 filed by the appellant as withdrawn being infructuous. In that case, Fazle Munim, CJ observed:</u>

<u>"17. In view of the circumstances above and in virtue of the power conferred upon this Court by the Constitution of Bangladesh, vide Article 104, to do complete justice in a case it is declared that Gannysons Limited is not an abandoned property, it should, therefore, be immediately, released. Along with the release of Gannysons Limited any of its properties, assets and capital should also be released and returned to it."</u>

<u>26. Since we are exercising the power vested in this Court under article 104 of the Constitution for doing complete justice, we are riot at all required to enter into the legal question as to the maintainability of the application filed by the judgment-debtor in the Artha Jari Case under section 57 of the Ain, 2003. The question may be decided in an appropriate case if occasion arises.</u>

27. For the reasons stated above, this petition is disposed of in the following terms:

(a) The order dated 29-7-2008 (impugned in the writ petition) passed by the Joint District Judge, Second Court, Gazipur in Artha Jari Case No. 52 of 2004 is maintained, the judgment and order dated 14-2-2011 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.4 of 2009 is set- aside.

(b) The Joint District Judge, Second Court, Gazipur is directed to pass necessary order/ orders in Artha Jari Case No. 52 of 2004 (though the same was disposed of by Order No. XLV dated 12-9-2011) so that the auction purchaser, namely, Md Asaduzzaman Belal can withdraw/receive Taka 16,43,000 (Sixteen Lakhs Forty Three Thousand) deposited by the judgment-debtor pursuant to the order dated 29-7-2008, passed in the case, if not withdrawn in the meantime.

End.

lawyer:
Md Khaled Ahmed, Advocate -----For the Petitioners. 
Mohammad Noor Hossain, Advocate ----- For Opposite Party Nos. 1 and 2.
parties:
Torab Ali and another Defendant-Respondent -----Petitioners
Vs.
Madris Ali Saha and others -----Opposite-----Parties
full_judgment:
On an application of the petitioner Torab Ali and another under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure without granting leave this court issued Rule calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 15-9-2005 passed by the learned District Judge, Moulvibazar in Civil Revision No. 34 of 2005 affirming the Order dated 24-5-2005 Passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Kulaura, Moulvibazar in Miscellaneous case No. 10 of 2005 arising out of Title Suit No. 153 of 2003 rejecting the Miscellaneous case should not be set-aside.

2. Facts necessary for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 153 of 2003 in the court of Senior assistant Judge, Kulaura, Moulvibazar for declaration of title and ,partition. The summons were duly served upon the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 who subsequently appeared before the court and prayed time for filing written statement which was allowed. But ultimately they did not file written statement and also did not appear before the court. The trial court took up the case for hearing and decreed the suit ex-parte on 8-2-2005.

3. Against the said ex-parte decree the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 filed -application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside the ex-parte decree and thus Miscellaneous Case No. 10 of 2005 was started. The trial court after hearing the parties and considering the facts and circumstances of the case rejected the said application on the ground that the petitioner failed to deposit Taka 2,000 provided under rule 7 of Order 17 of the Cody of Civil Procedure while filing the application against the judgment and Order dated 24-5-2005,

4. Against the said judgment and order of the trial court the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 filed Revisional application No, 34 of 2005 under section 115(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure before the learned District Judge, Moulvibazar, Who after hearing the parties and considering the relevant law rejecting the revisional application on the ground that the petitioner did not fulfill the provision of rule 7 of Order 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure by its judgment and order dated 15-9-2005.

5. Being-aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order of the courts below the petitioner filed this revisional application 'under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure and according by the Rule was issued.

6. Mr Mohammad Noor Hossain, the learned Advocate enter appeared on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 through Vokalatnama to oppose the Rule.

7. Mr Md Khaled Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners argued that both the courts on misconception of the provision of law erroneously rejected the application of the petitioner. He argued that the trial court rejecting the application on the ground that the plaintiff did not deposit Taka 2,000 as per provision of sub-rule 7 of rule 1 of Order XVII of the Code of Civil Procedure without considering that the petitioner did not file application under sub-rule 7 of rule 1 of Order XVII or Order IX, rule 13(a) rather he filed application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate further argued that the learned District Judge also committed error in law while rejecting the revisional application on misconception of provision of law since in the instant case the amendment provision of sub-rule 7 of rule 1 of Order XVII of the Code of Civil Procedure is not at all applicable in the instant case since the trial court did not avail the procedure of sub-rule 3 and 4 of rule 1 of Order XVII so the judgment of the courts below is erroneous one which should be interfered with. He prayed for making the Rule absolute.

8. On the contrary Mr Mohammad Noor Hossain, the .learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 argued that the petitioners as defendants though appeared but without filing written statement trying to delay to proceed the suit even did not take any step for adjornment of the matter thus the trial court rightly took up the case for ex-parte hearing and decreed the suit ex- parte in such a case the newly amendment provision of the Code of Civil Procedure is very much applicable in the instant case and the courts below rightly passed the impugned which should not be interfered with. However, lastly he argued that this court may send back the matter to the trial court to consider the application on merit.

9. I have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the impugned judgment of the courts below, the papers and documents as available on the records. It appears that the opposite party No. 1 and 2 as plaintiffs flied Title Suit No. 153 of 2003 before the Assistant Judge, Kulawara, Moulvibazar for declaration of title and partition. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 appeared before the court and obtained time for filing written statement but ultimately did not file written statement and also did not take any steps to con- test the suit and the trial court took up the case for ex-parte hearing and decreed the suit ex-parte on 8-2-2005 without availing the procedure of rule 1 of order XVII of the Code of Civil Procedure. Against the said ex-parte decree of the trial court the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 filed application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside the ex-parte decree. Which was heard by the trial court and the trial court without going to merit of the case of the petitioners only considering the amendment provision of rule I of order XVII the Code of Civil Procedure opined that since the petitioners without depositing Taka 2,000 as provided under sub-rule 7 of rule 1 of order XVII filed the application which is against the provision of law and rejecting the application. Against which the petitioners filed revisional application before the District Judge, Moulvibazar under section 115(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, who after hearing the parties and con- sidering the procedure of law also rejected the revisional application considering the same view as taken by the trial Court. The appellate court opined to the effect:

“উল্লেখিত বক্তব্যের পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে আমি The Code of Civil Procedure 3rd Amendment, 2003: এর ১৭নং আদেশের ৭নং বিধিটি যত্ন সহকারে পাঠ করিলাম, যাহা নিম্নরূপঃ-

"(7)suit dismissed disposed of ex-parte under sub-rule (3) or (4) shall not be revived for hearing unless the party for whose noncompliance the suit was dismissed or disposed of ex-parte, makes within thirty days of such dismissal or ex-parte disposal, non- application together with cost of two thousand taka into Court for such revival, and upon such application being made the suit shall be revived for hearing without any further proceeding, and cost deposited into Court shall be paid to the other party."

10. বণির্ত আইনের উল্লেখিত বিধি পর্যালোচনা করিয়া দেখা যায় যে, বিবাদী-প্রার্থী পক্ষ আদালতের আদেশ অনুসারে লিখিত জবাব দাখিল করিয়াছিলেননা এবং সেই কারণে বিজ্ঞ আদালত একতরফাভাবে মূল মোকদ্দমাটি নিষ্পত্তি করিয়াছিলেন। সেহেতু বিবাদী প্রার্থীপক্ষ উক্ত আদেশের দ্বারা ক্ষুদ্ধ হইয়া দেওয়ানী কার্যাবিধির ১৭ আদেশের সংশোধিত ৭নং বিধির বিধান অনুসারে ২০০০ টাকা খরচে মূল মোকদ্দমা পুনরূজীবিত করার প্রার্থনা দাখিল করিলে বিজ্ঞ আদালত উক্ত প্রাথর্না মজ্ঞুর করিয়া মূল মোকদ্দমাটি বিধি মোতাবেক পুনরুজীবিত করিতেন। কিন্তু বিবাদী-প্রাথীপক্ষ আইনের উল্লেখিত অবলোকন করিয়া দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধির ৯নং আদেশের ১৩ নং বিধির বিধানানুসারে একতরফা ডিক্রি রদ ও রহিতের প্রার্থনা করিয়া ১০/২০০৫ নং বিবিধ মোকদ্দমা আনয়ন করিয়াছিলেন এবং  সেই কারনেই বিজ্ঞ আদালত সঠিকভাবে উক্ত বিবিধ মোকদ্দমাটি রক্ষণীয় নয় বলিয়া উল্লেখক্রমে আদেশ প্রদান করিয়াছিলেন।

বিজ্ঞ আদালতের তর্কিত আদেশের উপরে হস্তক্ষেপ করার আদৌ কোন কারণ আছে বলিয়া আমি মনে করিনা।

11. I have considered the impugned Judgment and the aforesaid provision of law. It appears that the courts below considering the procedure of rule 1(7) of order XVII of the of the Code of Civil Procedure passed the impugned Judgment but the trial Court without exhausting the procedure of rule 1(3) and 1(4) of Order XVII of new amendment law decreed the suit ex-part.

12. The trial court also without considering the procedure as laid down in the amendment order 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure passed the order. The rule 1 of order XV II, of the Code of Civil Procedure reproduced as under:

Order XVII

(1) The Court may, if sufficient cause is shown, at any stage of the suit grant time to the parties or to any of them, and may from time to time adjourn the hearing of the suit.

(2) In every such case the Court shall fix a day for the further hearing of the suit, and may make such order as it thinks fit with respect to the costs occasioned by the adjournment:

Provided that, when the hearing of evidence has once begun, the hearing of the suit shall be continued from day to day until all the witnesses in attendance have been examined, unless the Court finds the adjournment of the hearing beyond the following day to be necessary for reasons to be recorded.

(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-rules (1) and (2), the Court shall not grant more than six adjournments in a suit before peremptory hearing at the instance of either party to the suit, and any adjournment granted to a party beyond the aforesaid limit shall make such party liable to pay a cost of not less than two hundred taka and not more than one thousand taka to the other party, within time to be specified by it; noncompliance with which, by the plaintiff shall render the suit liable to be dismissed and, by the defendant shall render the suit liable to be dismissed of ex-parte: provided that the Court shall not grant more than three adjournments to a party even with cost under this rule.

(4) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code, the Court shall not grant any adjournment at the peremptory hearing stage and thereafter in a suit at the instance of either party to the suit:

Provided that if for ends of justice any adjournment is granted to a party under this sub-rule, the Court shall direct that party to pay a cost of not less than two hundred taka and not more than one thousand taka to the other party, within time to be specified by it, noncompliance with which, by the plaintiff shall render the suit liable to be dismissed and, by the defendant shall render the suit liable to disposed of ex-parte: Provided further that the Court shall not grant more than three adjournments to a party even with cost under the above proviso.

(5) Where applications are made by both the parties for any adjournment under sub- rule (3) or (4) and the applications are allowed with costs, the Court shall direct each party to pay such cost as revenue to the State.

(6) The Court shall not, of its own, order any adjournment under this rule without recording reasons therefor.

(7) A suit dismissed or disposed of ex- parte under sub-rule (3) or (4) shall not be revived for hearing unless the party, for whose noncompliance the suit was dismissed or disposed of ex-parte, makes within thirty of such dismissal of ex-parte disposal, an application together with cost of two thou- sand taka into Court for such revival; and upon such application being make, the suit shall be revived for hearing without any further proceeding; and cost deposited into Court shall be paid to the other party.

<u>13. In the aforesaid procedure it is clearly provides that if any case decreed ex-parte on failure of the parties for noncompliance of the procedure of sub-rule 3 or 4 of rule 1 of order XVII only then the question of setting aside the ex-parte decree under sub-rule 7 of rule 1 of order XVII is applicable. But it appears that without prevailing the aforesaid procedure the trial court decreed the suit ex-parte. In such a case no scope to file application under sub-rule 7 of rule 1 of order XVII and the defendants Tightly filed the application under rule 13 of order IX of the code of civil procedure, as such the findings of the courts below is erroneous one. Even the procedure of Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure has not been repealed, so, the Petitioner has every right to invoke the said jurisdiction.</u>

14. Order IX, rule 13 provides that if he satisfies the Court that the Summons was not duly served, or that he was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing the Court shall, make an order setting aside the decree as against him upon such terms as to costs, payment into Court or otherwise as it thinks fit. So in such a case the Court shall consider the application of the petitioner as provided under the provision of Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure but erroneously passed the impugned Judgment considering the procedure of rule .1 of order XVII of the Code of Civil Procedure which they committed serious error in law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of Justice,

15. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and the discussions made above I find merit in the Rule.

16. Accordingly, the Leave is granted arid the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and order dated IS-9-200S passed by the learned District Judge, Moulvibazar in Civil Revision No. 34 of 2005 affirming the Judgment and order dated 24-5-200S passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Kulaura, Moulvibazar in Miscellaneous case No. 10 of 2005 arising out of Title Suit No153 of 2003 are hereby set-aside, however, with- out any order as to cost.

17. The trial court is directed to dispose of the Miscellaneous Case No. 10 of 2005 filed under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure on merit considering the discussions as made above.

18. Since this is a long pending case, the trial court is directed to dispose of the Miscellaneous case No-10 of 2005 as early as possible preferable within 4 (four) months from the date of receipt of the judgment.

19. The order of stay granted earlier by this court is hereby recalled and vacated.

Send down the Lower Court's Records at once.

End.

lawyer:
Quayyum Chowdhury, Advocate -----For the Petitioner. 
Shamim Khaled Ahmed with Abdun Noor Advocates -----For the Respondent No.4.
Mahbubey A lam, Senior Advocate with S Rashed Jahangir and Harunur Rashid, Advocates ----- For the Respondent No.5.
parties:
Mukleshur Rahman (Md) ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj and others -----Respondents
full_judgment:
Mahmudul Hoque J: In this application under Article 102(2) of the Constitution of Bangladesh, this Rule Nisi has been issued at the instance of the Petitioner calling upon the Respondents to show cause as to why the Order No. 50 dated 26-4-2007 passed by the Judge of Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj, in Artha Rin Suit No.1 of 2005 directing the Respondent No.4 to execute and register the mortgaged property within 10(ten) days from 26-4-2007 should not be declared to be without lawful authority and for pass such other or further order or orders as to this

Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts necessary for disposal of this Rule, in brief, are that the City Bank Limited, Respondent No.4, at the request of one Anil Kumar Shaha Proprietor of M/S Balaka Bostra Bitan granted loan to the tune of Taka 50,00,000. The Petitioner, being a co-sharer in the property, at the request of said Anil Kumar Shaha mortgaged his portion of the said property as security against the loan granted by the Bank as 3rd party mortgagor. Subsequently, the said limit was enhanced by the Bank to the tune of Taka 1,75,00,000 and for the enhanced facility, the Respondent No.5, SM Arif mortgaged the property owned by him as 3rd part mortgagor. The borrower having failed to liquidate the said facility to the Bank as per terms and conditions of the sanction letter, the Bank published a notice under section 12(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 ("Ain") to sell the mortgaged property by auction: Challenging the said auction notice published by the Bank, the Petitioner and the Respondent No.5 filed Writ Petition Nos. 995 of 2004 and 7506 of 2003 respectively and obtained Rules and Orders of Stay. The said Writ Petitions were disposed of with direction to sell the property of the borrower first.

3. In the auction held before filing of the Writ Petition No. 995 of 2004 in respect of the property mortgaged by the borrower and the Petitioner, the quoted price was found at Taka 48,16,000. After disposal of the said Writ Petitions, the Respondent Bank proposed the highest bidder to purchase 8 decimals of land mortgaged by the borrower Anil Kumar at the price of Taka 24,08,000, but the highest bidder did not come forward to purchase the said property as it was not partitioned. Thereafter, the Bank offered the property to Respondent No.5 at the price quoted by the highest bidder. The Respondent No.5 by a letter though expressed his willingness to purchase the said property at the quoted price, but ultimately failed to deposit the price money to the Bank in spite of repeated call by the Bank. As a result of which the Respondent No.4 Bank instituted Artha Rin Suit No.1 of 2005 in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj for recovery of the Bank dues against the borrower and the mortgagors. The said Suit was decreed on contest by Judgment and Decree dated 8-4-2007.

4. After passing the decree, the Petitioner filed an application on 23-4-2007 before the Respondent No.4 Bank requesting them to sell the aforesaid 8 decimals land owned by Anil Kumar to him as co-sharer of the plot and possessing the same jointly and to receive the proportionate amount of decretal money from the Petitioner. But the Respondent No.4 Bank did not allow the Petitioner to purchase the property at the quoted price. Subsequently, the Respondent No.5 at the back of the Petitioner filed an application in the trial Court on 26-4-2007 without serving any copy to the Petitioner praying for a direction upon the Decree holder Bank to sell the property to his representative named Khairunnessa at the quoted price found in the auction held under section 12(3) of the Ain before filing of the Suit. The trial Court allowed the same by the Impugned Order dated 26-4-2007 directing the Bank to execute and register the kabala in favour of one Khairunnessa within 10 days of the Order and to deliver possession of the mortgaged property to the said purchaser. At this stage, the Petitioner being aggrieved by the said Order, moved this Court by filing this application under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule and Order of Stay.

5. The Respondent No. 4 Bank and Respondent No. 5 contested the Rule by filing separate Affidavits-in-Opposition denying all the material allegations made in the application. The Respondent No.4 Bank contended that the Court below failed to consider that, after pronouncement of the Judgment and drawing up of the decree, it has become functus officio and yet, it most arbitrarily passed the Impugned Order allowing the application filed by the Respondent No.5. It is also stated that the Artha Rin Adalat committed gross illegality in allowing the application filed by the Defendant Respondent No.5 directing the Decree holder Bank to sell the mortgaged property in question to the representative of Respondent No. 5 within 10 (ten) days. The Respondent Bank did not agree to sell the mortgaged property at the price offered by Defendant Respondent No.5 and the Petitioner, because none of the guarantors have had any right to purchase the mortgaged property at the price quoted in the auction held under section 12(3) of the Ain. Further case of the Respondent No.4 are that the Court has had no jurisdiction to pass any order after pronouncement of the Judgment and Decree unless an execution case is filed by the Decree holder Bank for recovery of the money from the Judgment-Debtors by selling the mortgaged property through auction under section 33 of the Ain and, as such the Impugned Order is palpably illegal and passed without jurisdiction.

6. The Respondent No.5 contended that the Petitioner neither owner of the property in question nor any property owned by him was directed to be sold and, as such the Petitioner is not an aggrieved person within the meaning of Article 102 of the Constitution and, as such the writ petition is not maintainable in law, rather it has been filed with an ulterior motive to harass Respondent No. 5 and his representative, The Respondent No. 4 Bank accepted the decree passed in Artha Rin Suit No.1 of 2005 and put the said decree in execution by filing Execution Case No. 32 of 2007 for recovery of the decretal money and, as such by the Impugned Order, the Decree- holder Bank has not in any way prejudiced. It is also stated that the Artha Rin Adalat passed the Impugned Order keeping conformity with the decree passed by it, hence there is no illegality in the Impugned Order and, by' the said order the Petitioner as well as the Decree-holder Bank had nothing to lose. Further case of the Respondent No.5 are that, after holding auction under section 12(3) of the Ain, the Bank offered 8 decimals of land owned by Anil Kumar to the highest bidder at the price quoted by him but the highest bidder did not come forward to accept proposal of the Bank as the property offered to him are joint property,

7. Thereafter, the Bank proposed the Petitioner to purchase the property at the price quoted in the auction, but' the Petitioner did not come forward to accept the proposal of the Bank. Subsequently, the Bank proposed to Respondent No.5 to purchase the property in question at the price quoted by the highest bidder. The Respondent No. 5 expressed his willingness to purchase the property, but the Bank at a point of time did not come forward to materialize the proposal made by it and filed the Suit before the Artha Rin Adalat against the borrower, present Petitioner and the Respondent No.5. The said Suit was decreed and the Artha Rin Adalat, in its judgment, specifically observed that the property was offered to the Respondent No.5 by the Bank at the price quoted by the highest bidder and the Respondent No.5 expressed his willingness to purchase the property. In this situation, Respondent No.5 filed an application before the Artha Rin Adalat on 26-4-2007 praying for a direction upon the Bank to execute a kabala and register the same in favour of the representative of the Respondent No.5 namely, Khairunnessa.

8. The trial Court allowed the said application and directed Respondent No.4 Bank to execute and register the sale deed in favour of said Khairunnessa. But the Bank failed to comply with the order passed by the Court. Consequently, the Court executed a deed of sale and registered the same in favour of Respondent No. 5's representative and delivered possession of the property to her and, as such the Court below committee no illegality, and did nothing detrimental to the interest of the Petitioner and the Decree holder Bank: Therefore, the Rule is liable to be discharged.

9. Mr MA Quayyum Chowdhury, the learned advocate appearing for the Petitioner submits that the, trial Court, after pronouncement of the judgment and drawing up the decree has become functus officio and, as such the trial Court cannot pass any order in the said proceeding giving any relief to any party to the suit. However, in the instant case, the Artha Rin Adalat not only reopened the- proceeding afresh, but also gave relief to the, Judgment Debtor who is not the beneficiary, of the decree. He also submits that after passing the decree, the trial Court cannot pass any order except correction of clerical or are thmatical error in the decree passed. It is also argued that unless an execution case is filed by the Decree holder to execute decree, the Court has no jurisdiction and or authority to pass any order in aid of the Decree holder or the Judgment Debtor.
