To establish such claim as to date of knowledge, the defendant has introduced the fact that the defendant was not aware about the ex-parte decree and for the first time it came to know about the said decree on 13- 5-2008 and from the said date of knowledge within 30 days the defendant filed the miscellaneous case (application) for setting aside the ex-parte decree as per sanction of second part of section 19(2) of the Ain. Since the defendant claims that the application has been filed within 30 days from the date of knowledge, therefore, the Adalat has to be satisfied about the said date of knowledge by a proper and fair adjudication, giving an opportunity of being heard to both the plaintiff and the defendant so as to determine the correctness/genuineness of alleged date of knowledge.

<u>26. But from the impugned order dated 15-7- 2008, it appears that without being satisfied about correctness/genuineness of the alleged date of knowledge, the Adalat allowed the miscellaneous case finding deposit of 10% of the decretal dues which is one of the requirements to file and consider the application for setting-aside the ex-parte decree as per section 19 of the Ain inasmuch as, unless the other requirement as to limitation under section 19(2) of the Ain is complied with, the Adalat has no scope to allow the said application, irrespective of the fact that the defendant deposited 10% of the decretal dues.</u>

27. In view of the above discussions, we have no hesitation to hold that the Adalat passed the impugned order dated 15-7-2008 without satisfying itself as to requirement of section 19(2) of the Ain and, as such, it warrants interference of this Court. Thus, we find merit in part of the Rule.

28. By the order dated 4-3-2009 passed in Artha Rin Suit No. 174 of 2006, the Adalat rejected petitioner's misconceived application on point of maintainability as it was filed under section 57 of the Ain for setting aside the order dated 15-7- 2008. This order dated 4-3-2009 being rejected on maintainability, has no effect over the main issue of this Rule and, as such, it is not necessary to give any decision on this issue.

29. In the result, the Rule is made absolute in part without any order as to costs. The impugned order dated 15-7-2008 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No.3, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 668 of 2008 is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. The Adalat is directed to dispose of the Miscellaneous Case No. 668 of 2008 in the light of the observation as made above.

Communicate the judgment and order to the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 expeditiously for taking necessary steps as per observations of the judgment.

End.

Abdul Quayum, Advocate with Md Harun-ur-Rashid, Advocate ----- For the Decree-Holder-Petitioner. 
Ramzan Ali Sikder, Advocate ----- For the Judgment-Debtor-Opposite Parties.

Sunny Fish Agency and Trading ------ Decree-Holder-Petitioner

Bangladesh Catfish Ltd and others ------ Debtor-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: This rule, at the instance of decree-holder, directed against judgment and order dated 18-10-2012 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna deducting the amount of vat and income tax from decree finally passed in Money Suit No. 16 of 2004.

2. Petitioner as plaintiff filed Money Suit No. 16 of 2004 for realization of Taka 6,18,57,952 with 16% interest till realization of the said amount. Upon contested hearing the suit was decreed on 16-5-2005 in the following manner i.e. the suit be decreed for Taka 2,47,50,109.60 against defendant No.2, Taka 4,62,74,473 against defendant No.3 and Taka 16,27,884.96 against defendant No.4, totaling, Taka 8,60,52,496.56, against the aforesaid defendants individually. First Appeal No. 53 of 2006 and First Appeal No. 95 of 2006 were filed before the High Court Division by judgment and decree dated 9-6-2008 heard both the appeals analogously and modified the decree and set-aside the judgment and decree of the learned Joint District Judge so far as it relates to passing decree against defendant No.2 at Taka 1,87,50,105 from Taka 2,47,50,138.60, against defendant No.3, Taka 3,50,56,419 in place- of 4,62,74,473 against defendant No.4, Taka 80,51428 in place of 16,27,884.96 totaling Taka 6,18,57,952 in place of 8,16,52,496.56. Judgment-debtors Nos. 2-4 as petitioner filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2495 of 2009 against the said judgment and order dated 9- 6-2008 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 59 of 2006 on 30-5-2010. The Appellate Division by judgment and order, after hearing the parties, dismissed the Civil Petition, affirming the judgment of the High Court Division. Decree-holder-petitioner filed Money Execution Case No.2 of 2006 for realization of decreetal amount on 29-1-2006. At the time of final decision of the matter, the judgment-debtor filed application praying for deduction of vat and income tax amount from decreetal amount. Learned Judge by judgment and order allowed the application of defendant and decree was modified from Taka 12,27,46,164 to 11,18,62,352 deducting Taka 1,08,83,812 from the aforesaid amount as vat and income tax.

3. Mr Abdul Quayurn with Mr Md Harun-ur-Rashid, learned Advocates, appearing for the decree-holder-petitioner, submits that, executing court has no jurisdiction to modify the decree finally drawn up as law did not permit to pass order frustrating the decree. Learned Advocate further submits that executing court committed an error of law in failing to appreciate that there was no such obligation upon the decree holder to pay the income tax and Vat upon the decreetal amount nor it is the requirement of any law that the judgment debtor will pay the income tax and VAT upon the decreetal amount on behalf of the decree-holder.

4. Mr Ramzan Ali Sikder, learned Advocate, appearing for the judgment debtor-opposite parties, on reference to Income Tax Manual, Part-I section 52 submits that, law permit defendant judgment-debtor to deduct the amount of income tax and VAT and can pay the amount, and after deducting the amount the judgment-debtor or defendant can pay to the decree holder the balance money to satisfy the decree. Learned Advocate relied on the case of Maksud Ali vs Eskandar Ali 28 DLR (AD) 99 and also a decision from Indian jurisdiction, made in the case of Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd. vs RS Avtar Singh &Co by the Supreme Court of India in Civil Appeal No. 7239 of 2012. In Bangladeshi decision leave was granted to consider in absence of any direction in the decree itself requiring the Court to take steps for obtaining income tax clearance on behalf of the judgment debtors for the purpose of registration of the document, the Executing Court is not competent to take such steps.

5.	In the Indian decision it has decided as:-

"An amount was to be adjusted strictly in accordance with the directions contained in the decree and in the absence of such directions adjustments be made firstly towards payment of interest and cost and thereafter towards payment of the principal amount subject, of course, to any agreement between the parties.

6.	Thereafter, when the Execution Petition No. 208 of 2000 was moved, the appellant took notice and filed application under section 47 of the CPC in EA 522 of 2000 and another application under Order XXI, Rule 26 in application EA 523 of 2000. The learned Single Judge of the Execution Court while granting time for final reply, in the EA 522 of 2000 and 523 of 2000 and rejoinder, if any, before the next date of hearing by order dated 30-1-2001 directed the appellant to deposit in Court a cheque for Rs 1,94,91,077 being the admitted amount in favour of the respondent subject to deduction of tax at source along with TDS certificate. The execution of the warrant of payment issued on 18-10-2000 was directed to be kept in abeyance. The sum of Taka 1,74,93,835 after deduction of tax at source in a sum of Rs 19,97,192 in all a sum of Rs 1,94,91,077 was realized by the respondent with an undertaking of the respondent that in case the Execution Petition found to be not maintainable, he would refund the amount of Rs 1,74,93,835 within a period of four weeks from the date of the order passed under the Execution Petition. The said order was passed on 30-1-2001 by the learned Single Judge by filing an undertaking dated 5-2-2001, the respondent also withdrew the sum of Rs 1,74,93,885. Ultimately the execution was ordered by the learned Single Judge by an order dated 12-7-2002 by calculating subsequent interest only in the remaining principal amount and dismissed the objection petition.

7. When the appellant preferred this appeal against the said order dated 12-7-2002, in EFA (OS) No. 9/2002, an interim order came to be passed on 23-8-2002 directing the appellant to deposit whatever balance amount due after deduction of TDS as per the final order passed by the learned Judge with a further order to realize the said sum subject to restitution and on furnishing security to the satisfaction of the Register."

8. Let us now go through the relevant laws to find whether the executing court can deduct the amount from decree.

9. Before making any comment on law the fact is that defendant against the decree went up to the Appellate Division and it appears nowhere defendant claimed for such deduction. This claim has been raised after decree was finally drawn up, sealed and signed.

<u>10. Now, we refer to the law. Rule 16 of Income Tax Manual part-I and-II and section 52 of Income Tax Manual runs as follows:-</u>

<u>Deduction of tax from payment to contractors, etc:-For the purpose of making a deduction of tax under section 52, persons responsible for making any payment (including a payment by way of an advance) to any other person (including a company, firm, association or Hindu undivided family) on account of supply of goods or execution of a contract to or with the Government or any authority, corporation or body, including its units, the activities or the principal activities of which are authorized by any Act, Ordinance, order of instrument having the force of law in Bangladesh, or any company as defined in clause (20) of section 2 of the Ordinance or any banking company, or any insurance company or any cooperative bank established by or under any law for the time being in force or any Non-government Organization registered with NGO Affairs Bureau or any university or medical college or dental college or engineering college, shall deduct an amount calculated on the payment made at the rates laid down in the Schedule below:</u>

<u>Provided that the tax to be deducted or collected at the time of making payment shall be according to the rates applicable appropriate to the slab of total payments in case the payments are made in part in any financial year:</u>

<u>Provided further that where the Board gives a certificate in writing on the application of any assesse or class of assesses that total income of such assesse or class of assesses who is a recipient of any of any payment will be less than the minimum liable to tax or will be liable to a rate of tax less than the rate specified in the rule, the person responsible for paying any amount on account of the supply of goods or execution of contract shall, unless such certificate is cancelled by the Board pay the amount without deduction or deduct the tax at a rate less than the rate specified in this rule:</u>

<u>Provided further that where the Board gives a permission in writing on the application of any person responsible for paying any amount on account of the supply of goods or execution of contract under any foreign aided project in Bangladesh, full payment of the bill may be made on production of the copy of challan as proof of payment of tax deductible from such bill."</u>

<u>11. Rule 16 of Income Tax Rule, 1984 is as follows:-</u>

<u>Deduction from payment to contractors. etc:-(1) Where any payment is to be made, whether in full or part, or by way of any advance, on account of indenting commission or shipping agency commission or supply of goods or execution of contract or sub-contract or local letter of credit (LlC) to any such person or class of persons as may be prescribed, the person responsible for making the payment shall at the time of making such payment deduct tax on the amount so payable at such rate as may be prescribed.</u>

<u>(2) Any amount deducted under sub-section (1) shall be deemed to be an advance payment of tax by the payee and shall be given credit for in the assessment of his tax.</u>

12. On a reading of these two laws upon which learned Advocate Mr Ramzan Ali Sikder give much emphasis, we are of the view that these laws relating to the assessee who pay the assessed amount himself, these two laws have no implication or nexus with the payment of money decreed which is between two individuals. Such deduction of amount can be made before filing of the suit or during continuation of the suit, even after judgment but before decree being finally drawn up, not after signed and sealed. Even the defendant could pray for set off instead on paying the defendant amount himself. Learned Judge of the 1st appellate court failed to consider that such deduction amount from the decree finally passed is in gross violation of Order XX, Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the case of Motilal, Banker vs Maharaj Kumar Mahmood Hasan Khan, AIR 1968 SC 1087 it is held "Order XX, Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not affect the executing court to record and enforce the compromise. Order XX, Rule 3 provides that a judgment once signed cannot afterwards be amended or altered save as provided by section 152 or on review. The parties cannot by an agreement confer upon the court the power to amend the decree in contravention of Order XX, Rule 3, or the power to enforce the amended shows that after the passing of the decree the court may order that payment of such terms as to payment of interest as it thinks fit. The two provisions read together show that a direction for postponement of payment of the decretal amount upon the term that the judgment-debtor should pay a reasonable rate of interest is not an alteration of, or addition to the decree."

<u>13. Decree is divine sacred and holy which cannot be altered, varied, modified and amended by the same court at the wish of anyone.</u>

14. From the aforesaid discussion it can safely said that these two laws are applicable when the matter has not been gone to the court and decree has not been drawn up. In the case before our hand the decree as drawn up was maintain up to the Appellate Division.

15. Considering all these aspects of the case, we find substance in the rule.

16. In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs.

17. The judgment complained is set-aside. Communicate this judgment at once.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2125 of 2010.
lawyer:
Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate instructed by Nurul Islam Bhuiyan Advocate-on-Record -----For the Petitioners.
Harun-or-Rashid, Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ----- For Respondent Nos. 6-9.
Hosne Ara Begum, Advocate, instructed by Chowdhury Md Zahangir, Advocate-on-Record ----- For Respondent No.4. 
None represented ----- For Respondent Nos.1-3 & 5.
parties:
Moklesur Rahman (Md) and another ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the order dated the 18th day of July, 2010 and the 18th day of August, 2010 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition NO. 878 of 2010).
full_judgment:
Md Abdul Wahhab Miah J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the two orders one dated the 18th day of July, 2010 rejecting the application filed by the petitioners for modification oftheth0rder dated 17-2-2010 and the other dated the 18th day of August, 2010 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.878 of 2010 making the writ petition out of list.

2. Facts giving rise to this leave petition are that the present petitioners (hereinafter referred to as the writ-petitioners) filed the writ petition before the High Court Division impugning the order dated 14-1-2010 passed by Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka in Artha Rin Execution Case No.560 of 2004 rejecting the application filed by them under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (the Ain, 2003) for setting-aside the auction sale of the mortgaged property held on 6-10-2009 and confirming the auction sale. In the writ petition, it was stated, inter alia, that respondent No.4, Janata Bank Limited, Armanitolla Branch, Dhaka as the plaintiff (hereinafter referred to as the decree-holder-Bank) filed Artha Rin Suit No.304 of 2003 in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka (the Artha Rin Adalat) impleading the writ-petitioners as defendants on the averments that on the prayer of writ-petitioner No.1, the decree-holder-Bank sanctioned Taka 5,00,000 as CC Hipo Loan in favour of M/s. Shabuz Medical Hall of which writ-petitioner No.1 is the proprietor. Writ-petitioner No.1 executed all necessary documents in favour of the decree-holder- Bank and enjoyed the benefit of the loan. The property of one Shahidul Islam was mortgaged with the decree-holder-Bank as security of the loan. Writ-petitioner No.1, the loanee became defaulter and in spite of several reminders did not repay the loan amount and by lapse of time the dues stood at Taka 28,59,333 as on 27-4-2003 including the interest and for realizing the same, the suit was instituted. To the four comer of the plaint, nothing was stated in respect of writ-petitioner No.2 and no statement was made as to why she was impleaded as defendant in the suit. Writ- petitioner No.2 has no connection with the business of writ-petitioner No.1, the proprietor of Shabuj Medical Hall, in whose favour loan was sanctioned. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 6-5-2004 and the decree was drawn and signed on 23- 5-2004. The decree-holder-Bank levied Artha Rin Execution Case No.560 of 2004 for realization of Taka 35,61,331 as decretal amount including cost and interest, which was registered on 28-10-2004. Earlier the writ-petitioners filed Writ Petition No.8139 of 2009 against the order dated 19-9-2005 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat issuing warrant of arrest to detain them in Civil Jail in which Rule was issued and operation of the order dated 19-9-2005 was stayed, subsequently, the Rule was discharged for default. The writ-petitioners filed application to the Manager of the decree-holder-Bank for exemption of interest by depositing 10% interest of the decretal amount. The Board of Directors of the Bank considering the application in its 91st General meeting exempted "94.30% Ararpitoka" interest and the said fact was intimated to them by the Manager of the decree-holder- Bank by letter dated 31-6-2009. It was further intimated that the writ-petitioners should make payment of Taka 26,10,546 (Taka twenty six lakh, ten thousand and five hundred forty six) only within 31-11-2009 by 6(six) installments. Pursuant to the letter dated 31-6-2009, the writ-petitioners paid Taka 2,00,000 and 20,000 on 30- 7-2009 and 1-10-2009 respectively by pay slip. On 6-10-2009, the date was fixed for auction of the mortgaged property. On this date, the writ-petitioners submitted an application praying for time stating that they have already paid some amount of money and they needed some more time to pay the rest amount. The Bank also filed application for time to inform the Court in that respect. The Artha Rin Adalat after hearing the application by its order of the same date (6-10- 2009) rejected the application; challenging this order, the writ-petitioners filed Writ Petition No. 6770 of2009. A Division Bench of the High Court Division by order dated 19-10-2009 stayed operation of the order 30-11-2009 and also directed the decree-holder-Bank to receive the decretal amount. In pursuance of the order dated 19-11- 2009, in Writ Petition No.6770 of 2009, the writ- petitioners submitted application to the decree-holder-Bank on 3-12-2006 and 6-12-2006 respectively for accepting the amount fixed by it, but writ-respondent No. 3 (Janata Bank, represented by its Managing Director) did not respond to the same till the filing of the instant writ petition. Thereafter, on 14-1-2010, the execution case was fixed for hearing. In the meantime, the writ-petitioners filed an application under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 for setting-aside the auction sale held on 6-10-2009 and for permitting them to make payment as per the claim of the decree-holder- Bank. The Artha Rin Adalat after hearing the application by its order dated 14-1-2010 rejected the same and hence the writ-petitioners filed the instant writ petition.

3. A Division Bench of the High Court Division on hearing the writ petition issued Rule on 17-2-2010 in the following terms:

"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondent(sic) to show cause as to why the impugned Order dated 14-1-2010 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No.1 Dhaka in Artha Execution case No.560 of 2004 rejecting the application under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 and confirming the auction of the mortgaged property (annexure-J) shall not be directed (sic) to have been issued without lawful authority and is of legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper."

4. The High Court Division while issuing the Rule also passed an interim order as under:

"Pending hearing in the Rule, the operation of the impugned order dated 14-1-2010 passed by the respondent No.3 in Artha Rin Execution Case No.560 of 2004 is stayed for a period of 6(six) months from date.

The petitioner is directed to pay entire claim amount within 6(six) months failing which the Rule shall stand discharged. The petitioner is directed to file an affidavit-of- compliance from time to time."

5. It further appears that respondent Nos.6- 9 herein filed an application in the writ petition for adding them as respondents claiming that they purchased the mortgaged property in auction sale held on 6-10-2009 and deposited the entire auction money with poundage fee in the executing Court in favour of the decree-holder-Bank in the execution case. Their application was allowed and they were added as respondent Nos.6-9 in the writ petition by order dated 27-4-2010. It further appears that an application was filed by the writ- petitioners to modify the order dated 17-2-2010 and the High Court Division by order dated 18-7- 2010 rejected the application. Then on 18-8-2010, the writ petition appeared in the list, but the same was made out of list. In the leave petition, both these orders have been impugned as stated at the beginning.

6. Similar facts as stated in the writ petition have been stated in the leave petition.

7. From the facts as noted hereinbefore, it is clear that the writ-petitioners failed to make payment of the dues of the decree-holder-Bank pursuant to the interim order passed by the High Court Division at the time of issuance of the Rule in Writ Petition No.878 of2010 and their application for modification was also rejected and in the meantime, the Rule stood discharged on 17-8- 2010 because of the default order passed on 17-2- 2010. In the above backdrop, the writ-petitioners filed Civil Miscellaneous Petition (CMP) for Leave to Appeal No.745 of 2010 before this Division on 22-8-2010 impugning the order dated 19-8-2010 passed by the High Court Division in the writ petition, though, in fact, no order was passed on 19-8-2010 therein. The cause title of the CMP is as follows:

"Judgment and order dated 19-8-2010 passed by a Division Bench of the Hon'ble Court Division in Writ Petition No.878 of 2010 who discharged the Rule and vacated the order of stay as granted at the time of issuance of the Rule."

8. In the CMP, the petitioners filed an application praying for staying operation of the judgment and order dated 19-8-2010 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.878 of 2010 (though no order was passed in the writ petition on that date) and the learned vacation Judge on 30-8-2010 passed the following order:

"Heard the learned Counsel and perused the application for stay. The respondent No.3 Janata Bank is directed to accept the pay order NO.0338020 for Taka '11,10,546 and pay order No. 033- 7070 for Taka 15,00,000 forthwith and intimate the petitioners-judgment-debtor the rest of decreetal dues immediately. The operation of the impugned judgment and order dated 19th August, 20 10 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.878 of 2010 be stayed till 3rd October, 2010 subject to payment of the rest of the decreetal dues, failing which, the order of stay shall stand vacated," 9. It further appears that the order of stay passed by the learned vacation Judge was extend- ed by the learned Judge-in-Chamber on 13-10- 2010 till 27-1-2011 and the leave petition was fixed for hearing on that date. Then again the order of stay was extended till hearing of the leave petition by order dated 24-1-2011.

10. Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioners, has sub- mitted that pursuant to the order passed by the learned vacation Judge on 30-8-2010, the decree- holder-Bank accepted the two pay orders as mentioned in the said order, i.e. for Taka 11,10,546 and Taka 15,00,000, i.e. in total Taka 26,10,546. Mr Bhuiyan has produced the photostat copies of these two pay orders which show that those were issued on 23-8-2010 and 3-8-2010 respectively. Mr Bhuiyan to show that these two pay orders have been accepted by the decree-holder-Bank, has drawn out attention at pages 174 and 175 of the paper book. From page 174, it appears that an officer or the decree-holder-Bank, accepted the two pay orders (amount already mentioned earlier) by making an endorsement on 29-9-2010 on the last page-of the application filed by Mr AKM Shahidul Huq, Advocate-on-Record (as then he was) on behalf of the petitioners. The said application was addressed to the Manager, Janata Bank, Armanitolla Branch, i.e. the decree-holder-Bank requesting him to pay "due respect to the order" of the learned vacation Judge and intimate his client about his conduct in that respect within 7(seven) days from the date of receipt of the application. In this application, the full context of the order passed by the learned vacation Judge in the CMP as quoted hereinbefore was mentioned. From the endorsement made by the officer of the Bank, it further appears that the request was made to the petitioners to pay Taka 19,80,787 within the time fixed pursuant to the order of this Division. The said endorsement reads as follows:

“বর্ণিত দুইটি-পে-অর্ডার গ্রহণ করা হইল। মাহামান্য সুপ্রিম কোর্টের আপীলেট ডিভিশনের সংশ্লিষ্ট আদেশ মোতাবেক Decreetal dues-19,80,787/- (ঊনিশ লক্ষ আশি হাজার সাতশত সাতাশি) টাকা নির্ধারিত সময়ের মধ্যে পরিশোধ করার অনুরোধ করা যাইতেছে।

স্বাক্ষর/অস্পষ্ট

২৯-৯-২০১০ইং

সময়ঃ ১২.৩৫(পি এম)

11. From page 175 of the paper book, it also appears that the decree-holder-Bank credited the amount paid by the said two pay orders in the account of M/s Shabuj Medical Hall on 07-10- 2010 vide deposit slip No. 352 and CDD 274263. It further appears that earlier the writ-petitioners paid to the decree-holder-Bank Taka 2,00,000 (two lakh) and 20,000 (twenty thousand) on 30-7- 2009 and 1-10-2009 respectively and thus the writ-petitioners have paid in total Taka 28,30,546.

12. From the plaint, it appears that the decree-holder-Bank filed the suit for realization of a sum of Taka 28,59,338 and the suit was decreed ex-part for the said amount directing the defendants to pay the same within sixty days along with interest from the date of institution of the suit in 2003. From the execution case filed before the Artha Rin Adalat, it appears that the same was filed on 28-10-2004 for realization of the amount of Taka 35,61,331. It further appears that the mortgaged property was sold in auction on 6-10- 2009 at Taka 45,10,000 only and the auction purchasers, respondent Nos.6-9 herein, already deposited the entire bid money.

13. Mr Bhuiyan has submitted that since the judgment-debtor-petitioners have already paid the entire decretal amount pursuant to the order passed by this Court, the order of default passed by the High Court Division while issuing the Rule, may be set-aside; the Rule may be restored to its file and number and the writ petition may be sent back on remand to the High Court Division for hearing on merit or in the alternative, the writ petition may be disposed of finally by this Court invoking the power vested in it under article 104 of the Constitution for doing complete justice in a case.

14. Mr Harun-or-Rashid, learned Advocate, entering caveat on behalf of the auction-purchaser-respondents, on the other hand, has submitted that the auction purchasers purchased the mortgaged property in question bonafide as the highest bidder at Taka 45,10,000 and they have already paid the entire bid money. So they should not suffer for the default of the judgment-debtor-petitioners in paying the decretal dues leading to the auction sale of the mortgaged property. He has submitted that besides paying the bid money, the auction purchasers have also paid Taka 1,35,300 as stamp duty and Taka 45,120 as poundage fee. He has further submitted that the auction purchasers also incurred expenses on other counts such as:

1.	Tk.35,000 for advocate and clerk fee in the trial Court

2.	Tk.40,000 for miscellaneous expenditure in the trial court

3.	Tk.50,000 for advocate fee in two writ petitions.

4.	Tk.50,000 for advocate fee in the Appellate Division, i.e. in total Tk.l,75,000

15. He has further submitted that since the judgment-debtor-petitioners failed to pay the decretal amount along with the interest as was directed by the trial Court and in the meantime, the mortgaged property has already been sold in auction and the Rule issued in the writ petition stood discharged, the question of sending the writ petition back on remand to the High Court Division for hearing on merit and also setting aside the auction sale does not arise at all and for similar reason the power vested in this Court under article 104 of the Constitution for doing complete justice should not be invoked.

16. Mrs Hosne Ara Begum, learned Advocate, appearing for the decree-holder-Bank, has echoed the submissions of Mr. Harun-or Rashid.

<u>17. We have given our anxious thought in the matter and considered the overall facts and circumstances of the case and particularly the fact that because of the direction given by this Court in CMP No.745 of 2010, the judgment-debtor-petitioners have paid the decretal amount to the tune of Taka 28,30,546 and the decree-holder-Bank accepted the payment made by the judgment- debtor-petitioners and that pursuant to the order of this Division, the Bank asked the judgment-debtor-petitioners to pay a sum of Taka 19,80,787 (nineteen lakh, eighty thousand and seven hundred eighty seven) only within the fixed time (নির্ধারিত সময়ের মধ্যে) though the said CMP was filed against a nonest order allegedly passed in Writ Petition No.878 of 2010. It is also a fact that the judgment-debtor-petitioners made the payment of the decretal amount on 29-9-2010, i.e. for more than 3(three) years and 4(four) months before and the leave petition could not be heard earlier though it was fixed for hearing on 27th January, 2011. It further needs to be mentioned that the decree giving rise to this leave petition was passed as far back as on 6-5-2004 and the execution case in question was levied on 28-10-2004, i.e. by now almost 10(ten) years elapsed from the date of passing of the decree. In the context, we do not consider it proper to send the matter back on remand to the High Court Division for hearing the Rule on merit setting-aside the order of default.</u>

<u>18. In view of the circumstances stated hereinabove, we consider it a fit case to invoke the power conferred upon this Court by the Constitution vide article 104 of the Constitution for doing complete justice in a case and accordingly, this leave petition is disposed of in the following terms:</u>

<u>(a) The judgment-debtor-petitioners shall pay a sum of Taka 19,80,787 (nineteen lakh, eighty thousand and seven hundred eighty seven) to the decree-holder-Bank (Janata Bank, Armanitotalla Branch, Dhaka having its head office at Janata Bank Bhaban, 110, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka) and the decree-holder-Bank is directed to accept the payment.</u>

<u>(b) The judgment-debtor-petitioners shall pay the interest to the auction purchasers at the rate of 10% on the auction money being Taka 45,10,000 from the date of deposit of the auction money till date (24-2-2014). The judgment-debtor-petitioners shall also pay a sum of Taka 1,35,000 and Taka 45,120 to the auction purchasers for the expenses, they incurred for stamp duty and for poundage fee respectively.</u>

<u>(c) The auction money of Taka 45,10,000 deposited by the auction purchasers shall be refunded back to them along with Taka 1 ,35,300 + Taka 45,120 and the amount of interest which will be paid by the judgment-debtor-petitioners on the auction money as directed in clause (b) hereinbefore.</u>

<u>(d) The judgment-debtor-petitioners shall make the deposit of the amount as detailed in clauses (a) and (b) hereinbefore in the Artha Rin Execution Case being No.560 of 2004 of the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka within two months from the date of receipt of this order failing this, the leave petition shall stand dismissed and the auction sale of the mortgaged property held on 6-10-2009 shall be treated as legal and valid.</u>

<u>With the deposit of the money by the judgment-debtor-petitioners as detailed in clauses (a) and (b) hereinbefore, the decree passed in the Artha Rin Suit No.304 of 2003 of the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka shall be satisfied.</u>

<u>(f) The Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka is directed not to cause any delay in giving back the auction purchasers money as detailed in clauses (b) and (c) hereinbefore. The Artha Rin execution case in question (No.560 of 2004) shall stand satisfied accordingly.</u>

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 288 of 2012.
lawyer:
Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate AJ Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate and Quamrul Islam Siddique, Senior Advocate instructed by Md Aftab Hossain Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner 
Mahmudul Islam. Senior Advocate and Aminul Hoque Senior Advocate instructed by Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ----- For Respondent No.1.
parties:
Ali Amjad Khan (Md) ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Md. Habibullah Dawn and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 12.12.2011 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3873 of 2011).
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J : This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 12-12-2011 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3873 of 2011 discharging the Rule and affirming the judgment and order dated 11-10-2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Sixth Court, Dhaka allowing Miscellaneous Case No.19 of 2011 arising out of Title Suit No.103 of 2004 renumbered as Title Suit No.2725 of 2008 and directing the petitioner (decree-holder) to hand over the possession of the suit land to respondent No.1 immediately.

2. The facts leading to this petition for leave to appeal, in a nutshell, are:

Respondent No.1 as 3rd party filed Miscellaneous Case No.14 of 2011 under Rules 100 and 101 of Order XXI read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of his possession in the suit land. His case, in brief, is that Rafique Ahmed Khan got allotment of the suit land from Rajdhani Unnayan Karthipakkha (RAJUK) and accordingly, RAJUK executed and registered a lease deed dated 13-8-1969 and he got possession thereof. After death of Rafique Ahmed Khan, his heirs Jalemur Nessa and three others got succession certificate in Succession Case No.637 of 1997 and his heirs appointed Md Kamrul Huda and Md Shahidul Islam Khan as their attorneys and they having got permission from RAJUK transferred the suit land to 3rd party-respondent No.1 by a registered deed of sale dated 4-4-2010. Respondent No.1 has since been in possession of the suit land through his tenant, Md Golam Faruk, who had a show-room of cars in the suit land. On 5-5-2011, decree-holder-petitioner dispossessed third-party-respondent No.1 by police force. 3rd party-respondent No.1 came to know that decree holder-petitioner by filing Title Suit No.103 of 2004 renumbered as Title Suit No.2725 of 2008 under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act got a decree for recovery of possession. In that suit, the plaintiff-petitioner got decree' against a dead person and the 3rd party- respondent was not a party to the suit. Therefore, Miscellaneous Case No.14 of 2011 was filed for restoration of possession in the suit land by respondent No.1.

3. The petitioner contested the Miscellaneous case by filing written objection denying the material statements made in the application filed under Rules 100 and 101 of Order XXI read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. His case is that he as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 103 of2004 renumbered as Title Suit No.2725 of 2008 under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act against Sarder Abdur Rahman and others and obtained decree on 22-11-2010. Subsequently, he filed Title Execution Case No.1 of 2011 and got possession in the suit land through Court. The deed of 3rd party-respondent No.1 is forged and fraudulent. The plaintiff-petitioner got the decree after long eight years of filing of the suit for recovery of possession and, as such, the Miscellaneous case is liable to be dismissed.

4. The learned Joint District Judge, Sixth Court, Dhaka by judgment and order dated 11-10- 2011 allowed the Miscellaneous case.

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 11-10-2011, the plaintiff-petitioner filed a revisional application before the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 3873 of 2011. After hearing the parties, the learned Judges of the High Court Division, by the judgment and order dated 12-12- 2011 discharged the Rule.

6. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the leave-petitioner has filed this civil petition for leave to appeal before this Division.

7. Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiya and Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Advocates, appearing on behalf of the leave-petitioner, submit that in view of Rule 102 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure, respondent No.1 is not legally entitled to file any application under Rules 100 and 101 of Order XXI read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and that the High Court Division without taking into consideration this provision of the law erroneously held that leave-respondent No.1 is entitled to recover of possession of the disputed property. They further submit that defendant Nos. 1 and 3 filed a joint written statement in Title Suit No.1 03 renumbered as Title Suit No.2725 of 2008 and, as such, it cannot be said that the leave-petitioner is a 3rd party bonafide purchaser having no knowledge of the decree passed in Title Suit No.103 renumbered as Title Suit No. 2725 of 2008 although defendant No.3 was a judgment-debtor. They also submit that on all counts leave-respondent No.1 cannot be regarded as a 3rd party bonafide purchaser, who admittedly purchased the disputed property from the heirs of the judgment-debtor during pendency of the suit.

8. Mr Mahmudul Islam, Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of respondent No.1, on the other hand, submits that though it was shown that Rafique Ahmed Khan was judgment-debtor in Title Suit No.103 renumbered as Title Suit No.2725 of 2008 in paragraph 10(Kha) of the written statement alleged to have filed by defendant Nos.1 and 3, it has been stated that Rafique Ahmed Khan died on 23-12-1996 leaving behind three sons, a daughter and a wife and, as such, Rafique Ahmed Khan cannot be designated as a judgment-debtor.

9. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates, perused the impugned judgment and the materials on record.

10. The salient findings of the High Court Division, in brief, are:

The 3rd party was able to prove his prima facie title to the suit land and he was in possession of the suit land through his tenant Md Golam Faruk, who had a show-room of cars in the suit land when he was dispossessed in Execution Case No.1 of 2011. The process server who was sent for execution of the writ of delivery of possession, stated in writing that he found that Md Golam Faruk, a tenant of 3rd party was in possession of the suit land having a showroom of cars and that the 3rd party willingly vacated the suit land as per direction of the Court and that the decree-holder was then put in possession of the suit land. In spite of its failure to consider the evidence of the witnesses the trial Court found the story of the possession and dispossession of the 3rd party to have been proved by both oral and documentary evidence and that this finding proved that the Court below had gone through the evidence on record.

11. Mr Mahmudul Islam, learned Senior Advocate, has drawn our attention to Annexure-B, the written statement filed by defendant No.1 (Sardar Md Abdur Rahman) and defendant No.3 (Rafique Ahmed Khan), in which, paragraph 10 (Kha) and (Ga) run as follows:

“(খ) অতঃপর উক্ত রফিক আহমেদ খাঁন নালিশী তফসিল সম্পত্তিতে একতলা পাকা বিল্ডিং ও একটি টিন সেড ঘর নির্মাণ করতঃ গোলাম মাওলা চৌধুরীর নিকট ভাড়া দিয়া নিয়মিত ভাড়া গ্রহণ করতঃ শান্তিপূর্ণ ভাবে ভোগ দখলে নিয়ত থাকেন। অতঃপর উক্ত রফিক আহমেদ খাঁন গত ২৩-১২-১৯৯৬ইং তারিখে মৃত্যুবরণ করিলে তাহার তিন পুত্র ১। শহীদুল ইসলাম খাঁন, ২। রাশিদুল ইসলাম খাঁন ও ৩। ইমদাদুল খাঁন  এক কন্যা রোকেয়া বেগম ও স্ত্রী জালেমুন নেছা নালিশী ভুমির ওয়ারিশ ও মালিক দখলদার নিযুক্ত হন। অতঃপর উক্ত গোলাম মাওলা চৌধুরী তফশীল সম্পত্তি লইয়া জাল দলিল সৃষ্টি করিলে রফিক আহমেদ এর পুত্র মোঃ শহীদুল ইসলাম খাঁন উত্তরা থানায় এজহার নং-৩৭(৯) ২০০৩ দায়ের করিলে উক্ত গোমাম মাওলা চৌধুরী বাড়ী ছাড়িয়া দিয়া পলাতক হন। বর্ণিত রফিক আহমেদ খানের ওয়ারিশগণ ঢাকায় ৩য় সাব জজ অদালত মোকদ্দমা নং ৬৩৭/৯৭ এবং ২নং সহকারী জজ ও পারিবারিক আদালত মোকদ্দমা নং ৯৫৭/৯৭ হইতে ওয়ারিশান সার্টিফিকেট প্রাপ্ত হন।

(গ) রফিক আহমেদ এর ওয়ারিশগণ ১নং বিবাদীকে তফশীল সম্পত্তি রাজউক হইতে নামজারী বিক্রয় বন্ধক সহ যাবতীয় কর্ম সম্পাদনের জন্য রেজিস্ট্রার্ড আম-মোক্তার নং-৪৪৬৫-৪৪-২৯২/১৯৯৮ নিযুক্ত করেন এবং একটি বায়নানামা সম্পাদন ক্রমে দখল হস্তান্তর করে নালিশী সম্পত্তির উন্নয়ন শাসন ও সংরক্ষণ এর দায়িত্ব অর্পণ করেন।”

12. Having gone through the statements of sub-para(kha), it appears that Rafique Ahmed Khan died on 23-12-1996 long before filing of Title Suit NO.103 of 2004 renumbered as Title Suit No. 2725 of 2008. How a dead person could file a written statement is not comprehensible. Even after receipt of the written statement, the leave-petitioner (the plaintiff) did not file any application for substituting the heirs of Rafique Ahmed Khan and allowed the suit to be decreed ex parte against Rafique Ahmed Khan on 22-11- 2010. Such a decree against a dead person is a nullity.

13. Even the heirs of Rafique Ahmed Khan obtained succession certificate by filing Succession Pase No.637 of 1997. The succession certificate was marked as exhibit-3 by the trial Court.

14. The learned Senior Advocates for the leave-petitioner rely on Rule 102 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure which is quoted as under:

"102. Nothing in rules 99 and 101 shall apply to resistance or obstruction in execution of a decree for the possession of immovable property by a person to whom the judgment- debtor has transferred the property after the institution of the suit in which the decree was passed or to the dispossession of any such person."

<u>15. This Rule recognizes the doctrine of lis pendence. It provides that a transferee pendente lite is not entitled to the benefit of the procedure under Rules 99 and 101 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the case in hand, Rafique Ahmed Khan was dead long before the institution of the suit and, as such, the purchase of the suit land by the 3rd party from the attorneys of the heirs of Rafique Ahmed Khan cannot be termed as purchase during pendency of the suit and therefore, the doctrine of lis pendens shall not apply here.</u>

16. In the light of the findings made before, it appears that Rule 102 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure does not apply to the purchase of respondent No.1 and he was admittedly a 3rd party, who was dispossessed in execution of the decree passed in Title Suit No.103 of 2004 renumbered as Title Suit No.2725 of 2008. Therefore, Miscellaneous case filed by him under Rules 99 and 101 of Order XXI read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure was maintainable.

17. The findings arrived at by the High Court Division having been based on proper appreciation of law and fact do not call for interference.

Accordingly, this civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 3033 of 2015
lawyer:

Mr. Shashanka Sekhor Nos.1 Sarker, Advocate, Instructed by Mrs. Nahid Sultana, Advocate-on- Record ----- For the Respondent:
Not Represented. Nos. 2-24 ----- For the Respondent

Versus

full_judgment:
Mr. Muhammad Imman Ali, J.:- This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 07.04.2014 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1005 of 2012 making the Rule absolute. 

2. Petitioner Nos. l and 2 herein as plaintiffs on 21.01.2010 instituted Other Class Suit No.4 of 2010 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Cox's Bazar against the respondents for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in respect of the land described in the schedule to the plaint and for further declaration that the decree dated 31.7.1986 passed by the then Munsif, Cox's Bazar in Other Class Suit No.235 of 1972, is void and inoperative. 

3. In that suit defendant filed an application under Order VII Rule 11(d) read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure alleging that the predecessor of defendant Nos.1-3 had instituted Other Class Suit No.235 of 1972 before the then Munsif, Cox's Bazar impleading the predecessor of defendant No.4 and others for declaration of their title on the self-same land and for khas possession. The said suit was decreed on contest on 31.7.1986 and that the predecessor of the defendant No. 4 and others had filed Other Appeal No.144 of 1986 in the Court of District Judge, Cox's Bazar. Ultimately the Subordinate Judge, Cox's Bazar after hearing, by judgment and decree dated 17.3.1987 allowed the appeal and thereby set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. Thereafter, the defendants and their predecessor filed Civil Revision No.562 of 1987 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which upon hearing was made absolute and the Title Suit No. 235 of 1972 was decreed. The predecessor of the present plaintiffs after 6 years filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.870 of 2009 before this Division, and after hearing, by judgment and order dated 12.11.2009 the petition was dismissed. Hence, the defendants of the instant suit filed the application for rejection of the plaint as being barred by law. 

4. The plaintiffs filed written objection against the application for rejection of plaint. 

5. The learned Judge by order No. 23 dated 26.02.2012 rejected the said application for rejection of plaint on the finding that without examining the witnesses at the time of hearing of the suit the point raised by the petitioners cannot be decided. 

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said order of the Joint District Judge, the defendants filed Civil Revision No.1005 of 2012 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which after hearing was made absolute. Hence, the plaintiffs are now before us having filed the instant civil petition for leave to appeal. 

7. Mr. Tobarak Hossain, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the petitioners owned and are in possession or the land in question for 23 years without any claim from any quarter and that the application under Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed only to delay the matter. He submitted that the trail Court rightly rejected the said application, but the High Court Division without properly considering the facts made the Rule absolute. He further submitted that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the schedule of the land of the defendants-opposite parties is not the same and without considering this aspect the High Court Division made the Rule absolute thereby allowing the application for rejection of plaint. Lastly, the learned Advocate submitted that the trial Court correctly found that the matters raised in the application under Order VII Rule 11(d) would have to be decided after taking evidence, but the High Court Division erroneously revered the decision of the trial Court. 

8. Mr. Shashanka Sekhor Sarker, learned Advocate appearing for respondent No.1 made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. 

9. From the evidence and materials on record we find that the predecessor of defendant Nos.1, 2, and 3 instituted Other Class Suit No. 235 of 1972 impleading the predecessor of defendant No.4 and others and that suit was decreed on contest. The said decree was upheld up to this Division. The plaintiffs of the instant suit purchased the suit land form the heirs of the defendants of the earlier Title Suit No.235 of 1972. In that suit the plaintiff's vendors had lost the claim of title up to this Division. We note that the plaintiffs of the instant suit purchased the suit land after the earlier litigation had concluded. Thereafter, they purchased from persons who did not have title to the land. Moreover, in the instant suit there is no claim of any fraud. 

10. The High Court Division observed that it is true "that a plaint of a suit should not be rejected under order 7 rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure only on point of res-judicata. But the facts of the present case are quite different. Apparently it shows that the predecessor of the plaintiffs-opposite parties lost their title up to Appellate Division and after settling dispute finally by the Appellate Division the present plaintiff-opposite parties purchased some lands in 2009 from the predecessor of the defendants of the former suit and they instituted present suit for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and for further declaration that the decree passed in previous Title Suit No.235 of 1972 against the predecessor of the present plaintiffs are void and not binding upon them. The issue of present title suit was decided by the Court finally in previously instituted suit and that issue cannot be agitated in the subsequent suit." The High Court Division concluded that the present plaintiffs-opposite parties having knowledge about the previous suit and having lost their title up to this Division, instituted the present suit which is nothing but a futile exercise. 

11. Having considered the facts and circumstances discussed above, we are of the view that the High Court Division has properly considered the relevant law and facts involved in the case. The decision arrived at does not call for interference by this Division and, accordingly, the civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed. 

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 23-08-2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3046 of 2008).
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J : This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 23-8-2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3046 of 2008 discharging the Rule and affirming the order dated 23- 6-2008 passed by the learned District Judge, Chittagong, in Other Appeal No.413 of 2007 admitting the appeal upon condonation of delay of 1492 days filed against the preliminary decree dated 20-11-2000 and final decree dated 18-10-2003 passed by the learned Acting Senior Assistant Judge, Fifth Court, Chittagong in Partition Suit No.84 of 1999 decreeing the same.

2. The facts, in a nutshell, are that the plaintiff instituted a suit for partition against the defendants. The trial Court upon hearing the parties by its judgment and order dated 20-10-2000 decreed the suit ex-parte in preliminary form and the final decree was drawn on 18-10-2003. Against the preliminary and final decrees, defendant No.13 along with her son as the appellants preferred Other Appeal No.413 of 2007 before the learned District Judge, Chittagong, which was out of time. The learned District Judge, Chittagong by his impugned judgment and order dated 23-6-2008 condoned the delay and admitted the appeal for hearing.

3. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 23-6-2008, the plaintiffs-petitioners filed a revisional application before the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 3046 of 2008. After hearing the par- ties, the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division, by the judgment and order dated 23-8- 2009, discharged the Rule without any order as to costs and vacated the order of stay granted earlier by this Court and also directed the Court of appeal below to dispose of the appeal within three months from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment and order.

4. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the leave-petitioners have filed this civil petition for leave to appeal before this Division.

5. Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the leave-petitioners, submits that the learned District Judge condoned the delay in respect of the appeal filed against the final decree and not against the preliminary decree and that the High Court Division without considering this aspect of the case discharged the Rule and, as such, the impugned judgment should be set-aside. He further submits that by one appeal, respondent Nos.1 and 2 cannot challenge both the preliminary decree and the final decree and that since the delay has been condoned with respect to the final decree, the appeal may be treated to have been filed against the final decree only and, as such, the impugned judgment delivered by the High Court Division should be set-aside.

6. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate, perused the impugned judgment and the materials on record.

<u>7. There is no gainsaying the fact that respondent Nos.1 and 2 have challenged both the preliminary decree and the final decree in one appeal. An appeal against a preliminary decree is filed under section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure and that against the final decree under section 97 of the Code of Civil Procedure. If an appeal is filed against the preliminary decree and if the preliminary decree is modified or set-aside then the final decree falls through.</u>

8. It is contended that the learned District Judge admitted the appeal condoning the delay of 1492 days which are equal to 4 years and 32 days and that as such, the appeal shall be deemed to have been admitted in respect of the final decree only.

9. Having gone through the entire order dated 23-6-2008 delivered by the learned District Judge, it appears that he has not stated anywhere that the delay has been condoned in respect of the final decree only. The entire order reveals that the appeal has been admitted against both the preliminary decree and the final decree. The learned District Judge committed a clerical mistake while converting years and days into days. Such a clerical mistake cannot stand on the way of getting the desired relief by respondent Nos.1 and 2. The learned District Judge was, however, satisfied with the explanation furnished by respondent Nos. 1 and 2 in the application filed under section 5 of the Limitation Act.

10. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 should have filed two appeals, one against the preliminary decree and the other against the final decree. Therefore, the appeal filed by respondent Nos.1 and 2 shall be deemed to have been admitted in respect of preliminary decree. Mere filing of an appeal against the preliminary is sufficient because the final decree falls through as soon as the preliminary decree is set-aside or modified.

11. In this connection, reliance may be made on the case of Taleb Ali vs Abdul Aziz, AIR 1929 (Calcutta) 189 (Full Bench), in which, it has been held that an appeal from a preliminary decree is not incompetent even if a final decree is made before the appeal is presented. Nor is it necessary for a party aggrieved by a preliminary decree to appeal both from that decree and against the final decree in order to maintain this appeal against the preliminary decree.

<u>12. Reliance may also be made on the case of Saradindu Mukherjee vs Jahar Lall Agarwalla. AIR 1942 (Calcutta)153, in which, it has been held that when no appeal is preferred against the final decree and only the preliminary decree is appealed against but a copy of the final decree has been placed on the record of the appeal it is the duty of the appellate Court in dealing with the appeal to give necessary and consequential directions regarding the final decree.</u>

13. From the cases referred to above, it appears that if the respondents appeal is treated to be admitted against the preliminary decree then they may get the desired relief provided they succeed in the appeal.

14. Having gone through the judgment of the High Court Division, we find that the learned Advocate for the petitioners has not raised this question before the High Court Division. Therefore, the High Court Division did not have the opportunity to address the question now raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioners.

15. The findings arrived at and the decision made by the High Court Division having been based on proper appreciation of laws and facts do not war- rant interference by this Division. Accordingly, this civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed.

End.

full_judgment:
AKM Shahidul Huq J: The judgment and decree dated 14-11-2011 passed by the Joint District Judge, ill Court, Gazipur, in Title Appeal No. 115 of 2008 reversing the judgment and decree dated 22-9-2008 passed by the Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 23 of 1998 dismissing the suit. A single judge of this Hon'ble Division on hearing the submissions of the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (Act V of 1908) was pleased to issue a rule calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1 to 15 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-11-2011 passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur in Title Appeal No. 115 of 2008 reversing those of dated 22-9-2008 passed by the Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 23 of 1998 dismissing the suit shall not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The short facts for disposal of the rule is that Maulvi Basiruddin, husband of plaintiff No. 1 and father of plaintiffs Nos. 2-5 were the owners of the suit land and other properties. Moulvi Basiruddin was killed by the miscreants in the year 1967 when plaintiffs No. 2-5 were all minors. Defendant No. 1 came forward to conduct the case regarding murder of Moulvi Basiruddin as tadbirkar. Plaintiff No. 1 being a helpless widow placed reliance and confidence on defendant No. 1 and under the dictates of defendant No. 1 she put her signature on some papers. Taking advantage of such reliance and confidence, defendant No. 1 created some documents with the signature of plaintiff No. 1. The plaintiffs were taken by surprise when the defendants claimed to have purchased the suit property from the plaintiffs in 1996. At the instance of the plaintiffs there was conciliation meeting (salish) with the participation of local dignitaries. In the said "salish" it was decided that the defendants would return the said property to the plaintiffs. Accordingly the parties went to execute and register necessary instruments on 19-2-1996 but defendant No.1fraudulently prepared a deed of compromise (solenama) and got it registered showing only 0.86 and 1/2 acres of land given to the plaintiffs and retaining 2.62 and 1/2 acres of land by the defendants. Moreover, defendant No.1 created a deed of gift (heba) in favour of his son in respect of some land out of the said 0.86 and 1/2 acres of land shown to have been returned to the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs having come to know about the said fraudulent acts filed Title Suit No. 44 of 1997 in Third Court of Assistant Judge, Gazipur for cancellation of the said fraudulent deed. The said suit was not framed in accordance with the instruction of the plaintiffs so the plaintiffs withdrew it on 18-2-1998 with leave to sue afresh. Thereafter the plaintiff s obtained certified copies of the deeds in question, gathered definite knowledge of those deeds and filed the instant suit.

3. The defendant Nos. 1-3 contested the suit by filing, written statement denying allegations made in the plaint and contending inter alia that the suit was not maintainable in its form and frame, barred by limitation and without cause of action. The substantive case of these defendants in short, is as follows: On the death of Moulivi Basiruddin the suit property devolved on his heirs namely, one wife (plaintiff No.1) two daughters (plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3) and two sons (plaintiff Nos. 4 and 5). Plaintiff Nos. 1, 2, and 3 transferred 2.01 acres of land out of9.54 acres of twelve plots to defendant No. 1 by executing and registering sale deed No. 8198/73. Plaintiff No. 3 by another registered deed No. 11764/75 transferred 0.60 acres of land to defendant Nos. 2 and 3. The plaintiffs also transferred 0.43 acres of land to defendant No. 1 by sale deed No. 8330/76. At the time of registering deed No. 8330 although plaintiff No.3' was major, the Sub-Registrar thought her to be minor and, as such, her mother plaintiff No. 1 executed the deed on her behalf. Plaintiffs No.1, 4 and 5 transferred 0.77 acres of land to defendant No.1 by registered sale deed No. 3597/78. In the above way defendant Nos. 1-3 lawfully acquired title to the entire suit property and have been possessing the same on payment of rent regularly.

4. After transfer of the suit property as, such, the plaintiffs went to the village Kumardi under Shibpur Police Station in Narishingdi district. After a long lapse of time the plaintiffs put pressure on the defendants to return the suit land on the plea that at the time of execution of the sale deed the plaintiffs were minors. Under pressure of some influential persons the defendants were constrained to execute and register a deed of compromise being No. 1683/96 giving back 0.86 acres of land to the plaintiffs. Plaintiff No. 1 obtained permission of the Court to transfer property of the minors. The part of the transferred property for which permission was not obtained, the defendants gave back to the plaintiffs and the defendants have been possessing remaining 2.94 and 1/2 acres of their purchased property as rightful owners.

5. Defendant No. 1 transferred 0.24 and 1/2 acres of land to his son by a deed of gift being No. 1235/97. The said gifted land is not the part of 0.861/ acre returned to the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs earlier filed Title Suit No. 44 of 1997 for cancellation of the said deed of gift and subsequently withdrawing that suit they have filed the instant suit. The criminal case on the murder of Basiruddin concluded in the year 1968, and on the other hand, the deeds in question were executed and registered in the years 1973; 1975, 1976, 1978 and 1996: So it is apparent that the allegations of the plaintiffs as to creating sale deed by taking thumb impressions and signatures in connection with the said murder case are untrue. Moreover, in the plaint of Title Suit No. 44 of 1997 the plaintiffs admitted the execution and registration of sale deed No. 1683; The suit has been filed on got up story and is liable to be dismissed.

6. Both the parties adduced oral and documentary evidence at the trial. The trial Court on appreciation of evidence on record dismissed the suit finding the same to be barred by the principle of estoppels; and permission of the Court was obtained for transfer of part of the property on behalf of the minors, and there was no ingredient of fraud in the transactions in question.

7. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal being No. 149 of 2003 before the District Judge, Gazipur and on transfer the Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur allowed the said appeal setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and sent back the suit on remand to the trial Court affording the parties opportunity to amend pleadings and to adduce additional evidence by the judgment and decree dated 24-8-2004.

8. Being aggrieved by arid dissatisfied with the said judgment and order dated 24-8-2004 passed by the Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur the, petitioner moved this application before this Hon'ble Court under section 115( 1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule.

9. Mr Probir Neogi the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner and other hand Mr Shamsul Haque Bhuiyan the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties.

10. Mr Probir Neogi the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits• that the impugned, judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal inasmuch as the Court of appeal below set aside the decision of the trial Court without adverting to the finding forming the basis of such decision. The learned. Advocate further submits that having regard to the findings of the appellate Court itself and terms of the remand the Court of appeal below committed an error of law resulting in erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned judgment and decree inasmuch as it is settled that order of remand cannot be made to give the erring party opportunity to fill up the lacuna in pleadings and evidence. The learned Advocate also submits that having regard to the purpose of impugned order of remand as stated in the ordering portion of the impugned judgment 'বাদী পক্ষকে প্রদর্শনী আই সিরিজ চিহ্নিত কগজাদি ও সঠিকতা সম্পর্কে আরজির প্রয়োজনীয় সংশোধনী সহ মৌখিক ও দালিলিক সাক্ষ্য দাখিল এবং দাবীকৃত বেদখল সম্পর্কে ও আরজির প্রয়োজনীয় সংশোধনীসহ মৌখিক ও দালিলিক সাক্ষ্য দাখিলের সুযোগ প্রদান করিবার উদ্দেশ্যে মূল মোকাদ্দমাটি পুনঃবিচারের জন্য নিম্ন আদালতে প্রেরণ করা হইল।' the Court of appeal below committed serious error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice inasmuch as it is apparent on the face of the impugned judgment that the order of remand has been made for the sole purpose of giving the plaintiffs an opportunity for the second time to fill up the lacuna in the pleadings and evidence. The learned Advocate lastly submits that is an elementary principle and practice of law that when the plaintiff is given opportunity to amend the plaint and adduce additional evidence, the defendant is legally entitled to equal and corresponding opportunity, and that elementary principle and practice of law having been violated in the instant case, the impugned judgment and decree are liable to be set aside and having regard to the fact and circumstances of the case, especially, the fact of earlier remand, the impugned judgment and decree are not sustainable in law.

11. Mr Md Shamsul Haque Bhuiyan the learned Advocate for the, opposite parties submits that the opposite parties No.1-5 as plaintiffs filed a Title suit being No. 23 of 1998, which was dismissed on 30-4-2003 on contest by the trial Court and the plaintiff as appellants filed a Title Appeal No.109 of 2003 before the learned District judge, Gazipur which was subsequently transferred to the Additional District Judge, Gazipur, After hearing the parties the appeal was allowed on remand to the trial Court on 24-8-2004 on the finding that the disputed deeds and the papers 112 permission cases are false fabricated, and' fraudulently obtained by the defendant respondent. But in the meantime plaintiffs lost possession in some portion of land so this appellate Court has not able to pass a decree in favour of the plaintiffs. For this reason the title suit is liable to be send back on remand to the trial Court. The learned Advocate further submits that the trial Court again dismissed the suit on22-9-2008 without considering and discussing the appellate Court's finding which passed in Title Appeal No.109 of 2003. The plaintiffs again filed a Title Appeal N. 115 of 2008 before the District Judge, Gazipur which subsequently transferred to the Joint District Judge,2nd Court, Gazipur the appellate. Court heard both the parties and allowed the appeal, remanded the case to the trial Court for re-trial as per observation of the two appellate Court's findings. Against above mentioned judgment and decree passed by the Appellate Court, the defendants-respondents preferred this revisional application before the Hon'ble High Court Division. The learned Advocate also submits that the plaintiff filed the Title Suit No. 23 of 1998 showing cause of action in the plaint on 19-2-1996 and the suit filed in the year 1998, so the suit is not barred by limitation and appellate Court gave findings in Title Appeal No. 109 of 2003 that the disputed deeds and 2 permission cases are false, fabricated, fraudulently obtained by the defendants which was not challenged by the defendants. So the defendants-petitioners claim is barred by Res judicata and estoppels. For this there is no need for expert opinion. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the suit filed under section 39 of the Specific Relief Act. for cancellation of the disputed deed and the plaintiffs made parties of the disputed deed. So the suit is not barred by defects of parties and there is no need to call for the records of the Permission Case No. 432 of 1970 by the plaintiffs which was declared false by the appellate Court in Title Appeal No. 109 of 2003 and the title suit filed under section 39 of the Specific Relief Act for cancellation of the disputed deeds, there is no need to pray possession on the suit land or some portion of the suit land and the disputed deed registered beyond jurisdiction. The learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties in course of his submissions refers the case of Shefali Rani and others reported in 50 DLR 349 where a single Judge of this Hon'ble Court held "when the questioned document was registered at a place by a Sub-Register where no portion of the property mentioned in the document was situated within: the jurisdiction of that Sub-Register the document was wholly void." He also refers the case of Nur Mohammad vs Mst Karim Bibi reported in PLD 1959 (WP) Lahore page 932- have no manner of 'application in the facts and circumstances of the present case.

<u>12. Heard the learned Advocate of both sides perused the impugned judgment and decree passed by the Joint District Judge 2nd Court, Gazipur in Title Appeal No. 115 of2008 reversing the judgment and decree dated 22-9-2008. passed by the Assistant Judge,3rdCourt, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 23 of 1998 dismissing the suit sending back the suit on remand to the Trial, Court. On perusal of the. impugned judgment and the order of the remand as passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur we find that the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur has totally misconceived the previsions of law as regards the order of remand as contain in order 41 Rule 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure where it is clearly provides that "where the court from whose decree an appeal is preferred has disposed of the suit upon a preliminary point and the decree is reversed in appeal, the Appellate Court may, if it thinks fit, by order remand the case, and may further direct what issue or issues shall be tried in the case so remanded, and shall send a copy of its judgment and order to the court from whose decree the appeal is preferred, with directions to re-admit the suit under its original number in the register of civil suits, and proceed to determine the suit; and the evidence (if any) recorded during the original trial shall, subject to all just exceptions, be evidence during the trail after remand." the appellate Court is very much competent to dispose of the suit finally instead of sending back the suit on remand to the Trial. Court as because as a final Court of fact the Appellate Court has got ample power to go into the root of the suit. As a final Court of fact the appellate Court can take additional evidence in order to arrive its definite finding in deciding the suit finally. The Appellate Court has got every power as that of the trial Court to settle the issues completely without sending back the suit on remand to the Trial Court. On perusal of the impugned judgment and decree of the Appellate Court we find that the Appellate Court has purposely and intentionally avoided and shifted his responsibility upon the Trial Court which the appellate Court was very much competent to perform. In avoiding such responsibility on the part of the appellate Court was not proper and according to us we find that all the materials for deciding the suit finally were before the Appellate Court. We also find the impugned judgment and order of remand has been passed by the final Court of fact in order to fill up the lacuna. It is not the duty of the appellate court to give an opportunity to the erring party to fill up the lacuna in pleadings and evidence on this count also the impugned judgment and decree of the Appellate Court suffers from serious miscarriage of justice which has resulted an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. We also find by the impugned judgment the appellate court encouraged the litigant to drag on the suit for an indefinite period which is not the solemn duty of the court more so the impugned order of remand virtually prolonged the early disposal of the suit for an indefinite period. In that view of the matter we observe the, impugned Judgment and order as passed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur cannot be sustainable under any provision of law. So it would be fit and proper to send back the suit on remand to the Appellate Court to write out a proper judgment after giving due and equal opportunity to the parties to adduce any evidence if necessary and shall dispose of the appeal preferably within three months which is mandatory with this observation the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-11-2011 passed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur in Title Appeal No. 115 of 2008 reversing those of passed by the Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 23 of 1998 is here by set aside. We find merit and substance in the rule. In the result the rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.</u>

13. Title Suit No. 23 of 1998 be send back on remand to the Appellate Court with a direction to write out a "roper Judgment after giving due opportunity to the parties to adduce evidence if any and dispose of the Appeal after due and proper consideration of the oral and documentary evidence on record within three months from the date of receipt of the lower Courts records positively.

14. The order of stay as granted at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby recalled and vacated.

Send down the lower courts records along with a copy of this judgment to the concern Court forthwith for information and necessary action.

End.

Shah Md Munir Sharif -----For the Petitioners.
